6.6.13 Automatic Cut-Off（G266      A* X* S* F*)

During the machining process, if an abnormal condition occurs (e.g., tool life expiration, tool breakage, machine fault), the machine must be stopped. After resolving the issue, a cut-off operation is required before restarting the machining process. The G266 command can be used to perform an automatic cut-off operation.

Command Format (G266   A* X* S* F*)

A: Quick Positioning Position – Bar Diameter Value (mm) X: Cut-off Feed Position – Parting Diameter Value (mm) S: Spindle Speed for Cut-off (RPM)

F: Feed per Revolution (mm/rev)

The G266 command implements automatic cut-off through a pre-packaged macro program (G266). The macro logic is structured as follows:

IF #1 =#0 THEN

ALARM(100,"G266 A* DATA ERROR");      //A OD Data Error END_IF;

IF #9 =#0 THEN

ALARM(101,"G266 F* DATA ERROR");       //F Feed Command Error END_IF;

IF #19 =#0 THEN

ALARM(102,"G266 S* DATA ERROR");      //S Spindle Speed Error END_IF;

IF #24 =#0 THEN

ALARM(103,"G266 X* DATA ERROR");      //X Cut-off Position Error END_IF;

WAIT();

N000;

IF(#1036=1) THEN     //T code Verification GOTO100;

ELSE;

T0101;             //Tool Call T0101

END_IF;

N100;

IF (@10721<=#24*1000) THEN        //X-axis Mechanical Position

IF (@10722=0.0) THEN         //Y-axis Mechanical Position GOTO999;

END_IF;

END_IF;

  1. T01 is predefined as the cut-off tool. Using any tool other than T01 will trigger axis collision risks due to unmapped tool offsets.
  2. T01 must be manually positioned above the workpiece at a safe Z-height before executing codes.

Synchronizes the speed and phase of the main spindle and sub-spindle. In this mode, the machine can perform the following operations:

  1. Transferring a workpiece from the main spindle to the sub-spindle.
  2. Simultaneously holding and machining a single workpiece with both the main spindle and sub-spindle.
  3. Maintaining phase synchronization between the main spindle and sub-spindle for machining irregularly shaped parts.

  3. Simultaneously holding and performing external thread turning on a single workpiece with the main spindle and sub-spindle.

M1001         Decouple Z1/Z2 Axis Synchronization

6.6.19 Machine Tool Control (T Command)

Tool changes are executed via servo axes controlled by the system. The T-code specifies the tool number in the program.

  • Command Format

T □□△△                    

□□：Tool Number

  • Turret Tool（T01～T09）
  • Lateral Live Tool（T11～T19）
  • Face Tool（T21～T29）
  • Back live tools（T30～T38）

△△：Tool Nose & Wear Offset ID

The4 -digit T code positions the tool:. The first 2 digits indicate the tool number,  and the last 2 digits denote compensation. T0000  cancels compensation. The X、Y、Z coordinates for each tool (tool number) are stored in the system's tool length registry.

Note:

  1. Tool selection defaults to rapid feed motion.
  2. T codes must be in standalone program blocks.
  3. Do not combine T-codes (T□□△△) with M/S-codes in the same block.
  4. Unauthorized personnel must not modify tool length values. Always back up data before changes.

6.7.1 Machine Linear Axes

The machine is equipped with 5 servo-driven linear axes:Y1 and X2 axes: Perform tool-changing motions.X axis: Controls radial positioning and radial cutting feed.Z1 and Z2 axes: Control axial positioning and axial cutting feed. All servo axes utilize absolute encoders for position feedback.

6.7.2 Spindle Rotation Direction

When facing the spindle from the right side of the machine:Counterclockwise (CCW) rotation is defined as spindle forward (M03).Clockwise (CW) rotation is defined as spindle reverse (M04).

During automatic program execution:Press the Cycle Stop button on the operator panel to activate M01 (Optional Stop).When the program pauses at M01, press the RESET key to halt the machine.

Follow the Normal Shutdown steps above.Press the red System Power Off button on the operator panel. Confirm the display and indicators are off.Turn the main power breaker to OFF.

6.8.3 Emergency Shutdown

Press the E-stop button (on the operator panel or front control box).Press the red System Power Off button.Turn the main power breaker to OFF.

WARNING: Avoid using the E-stop during normal operation. Emergency stops may damage workpieces, tools, or machine components.

6.9 Pre-Machining Preparations

  1. Turn on Air Supply: Ensure the pneumatic system pressure is 0.5 MPa ±10%.
  2. Lubrication: Verify the lubricant level in the lubrication unit exceeds the minimum mark.
  3. Coolant (if required): Ensure the coolant tank level exceeds the minimum mark.
  4. Confirm the factory voltage matches machine requirements. Turn the main power breaker to ON.
  5. Close the machine tool power circuit breaker to the "ON" position.
  6. Press the "System On" button on the upper part of the operation panel to start the CNC system.
  7. Reset (rotate to the right) the emergency stop button on the main operation panel and front operation box.

If coolant is needed, confirm that the cooling system can work normally: press the "Coolant" button to turn on the coolant, then press the "Coolant" button again to turn off the coolant.

Figure 25 Clamping Mechanism Schematic Main/Sub Spindle Clamping Force Adjustment Procedure：

  1. Loosen the spindle locknut ( Back) counterclockwise to release the collet.
  2. Install the taper sleeve
  3. Install the spring
  4. Install the spindle collet
  5. Install and tighten the spindle nut.

  1. Use a special hex wrench to confirm that the locking screw on the left edge of the collet locking nut has been loosened.
  2. Clean the installation hole of the guide sleeve collet and the guide sleeve collet, and add lubricating oil.

There must be no significant gap between the bar stock and the Guide Sleeveing collet; otherwise, the part’s machining quality will deteriorate.
  6. After adjusting the clamping force of the guide sleeve collet appropriately, use a special hex wrench to tighten the locking screw. Check the clamping force of the guide sleeve collet again. If the clamping force is not appropriate, repeat the above steps.

6.12 Application of Bushingless Mode

This machine tool is capable of operating in bushingless mode.

For parts with a length-to-diameter ratio of less than 2.5, the bushingless mode can be selected to effectively reduce the length of the remaining material.

Maximum part length for bushingless mode: 80mm.

Before using the machine, the bushing mode must be correctly configured. Different bushing modes will invoke different Z1 -axis soft limits.

On the initial page of the NC system, navigate to the right and find the "SYIL Machinery" function option in the last item. Within the "SYIL Machinery" function option, locate the "Bushing" setting option. Use the up and down arrow keys to select the appropriate bushing mode.

6.18 Part Machining Procedure

The procedure for formal part machining is shown in Figure below.

Figure 45 Part Machining Flowchart

Special attention should be paid to the following items during the part machining procedure:

  1. If there is an error in the part machining program, it must be corrected before continuing to run the program.
  2. After programming, the program must be run without tools installed to perform a dry run. Only after the dry run is error-free can subsequent work continue.
  3. Install the tools and the part blank. Position each tool to the pre-feed position according to the programming data and confirm if there is any possibility of interference or tool collision.

Press the "Single Block" button on the operation panel, lower the feed rate override knob value, and run the program in single block mode. Only after the previous block runs without errors can the next block be executed. During single block operation, closely monitor for any command errors or tool offset setting errors that may cause discrepancies. If any potential error actions are detected, immediately press the emergency stop button, exit the operation, and resolve all errors before resuming automatic operation.

To predict machine failures or detect them early and minimize production losses, regular inspections of the machine should be conducted regardless of whether there are any faults. This chapter summarizes and explains the necessary inspection items from daily checks to those required every six months.

7.2 Common Faults and Solutions

This chapter introduces the handling methods for common faults. The methods provided are for common issues, but in practice, faults beyond these may occur. If the cause cannot be identified or resolved, please contact Manufacturer for repair.

7.2.1 Main/Sub-Spindle Collet Failure to Open/Close and Timeout Alarm

If the spindle chuck fails to open, it may result in short workpieces or failure to eject the bar stock.

Troubleshooting steps：

  1. Verify pneumatic supply integrity
  2. Check if the clamping solenoid valve is functioning properly.
  3. Check if the clamping cylinder is functioning properly.
  4. Check if the clamping sensor switch is functioning properly and if it is loose or damaged.
  5. Check if the clamping cylinder connecting rod is loose.
  6. Check if the chuck jaws' travel is normal.
  7. Disassemble the spindle nut, clean the collet and collet cone , and clean the spindle bore.
  8. Check if the collet cone is scratched or if it is stuck in the spindle bore.
  9. Replace the collet with a new one.

If the issue persists after these checks, contact  Manufacturer  for repair.

7.2.2 Low Coolant Flow

The machine uses cutting oil  for cooling. Insufficient cooling may pose a fire hazard. Address low coolant flow promptly.

Troubleshooting steps:

  1. Inspect coolant line connections
  2. Check if the coolant pump is functioning properly.
  3. Check if the coolant tank has sufficient oil.
  4. Clean the chip collection cavity in the machine base.
  5. Clean the coolant tank and filter screen.

Figure 46 Chip Conveyor and Coolant Tank Diagram

Spindle/Sub-spindle Overheat Alarm

The spindle and sub-spindle of this machine are equipped with built-in motor spindles with temperature sensors. An alarm will trigger if the spindle temperature is too high.

Handling Steps:

  1. Check the I/O input module's I16 (spindle overheat detection) and I23 (sub-spindle overheat detection) inputs. A faulty module may cause false alarms. Contact Manufacturer Customer Service Center if the module is damaged.
  2. Check if the spindle temperature is abnormally high and if there is a burning smell. If so, the spindle stator may be damaged. Contact Manufacturer Customer Service Center.
  3. Check if the spindle speed fluctuates abnormally. If so, the spindle stator or encoder may be damaged. Contact Manufacturer Customer Service Center.
  4. Check if the spindle load fluctuates abnormally during idle operation. If so, the spindle stator may be damaged. Contact Manufacturer Customer Service Center.
  5. Check if the spindle's three-phase resistance is balanced. If not, the spindle stator may be damaged. Contact Manufacturer Customer Service Center.
  6. Check the resistance between the spindle's three-phase coils and the spindle housing. If any phase shows finite resistance, the spindle coils may be shorted to the housing. Contact Manufacturer Customer Service Center.
  7. Check if the spindle power cables are damaged or there is a phase loss.
  8. Check if the spindle drive unit is damaged.

Ejector Malfunction Alarm

The counter spindle integrates an ejector mechanism that automatically unloads sub-100mm workpieces through frontal ejection.

If the part is not ejected, it may interfere with subsequent parts or machine components, causing a crash.

For the configuration and calibration of the ejector device, refer to Section 6.16: Installation and Adjustment of the Ejector System.

During ejector operation, if the machine control system fails to detect the signal from the ejector cylinder proximity sensor, a corresponding alarm will be triggered.

Troubleshooting steps：

  1. Verify pneumatic pressure is within specification
  2. Check if the ejector solenoid valve is functioning properly.
  3. Check if the air hoses are damaged.
  4. Check if the ejector cylinder's throttle valve is adjusted properly.
  5. Check if the ejector cylinder operates smoothly without sticking.
  6. Check if the ejector sensor switch is loose or damaged.
  7. Check if the ejector rod is bent or stuck.
  8. Check if there are any residual workpieces or chips in the sub-spindle and clean them.

7.2.4 Lost Position Command Alarm

Alarm Description

The controller stops outputting commands to an axis for 1 second and checks if the feedback matches the command within the allowed error range. If not, this alarm is triggered.

Potential cause

Potential cause     

  1. Mechanical obstruction in motion system
  2. Servo drive unexpectedly enabled or disabled.
  3. Data loss between the CPU board and Axis Control Card due to CPU/Card failure or poor contact.
  4. Poor contact or broken wires in the command transmission line between the controller and servo drive.
  5. Local electromagnetic interference.

Solution              

  1. Verify the integrity of the mechanical lubrication system and proper guideway lubrication
  2. Manually rotate the lead screw to check for jamming.
  3. Check the motor power and encoder cables for proper connection.
  4. Check for damage in the motor power and encoder cables.
  5. Check if the drive is powered properly and if there is any phase loss.

After the alarm, without shutting down, check if diagnostic data 8, 9, and 10 converge to 0. If not, re-home the axis and observe diagnostic data 24, 25, 26, 40, 41, and 42. If any of 24, 25, or 26 are non-zero, there is a feedback loop issue. If any of 40, 41, or 42 are non-zero, there is a command loss issue. If both sets have non-zero values, signal interference is likely. Specifically, during machining, the values of variables 8, 9, and 10 gradually increase. The possible fault point may be poor contact between the CPU board and the axis control card. Try replacing the CPU board and the axis control card.The motor or drive may be damaged. Try replacing them.

7.2.5 Following Error Alarm, Severe Following Error Alarm

Alarm Description

Due to servo characteristics, the servo motor's positioning may lag behind the controller's command. If this lag exceeds the allowed range, a following error alarm is triggered.

Potential cause   

  1. Irregular mechanical movement
  2. Poor cable contact
  3. Controller acceleration/deceleration time is set too short.
  4. Drive or motor failure.

Troubleshooting steps        

  1. Inspect the lubrication circuit to ensure adequate lubrication at all machine points.
  2. Check the machine's wiring to ensure all connections are secure and undamaged.
  3. Adjust the acceleration/deceleration time for the affected axis.
  4. Run the machine idle to confirm smooth operation without interference.
  5. If the alarm persists, contact Manufacturer Customer Service

Center. Note:

  1. Diagnostic variable 32: X-axis allowable following error.
  2. Diagnostic variable 33: Y-axis allowable following error.

Diagnostic variable 34: Z-axis allowable following error.

7.2.6 Low Absolute Position Encoder Battery

The servo motors of this machine tool are equipped with absolute position encoders. After the machine is powered off and restarted, there is no need to perform a reference point return operation, and machining can be directly carried out. When the machine is powered off, the servo motor encoders record the position information of each linear axis. The power for the servo motor encoders is supplied by a battery located in the electrical cabinet at the rear of the machine. When the battery voltage is low, the system will issue a "Low Absolute Position Encoder Battery" alarm. Please replace the battery promptly.

Precautions for Battery Replacement

  1. Battery Specification: LR20 type (i.e., D-cell battery).
  2. The battery must be replaced while the machine is powered on; otherwise, the absolute position data will be lost.

7.2.7 Absolute Position Zero Point Lost

The servo motors of this machine tool are equipped with absolute position encoders. After the machine is powered off and restarted, there is no need to perform a reference point return operation, and machining can be directly carried out. When the machine is powered off, the servo motor encoders record the position information of each linear axis.  If the system fails to read the position data from the servo motor encoders when the machine is powered on, this alarm will be triggered.

Possible Causes

  1. The machine has been idle for an extended period, and the absolute position encoder battery has been depleted.
  2. The absolute position encoder battery was not replaced in time when it was low.
  3. The motor or drive unit is damaged.
  4. A new motor has been installed.

Troubleshooting Steps:

  1. If the machine is not used for an extended period, it should be powered on at least once a week.
  2. Replace the absolute position encoder battery promptly when it is low.
  3. Reset the absolute position zero point.

Machine Zero Point Reference: Refer to Section 5.6 the machine travel diagram.

Z1 Axis Zero Point: 5mm from the positive hard limit block of the Z1 axis.

X1 Axis Zero Point: The center of the T24 drilling tool position coincides with the spindle center. Y1 Axis Zero Point: The right face of the T01 tool coincides with the spindle center.

X2 Axis Zero Point: The sub-spindle center coincides with the spindle center Z2 Axis Zero Point: 5mm from the negative hard limit block of the Z2 axis.

Steps to Set the Zero Point:

  1. Use the rotary switch on the control panel to switch the machine to MPG control mode.
  2. Use the MPG to move each linear axis to the origin position indicated in the machine travel diagram in Section 5.6.
  3. Use the rotary switch on the control panel to switch the machine to reference point mode.
  4. Use the NC function keys to navigate: "Parameter Setting" → "Serial Parameters" → "General Serial Axis" → "Absolute Zero Point" to enter the mechanical zero point setting interface.

Move the cursor to select the corresponding axis number and complete the zero point setting.

7.2 Maintenance Precautions

  1. Qualified maintenance personnel should familiarize themselves with the electrical control principles and operating procedures of the machine before performing any repairs.
  2. Regularly clean the dust inside the electrical enclosure during machine operation.
  3. Ensure the power is turned off before cleaning.If the machine is idle for an extended period, power it on at least once a week and let it run at low speed for at least 2 hours.
  4. When a fault occurs, first check whether the power supply and control voltages are normal, whether the circuit breakers and switches are in the correct state, and whether all connectors and plugs are securely connected and not loose.
  5. Do not plug or unplug any connectors while the machine is powered on.
  6. Do not solder electronic circuits while the soldering iron is powered on.
  7. The positions of switches and limit blocks on the machine are pre-adjusted before leaving the factory. Users should not adjust them casually to avoid affecting normal operation.

Note: If the user cannot resolve the fault, please contact our company promptly for proper handling.

IMRMD (Igen Measuring and Revise Machining Degree of accuracy) is a set of efficient tools for rapid measurement and correction of coordinate transformation vector deviations on five-axis machining center, allowing complex five-axis deviation corrections with simple parameter selection.

This function is optional for the machine tool and must be purchased separately.

1.1 Function Introduction:

The IMRMD uses a standard ball and a standard probe to achieve five-axis coordinate transformation vector measurements. Simply fix a standard ball on the workbench and calculate the five-axis transformation vector by measuring the position of the standard ball at several specific angles for each rotary axis through the probe.

The IMRMD for five-axis machining center with RTCP is easy to operate and highly reliable, accomplishing five-axis transformation vector measurement and correction of both rotary axes in just a few minutes.

1.1      Application range:

  • Applicable system: Siemens ONE CNC,6.15 and above
  • Applicable machine：U5 five-axis machining center

2.1 Software and hardware composition:

  1. RENISHAW OMP60 standard probe kit     1PC
  2. φ30 standard ball measurement kit   1PC
  3. IMRMD measurement cycle toolkit       1PC

2.2 Option requirements.

  1. Run MyScreens option: This option is required when the total number of EasyScreen screens is greater than 5.

2.3 Main Features:

  1. Easy to operate. The ordinary machine operator can complete the entire measurement and correction work, without the need to understand the basic structure of the machine.
  2. For hardware, only standard probe and standard ball are required for measurement, eliminating the need for a variety of complicated gauges.
  3. Graphical parameter interface, easy and intuitive to set up.
  4. With automatic alignment function, the operator only needs to visually locate the probe and standard ball position. The program will automatically perform an alignment action before starting formal measurement, and then automatically start the entire measurement and correction process.
  5. The measurement results are displayed in tabular form for intuitive clarity.
  6. It has the highest five-axis transformation vector measurement accuracy and efficiency, and the results are stable.
  7. The machine can be recalibrated periodically with the IMRMD function, so that the machine always maintains the highest five-axis machining accuracy.

3.1 Prerequisites:

  1. IMRMD is mainly used to correct the five-axis RTCP accuracy, so the machine tool must have been manually performed five-axis transformation vector measurement and the five-axis related parameters have been set before using this function.
  2. Make sure that the geometric accuracy of the machine should be within the standard range, and the RTCP deviation is less than 1mm. Excessive deviation can cause collision with the standard ball during the movement of the probe, resulting in measurement failure.
  3. Make sure that the concentricity deviation of the probe and spindle axis is less than 0.005mm.
  4. The standard ball installation form is based on the principle of providing the maximum measurement angle. For VM500U machining center, the B-axis can achieve a measurement range of 0~ 100° when using the tilted ball seat; while only a measurement range of 0 ~ 60° can be achieved when using the vertical ball seat. Generally speaking, the larger the measuring range is, the more accurate the measurement can be.
  5. The probe needs to be calibrated for length and probe diameter.
  6. The operating level of the machine tool should not be lower than "Key Switch 3".

3.2 Hardware installation:

  1. The standard ball holder is fixed to the workbench by T-nut. The fixation must be firm so that the ceramic ball or probe is not damaged by falling off during the measurement process.
  2. The effective stroke of each linear axis after the workbench is turned over should be taken into account when the ball seat is fixing, meanwhile, the ball should be as far away from the center of the workbench as possible.
  3. As the B-axis stroke is -5 to 110°, the ball should be installed towards the direction of maximum B-axis angle to obtain the maximum measurement range.
  4. The probe is fixed to the spindle by means of an HSK shank.

3.3 Newly created cutting edge:

Before starting operation, the machine tool must be in a non-processing state and the system must be in normal condition.

  1. Press the [MENU SELECT] key at the bottom right corner of the screen, then click the [PARAMETER] soft key at the bottom of the screen to enter the [Tool List] screen.
  2. Use the arrow keys to move the cursor and select the probe in the tool table, ensuring that the probe is not on the spindle or mechanical jaws. If it is, return it to the magazine or unload it firstly.

  3. Press the [Tool Edge] soft key on the right, then press [Newly Created Tool Edge] to create a new tool edge D2.

  4. Load the probe to the spindle.
  5. Calibrate the tool edge D1, and refer to SINUMERIK 840D sl Measuring Cycle Manual for the probe calibration method.

3.4 Probe rough alignment:

  1. Switch the machine tool to JOG mode and manually move the Z-axis so that the probe is approximately 2 to 3mm from the surface of the ball, a value corresponding to the IMRMD parameter page RDFA.
  2. Move the X and Y axes so that the probe is visually aligned with the vertical center line of the sphere, with a deviation of less than 1mm as far as possible to avoid triggering an alarm during measurement.

 

3.5 IMRMD operating steps：

  1. Press the [CUSTOM] key, or press the [MENU SELECT] key at the bottom right corner of the screen, then press the screen soft key [CUSTOM].
  2. Press the [5-axis Param] soft key.
  3. Press the [IMRMD >] soft key to enter the IMRMD parameter setting screen.
  4. Set the IMRMD parameters (refer to the parameter description on the back page for details), and after that, press the [Execute >>] soft key on the right then the machine tool will automatically switch to AUTO mode and generate an operating command.
  5. Press the [CYCLE START] key, then the probe starts to move and carry out alignment. The measurement process starts automatically after the alignment is completed.
  6. Each rotary axis measures 3 positions, which vary depending on the type of ball seat selected.
  7. Default measurement position for tilted ball seat: [0°,45°,90°] for the B axis and [0°,120°,240°] for the C axis.
  8. Default measuring position of the vertical ball seat: [0°, 30°,60°] for the B axis and [0°,120°,240°] for the C axis.
  9. After measuring the two rotary axes, the operator will be prompted to press the [CYCLE START] key to start the calculation, and then the system starts to calculate the five-axis transformation vector values and displays the calculation results in tabular form.

  1. The values in the table show the vectorial relationship of the rotary axis with respect to the linear coordinates.
  2. Continue to press the [CYCLE START] key. When the measurement purpose is "measurement only", it will automatically return to the processing interface and the program operation ends.
  3. If the purpose of the measurement is "RTCP correction", the system will display a warning message with code 62315 after pressing the [CYCLE START] key again. Continue to press the [CYCLE START] key, then the new data will be written to the machine data.

3.6 Parameter description:

6.3.1 Parameter interface:

  1. Measuring Purpose:
    • Measuring Only: The measurement results are only displayed and are not written into the machine parameters;
    • RTCP Correction: The measurement results are written into the machine parameters to correct the RCTP deviation;
  2. Ball Seat Types:
    • Oblique Ball Seat: The club is installed at 45° on the ball seat. This method provides a greater measuring range;
    • Straight Ball Seat: The club is installed vertically on the seat;

    • Sphere Moving Mode:
      • Along the Arc: The probe moves around the surface of the ball along a circular path;
      •  Along the Line: The probe moves around the surface of the ball along a standard line path;
    •  Probe Contact Direction:
      • Based on Position: The probe automatically rotates the spindle before each contact with the ball, ensuring that the probe touches the ball in the same direction each time. This method minimizes probe alignment errors.
      • Fixed Direction: The probe does not rotate its direction each time it touches the ball but touches the ball directly.
    • Standard Ball Diameter:
      • The actual diameter of the ball can refer to the size marked on the club. The default is 30mm standard ball and the roundness of the ball should be less than 0.005mm;

    • Measuring Angle α0:

      • The probe touches the surface of the standard ball at an angle , which increases the measuring range when there is an interference between the probe and the club;

       

    • Align Meas. Stroke RDFA:

      • The moving distance the probe approaches the ball in the measuring direction during alignment, which is set by the distance between the probe and the surface of the ball after rough alignment;
    •  Measuring Stroke DFA: 
      • The moving distance the probe approaches the ball in the measuring direction during measurement;

    • Confidence Interval TSA:

      • Confidence area for the measurement results. The TSA contains the maximum allowable angular deviation values;

       

    • Measuring Times:

      •  The number of times the probe measures each point during alignment and measurement.

1.1 Range:

This chapter only introduces the alarms and information handled by the PLC. For the alarms and information sent by the NCK, please refer to the "SINUMERIK ONE SINAMICS S120 Diagnostic Manual";

The alarms in each section are sorted and arranged according to the increasing alarm numbers, and the serial numbers are not continuous;

2.1  Alarm Description Structure

Each alarm (fault or warning) is composed of a number and an alarm text, and is described by other information in the following categories:

  • Categories– Alarm message type;
  • Reaction – The performance of the machine tool after the alarm;
  • Reason – Cause of alarm；
  • Treatment – Troubleshooting method;
  • Response – Alarm message response method；

The alarm category is divided into fault message (FM) and basic message (BM):

  • Fault Message: After the fault is eliminated, press the <RESET> key to eliminate the alarm message；
  • BasicMessage：After the status is restored, the prompt message is automatically eliminated；

A non-sealing condition between the shank and cooled lubricant tube shall be cleared, or the tool will not allowed to use.

35.1 Attentions

  1. Read this manual in detail before using this TTC200 tool setter.
  2. Before installing the TTC200 tool setter, the logic of the output signal of the tool setter should be set up exactly and the output signal of the tool setter should be checked by avometer to make sure that it is normal. Read this manual for detail operation method.
  3. The logic of the output signal from the tool setter should be adjusted to fit the CNC system and the process of tool setting should be tested to make sure it is right before installing. Read this manual for detail operating method.
  4. If customers do not check signals according to the above method before installing and using, signals may not match the CNC system, which may lead to error action and damage the tool setter even the CNC machine.
  5. Statement: All the signals and connections should be checked to insure that they are all right according this manual before using the tool setter, so, Harbin Pioneer no longer provide free repairments for any mechanical damage after using, and also do not assume the responsibility of the damage of CNC machine, workpiece and jig whether customers consider it is caused by this tool setter.
  6. Guarantee: Harbin Pioneer has the responsibly to repair the product no matter what damage occurred during your using.(10 years)

35.2 Composition of the TTC200 tool setter

As it shown in the right picture, this TTC200 tool setter contains the following parts:

1)         Main part；

2)         Cable (model:LA04-06A-C3);

3)         Wrenches;

4)         Fasteners.

35.3 Functions and characters of the TTC200 tool setter

  1. Super hard working plane
    The working plane is manufactured by ceramic which has a good scratch resistance to make this tool setter has a long life-span.
  2. Floating and resetting of the working plane
    The working plane of this tool setter can move a little through ±X, ±Y and –Z and the max distance of the movement is 5.0mm through –Z. It can reset to the initial position with a high precision, when the tool move apart from the working plane 

  3. Principle of this tool setter

    When the tool touch the working plane, the position of the working plane will has a tiny

    change, and a special mechanism inside the tool setter will change the status of the electric circuit and generate triggered signal until the working plane return to its initial position.

    Special protection have been taken on the main body, output plug, cable and other parts of the tool setter, so that this tool setter can work in the liquid spraying environment.

  4. Good sealing performance

    Special protection have been taken on the main body, output plug, cable and other parts of the tool setter, so that this tool setter can work in the liquid spraying environment.

35.4 Parameters of the TTC200 tool setter

Diameter of the base (D2): 50mm

Size (L×H): 105×80mm

Diameter of the working plane (D1): 12.7mm

Height (H): 80±0.5mm

Weight: 500±20g

Quantity of the Red LED: 1pcs

Sense directions: ±X,±Y,-Z

Maximum over travel in –Z: 5±0.5mm

Trigger force (F): 3.4-3.6N（340-360gf

Hardness of the working plane: HRC93-94

Repeatability (2σ): 2.0μm

Parallelism between the working plane and the bottom: 3.0μm

Ingress protection: IP68

Rated input voltage: 24±50%V DC

Rated input current: 50mA

Length of the cable: 6m

Length of the jacket: 3m


TTC200 tool setter is an automatic, high precision device to set the parameters of the tools. Please read this user manual in detail before using. This device need maintenance regularly so that it will have a high precision and long life-span.

35.5 Install and adjust the tool setter on the bench

The parallelism between the working plane and the bottom surface has been adjusted to 0~0.003mm before leaving the factory, you can use the standard wrenches and fasteners to Install the tool setter on the bench by following steps:

  1. Loosen all the M4 and M6 screws on the base. (Picture1)
  2. Put the M12 screw into the central hole of the base and joint the base and the T-slot nut
    (Picture2)
  3. Choose a right place on the bench to install the base and use the wrench (LW10) to fasten the screws. (Picture3)
  4. Put the main part into the base and then fastened all the M4 and M6 screws. (Picture4,5,6) Attention: Make sure that there is no scissel chip on the surface of the tool setter and the bench, or it will influence the parallelism

You can use this tool setter directly after installing it on the bench. If you find the parallelism can not meet your needs, you can make phone calls to the salesman of Harbin Pioneer for the method to adjust it. As it shown in the right picture, there are three adjustment mechanisms on the TTC200 tool setter:

  1. Deflection adjusting screw
  2. Pitching adjusting screws
  3. Screws to adjust left and right.

Please fastened all the screws after the adjustment.

35.6 Connect the tool setter to the CNC system

  1. The status of the output signal can be changed conveniently
    In order to meet the different requirements of different kinds of CNC systems, the status of output signal can be switched by changing the polarity of the power supply. This method is a patent belongs to Harbin Pioneer, read the page12 for details.
  2. Transmission and indication of the signal
    When the tool setter touch the working plane, this TTC200 tool setter sent a switching signal to the CNC system through the cable (LA04-06A-C3) with the red LED on the body of the device light up.
  3. Choose the status of the signal and connect the cable

    As it shown in the right picture, the cable of the TTC200 tool setter has four cores: red, green, blue and black.

    Logic status 1: Connect the red line to +24V，the green one to 0V, the black and blue lines to the input of the CNC system, the logic status of the output signal is a normally opened signal (default setting).

    Logic status 2: Connect the green line to +24V, red line to 0V, the black and blue lines to the input of the CNC system, the logic status of the output signal is a normally closed signal.

    The logic status of the output signal should be set up exactly so that it can be distinguished by the CNC
    system.

  4. Check the output signal of the tool setter

    Before installing the tool setter, please connect the red line to +24V and the green one to 0V in the electrical cabinet of the CNC machine, power on the CNC machine, and then use the avometer to measure the resistance between the other two lines of the tool setter.

    Steps: Touch the working plane by hands to trigger the tool setter (the Red LED light up) and observe the value of the avometer.

    1. If the value is “ 0 ” (picture 1), the logic status of the output signal is normally closed SSR signal.
    2. If the value is not “ 0 ” (picture 2), the logic status of the tool setter is normally opened SSR signal.
  5. Check whether the signal can be received exactly by the CNC system

    Connect the black and blue lines to the signal ports of the CNC system, and then run the measuring program according to the following steps:

    Run the measuring program, press the working plane by hands and remove hands quickly, this tool setter will sent a signal to the CNC system, observe the movement of the machine to see whether the signal can be received exactly.

  6. Check the progress of automatic measurement

    When it is confirmed that the signal of the tool setter can be received exactly by the CNC system. It is suggested that you should run the program step by step and adjust the feed rate to low level for the first time. Press the emergency stop button as soon as possible when you find anything wrong.

    After all the steps above are completed, you can measure your tools automatically in normal feed rate many times to get skilled.

35.7 Set the length and diameter of the tool automatically

The purpose to set the length of the tool is to establish the position relationship between the cutting tool and the surface of the workpiece. This tool setter is a elastic device with fixed height, which is installed on the platform of the CNC machine, when the tool touch the working plane, the position relationship between the blade and the surface of the workpiece can be achieved indirectly according to the relationship between the blade and the bench.

Steps:

Semi-automatic operation: Move the spindle of the machine in manual mode and let the cutting tool axis upon the center of the working plane, make the cutting edge 10~20mm upper than the working plane.

Run the tool setting program, the length and the diameter value will be set up in the CNC system automatically.

Automatic operation: Put the program of preparation and semi- automatic operation into one program to run.

Read the software specification for detail information of the measuring program.

35.8 Maintenances of the tool setter

  1. It is suggested that you should clean the working plane and the tool to make sure it does not have any metal fragment and grease which may influence the accuracy of the measurement before each use of this tool setter.
  2. If the tool setter is unused for a long time, before using it again, please run the measuring program in low speed to make sure that the progress of the measurement is right. If you find something wrong, please check out the reason and solve the problem before using.
  3. Cable will move with the movement of the CNC machine, so it should be checked regularly to make sure it is in good condition. If you find the cable, cable interface or the stainless steel jacket are damaged, please replace it in time, or it may cause the tool setter and the CNC machine damaged and other serious consequences.
    Attention: TTC200 tool setter is a high precision device and it should be used and placed in a stable environment to avoid shock. The swinging mechanism has a certain life-span, do not press the working plane too much by hands.

35.9 Fault diagnosis

  1. When the tool setter cannot work normally, please find the reasons by following steps:
    1. Check the tool setting program to see whether it is correct.
    2. Check the status of the Red LED on the tool setter to see whether it can light up when you touch the working plane.
    3. Check the signal line (black and blue lines) between the tool setter and the CNC system by avometer to see whether it has output signal.
    4. Check the cable, plug between the tool setter and the CNC system.
    5. Check the power supply of the CNC system to see whether it is normal.
  2. When the precision of the tool setter is abnormal, please find the reasons by following steps:
    1. Check the working plane to see whether it is broken, whether it has metal scrap or other dust on the surface.
    2. Check the tool to see whether it has magnetism.
    3. Check the reset progress of the working plane to see whether it is normal.
    4. If you cannot check out the detail reason of the problem, or you could not slove the problem even if you find out the reason, please connect with the technical service department of the Harbin Pioneer. Tel:86-451- 82293947.

Article subtitle: Clothing and Personal Safety
Article body:
1. Tie back long hair that could get caught in the undercarriage.
  2. Wear safety equipment (helmet, goggles, safety shoes, etc.) to ensure your safety.
  3. Always wear a helmet if there are obstacles at height in the work area.
  4. Always wear a protective mask when working with workpieces such as magnesium alloys or graphite.
  5. Never wear loose or baggy clothing.
  6. Always close buttons completely and tie the arms of clothing so that they do not get caught in rotating parts.
  7. Do not operate the machine if you are under the influence of drugs with a strong effect, non-prescribed medication or alcohol.
  8. Do not operate the machine if you feel faint or lose consciousness.
  9. Always use gloves when loading or unloading workpieces or tools and when removing crisps.
  10. Always use safety shoes with steel toecaps and oil-resistant soles.

All operations, maintenance and cleaning work must be carried out in the safest possible conditions by wearing protective clothing (see table).

Always follow the personal safety standards and laws of the country in which the machine is used.

Title

Symbol

Description

 

Helmet

 

Helmet must be used in case of machine installation in place with risk of falling object.

 

 

Gloves

 

Gloves must be used when working with material with spikes or cutting edges, oil, coolant, workpieces contaminated with oil or coolant, swarf, etc.

Gloves must not be worn when working on the CNC keyboard or control panel.

 

 

Safety Shoes

 

 Safety shoes must be always used

 

Working clothes

 

 Working clothes must be always used.

 

 

Safety Glasses

 

 

Safety glasses must be used when use air or coolant gun.

 

Ear Protector

 

 

Ear protector must be used when work with air gun or when it is requested due to the acoustic condition of work place.

17.1 lonizing Radiations

This machine's radiation emissions are only electromagnetic low frequency type.

Test measure was done to demonstrate that radiation levels are within the allowed range specified in directive 2006/42/EC, please check the table below.

17.2 Not ionizing Radiations

The emission level for not ionizing radiations are negligible so it does not represent a risk for machine users.

17.3 Vibrations

If the machine is used in the right conditions and the maximum rating is respected, the vibrations level is low and not represent a danger.

17.4 Noise Emission

  1. The machine was checked for noise level based on actual norms.
  2. Noise level during normal work condition is not over 80dB.
  3. Particular care must be taken when air gun is used, the air gun can generate high noise level peak so ear protectors and safety glasses must be used.
  4. In case of not normal machine noise, it is highly recommended to call immediately the authorized technical service company.
  5. Values of areal noise produced by the machine, according to section 1.7.4.2 (u) ANNEX 1 of 2006/42/EC DIRECTIVE.

Measuring method: ISO 11202:1997

  • The measuring positions is four, as shown on drawing and is taken at 1600mm from the floor and at 1000mm from the machine.
  • The machine is completely closed with covers.
  • Spindle rotation at maximum speed. (not cutting)

NOTE

  1. The noise values indicated are emission levels and they don't represent absolute safe level.
  2. The relation that exists between exposition and emission level can't be reliably used to prove that a specific protection must be used.
  3. The operator exposition level must consider the time of exposition, the acoustic behavior of the room and finally the presence of other noise source (ex. other machines near the operator).
  4. The exposition level can be different for different country.
  5. This information is useful primary for a proper evaluation of risk and danger to which the operator is exposed.

17.5 Electromagnetic Emission

The machine was built for working in electromagnetic environment of industrial type (environment type A as defined in EN 60439-1, net and not public place or low voltage industrial environment).

  1. This machine is for environment of type A. In domestic environment this product can generate interference in radio frequency range, the final user must take care of this fact and find the right solution or require for a special execution to the machine's manufacturer.
  2. The conformity to maximum level of immunity and emission in case of industrial environment is obtained by the application of product harmonized technical norm.

  2. Machine internal area, where there is motor, actuator and transmission device like gears and/or belt, this area is protected by fixed covers.

The installation and commissioning procedure is summarised in the following steps. Keep a record of your installation for warranty purposes if you are self-installing the SYIL.

25.1 Steps Overview

  1. Check and record the state of the crate as delivered
  2. De-crate the machine
  3. Visually check the machine and accessories, photograph as needed
  4. Remove the loose accessories from the pallet
  5. Lift the machine off the pallet
  6. Seat the machine
  7. Check the coolant tank for watertightness and fill with coolant
  8. Connect the air
  9. Connect power cable
  10. Power on for first time
  11. Check the correct phase rotation and correct if needed
  12. Lift the Z axis off the table and clean the spindle
  13. Clean all greased or coated surface including the inside of the coolant tank
  14. Remove the shipping straps on the axes and the ATC
  15. Clean and install the armour on the X and Y axes
  16. Fill the oilers
  17. Level the machine
  18. Test functionality

25.2 Consumables Required during Installation and Commissioning

  • Slideway oil
  • WD-40 or similar
  • Grease
  • Air line/tool oil
  • Soluble coolant oil
  • Water

25.3 Disassembly of the Crate

Complete this task with the machine on solid ground with sufficient space around it.

NOTE: It is not advisable to remove the plywood panels in locations such as the bed of a lorry. Required tools for this task are:

  • a set of metric Allen Keys to remove the retaining screws
  • a crowbar to lift and pry the panels

25.3.1 How to disassemble the crate

  1. Using the crowbar, lift the lid portion of the crate such as to disengage the nails holding it in Lift the perimeter in total before attempting to move the lid
  2. Pull the free lid over side of the crate using the crowbar to dislodge it and to lift the lid as needed
  3. Once on the ground make the nails safe
  4. Select the first panel you will be removing and unscrew the self-drilling screws holding it in position on the base. (The hexagon head is 12 mm) Do not remove the screws holding the other panels yet
  5. Pry the panel free and lay Make any nails present safe
  6. Repeat until the crate is removed in its entirety

 

 

NOTICE
  • Moving the machine from a cold environment to a warm indoor location may cause moisture to condense on the machine
  • Moisture may affect the electronics and electrics of the machine or cause damage
  • Keep the machine covered for at least 24 hours for its temperature to equalise

25.4 Inspect the Machine for Damage

SYIL recommends that the machine equipment be inspected for shipping damage before unloading and placing machine onto foundation.

  • Remove all wrapping around machine
  • Examine the machine for structural damage
  • Note any shipping damage to the machine on the shipper’s bill of It is the customer’s responsibility to file a damage claim
  • Photograph any equipment damage for your records

25.5 Removing Machine from the Steel Pallet

SYIL recommends that the customer review this section to determine if there is proper capacity and ability to lift and place the machine into the location. If not, then a rigging agency should be contacted.

25.5.1 Preparation

Remove any loose items that may have been supplied with the machine. These may include some or all:

  • Coolant tray – now coolant tray is a single piece
  • Coolant washdown and air hose
  • Slide way armour panels
  • Toolkit
  • Manuals and paperwork

25.5.2 Releasing the machine from the pallet

The machine is held on to the base using 3 threaded studs. These pass through the jacking/levelling studs that in turn thread into the base of the machine.

Remove the nuts on the threaded studs.

 

25.6 Safe Lifting of the Machine off the Pallet

25.6.1 Lifting with a crane

  • Pay special attention to machine balance while lifting
  • Beware that the machine might be overturned because of an improper lifting Otherwise injury to people or machine damage may occur
  • Always assign a person to guide the way to ensure safety

When transporting the machine by crane, be sure to take the following precautions:

  • Position the base of the crane and the horizontal support plate so that the machine can be loaded with the fulcrum of the overhanging steel cable directly above its centre
  • Ensure the angle of the steel cable’s fulcrum does NOT exceed 90°. If possible, adjust the angle to 60°
  • Ensure that the steel cable is secured on both sides of the pedestal or with a fixing device designed for transporting heavy equipment

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

CAUTION
  • Lifting work should be performed only by qualified personnel
  • Lift the machine slowly while ensuring it is balanced on all sides and that the lifting cables are positioned against its external casing or outermost components
  • If two or more people are lifting the machine, they should communicate to ensure they exert force on it simultaneously and in the same direction
  • Do not use cables of inadequate length or that have sustained rust or other damage to lift the machine
  • Lift the machine slowly. When one of the steel cables has reached maximum tension, temporarily halt lifting and check that the machine is balanced before continuing to lift it to the designated height
  • The machine should be lowered slowly. When lowered almost to the ground, temporarily halt lowering and check that the machine’s base is level and aligned with the intended position, then resume lowering to set it down completely

25.6.2 Lifting with a Forklift

When transporting the machine by forklift, be sure to take the following precautions:

  • Ensure you have read and understood the manual’s safety instructions before installing the machine
  • Ensure the ground is free of lubricant oil, grease, or water to prevent slipping and falling during installation
  • Before beginning installation, check and confirm that the machine has been placed in the correct position

 

 

 

 

CAUTION
  • Only qualified personnel to operate a forklift should attempt to transport the machine
  • In order to avoid damaging the machine or its surroundings, a minimum of two people should be present while operating the forklift
  • Lower the machine slowly to prevent impact with the ground
  • A wooden pallet can be used to support the machine during the lifting process

This machine should be lifted and moved by a forklift. Attention should be paid to the machine balance during lifting and moving. This machine should be lifted under the following conditions:

  • The weight of the machine is approximately 2,000 Kg. It is the responsibility of the operator to ensure that the rating of the forklift and the load capacity of the forks at the load distance are suitable for the task.
  • Beware that the lifting truck might overturn because of an improper lifting This might cause people injury and damage the machine
  • Always assign a person to guide the way to ensure safety

NOTE: Extended forks are required for this operation to be completed with ease.

NOTE: Having a selection of timber to hand will help with any potential mismatch in level of the front and rear of the machine.

NOTE: Do not lift the machine higher than it needs to be lifted. Adjust the levelling screws to get enough clearance, if necessary.

25.7 Installing the feet

The studs that secure the machine to the shipping pallet must be retained when the machine is lifted. The studs are then used to hold the cast iron feet to the machine for easy relocation of the machine.

Reuse the shipping nuts on the studs.

NOTE: Do NOT place the thick steel washer on the stud under the foot. This will result in the hexagon head of the stud protruding from the foot and result in the machine being unstable.

25.8 Fitting Through Low Doors

The SYIL X5 has two cable chains extending past the head of the machine. It may become necessary to unscrew these to allow the machine to pass through doors with an opening height of less than 2.1 m. 

To loosen the cable chains, unscrew the 4 cap head screws, 2x each side, holding them to the column.

25.9 Test the Coolant Tray for Water Tightness

While the machine is not yet connected to the coolant hoses and the power, test the seal of the plug by doing these steps:

  1. Wipe down the coolant tank to remove excess oils
  2. Fill with water
  3. Let the tray sit for a few hours to identify if there are any small leaks

  4. If the tray is leaking from:

    • the plug, remove the plug and reapply the PTFE tape

    • any other location, contact the customer service

25.10 Connect the Coolant Hoses and Pump

  1. Move the coolant tank into position behind the machine
  2. Align the chip trays with the spouts on the machine casting
  3. Screw and tighten the rubber coolant hose on to the pump outlet
  4. Insert the second return line into the smaller hole of the coolant tank
  5. Connect the power connector of the pump to the socket on the right hand side of the electrical enclosure
 
 

25.11 Connecting the Air Supply

NOTE: The factory supplied air inlet fitting receives a 10 mm pneumatic hose.

Push the hose into the inlet until it is fully seated. Test the grip of the connection by pulling the hose.

25.11.1 Air and consumables required

Compressed air is required for:

  • Clearing swarf and cuttings – Air blast (activate with macro M07)
  • Ensuring tool holder tapers are clean during tool change
  • Air curtain of the Keeps coolant and debris out of the high speed elements of the cartridge while also offering cooling to the cartridge

The Air Curtain of the spindle has a parameterised time delay. Contact customer service for instructions.

A 90 psi with capacity more than 50 litre compressor is necessary for normal use if it is rated for extended duty cycles.

25.12 Connecting Power

NOTE: See Chapter 5 before connecting the machine to the power supply. Open the electrical cabinet using the keys provided in the toolbox.

Under the safety isolator switch, a terminal block can be seen as shown in Figure below.

NOTE: Use crimp terminals with a 6 mm hole.

At this stage, also connect the MPG to the controller panel

25.12.1 Pre-Power ON Checks

Before powering on, check the following:

  1. Power cable is secure
  2. Using a multimeter check that the PE (Earth) cables are all connected to the PE connection of the input terminal
  3. Check that all DIN rail mounted electrical components are held well in place and have not come loose during shipping
  4. Gently pull each of the cables in terminal block in the electrical panel to ensure they are tight
  5. Take the panel off the rear of the controller and inspect the cables in that enclosure

25.12.2  First Power ON

NOTE: Keep the electrical cabinet doors always closed before powering on. The isolator will not rotate unless the door is closed.

  1. Ensure that the Emergency Stop on the front panel is also pressed in

  2. After the isolator switch is turned on, the following elements are audible:

    • Lubrication pump

    • Electrical cabinet fans and chiller

    • Spindle fan

  3. Press the Green illuminated button to start the controller
    NOTE: The Controller On button for the machines is shown in Figures below. 

    The machine will then boot up.

    NOTE: When the machine is fully booted, the controller may give the E-stop warning as well as the air pressure low warning.

    NOTE: It is preferable to use the MPG for this operation. Do not attempt to move the X or Y axes yet.

  4. Release the E-stop button and press the relevant Reset button to clear any
  5. Move the machine Move the Z axis up so that the supporting block or tube can be removed.

25.12.3 Checking phase rotation

NOTE: It is very important that the 3 phases of the power cable are installed in the correct sequence. The effect of incorrect phase sequence is to make 3 phase synchronous motors rotate in the opposite direction they are intended.

To check the correct sequence, the easiest test is to check the rotation of the coolant pump. The pump must rotate in the counterclockwise direction. See Figure below

Remove the cover of the pump’s fan to be able to see the rotation easier, if needed. Remember to replace the cover to avoid injury or damage to the pump.

NOTE: Rotation of the pump is the best indicator of the phases of the 3-phase supply being installed correctly. If the pump rotates in the incorrect direction:

  1. Power off the machine and isolate the power
  2. Swap any two of the power cables on the power inlet terminal

25.12.4 Clean the machine

NOTE: The machine will be shipped with some surfaces covered in a protective wax, while others are covered in grease

  1. Clean the machine using WD-40 and rags
  2. Clean the spindle taper
  3. Clean the coolant Remnants of oil from the testing of the machine may be found

25.12.5 Check Lubrication Circuit

The lubrication pump can be activated manually by pressing the FEED button on it.

  1. Hold for 2-5 seconds and observe the pressure dial
  2. Look in the machine to ensure that oil has come through into the ways and ballscrews

NOTE: The 16 tool version does not have the straps. Shipping straps are now painted red for easy identification.

Straps are placed:

  • On the 12 tool umbrella type tool changer
  • Between the table saddle and the table to restrain the X axis
  • Between the table saddle and the Y axis ballscrew bearing housing

Ensure that power is switched OFF and the air system is NOT pressurised. Remove the ATC retaining strap

Before removing the axis retention straps:

  2. Press the Emergency STOP button to ensure that the axes do not lose reference accidentally
  3. Remove the shipping straps and store them for future

25.14 Fitting the Axis Armour

The axis covers are shipped removed. A total of 3 loose elements are to install:

  • The front cover of the X axis
  • 2 angle plates (see below)

Assemble the armour as follow:

  2. Using the two angle brackets (See Figure below), connect the front and rear Y axis See Figure below  for correct installation of the angles
  3. Assemble the front X axis cover

25.16 Levelling after Seating

Use a precision level to level the machine with a sensitivity of 0.02 mm/m, example shown in Figure below

Connect power and air to have access to the bed. This allows to move the Z axis up and out of the way.

The machine is levelled through the 3 jacking screws that that locate on the conical machine feet. Applying grease to the threads makes the process easier, as does the use of a ratchet socket wrench. For optimum performance of the machine, it is advisable to achieve a level in the X and Y axes of 0.04 mm/m or better.

The procedure is as follows:

  1. Using all three of the jack bolts, lift the machine such that the coolant tray slides under it with Depending
  2. on the floor’s flatness, this may Typically, an extension of 30 mm is required
  3. Place the spirit level along the X axis of the machine and adjust the lowest foot
  4. It is easier to do with two people, one adjusting, the other advising of the level
  5. Once the bubble of the spirit level is centred in the sight glass, the right-to-left level is good
  6. Place the spirit level parallel to the Y axis of the machine and adjust the front foot
  7. When the front to back is level, check that the coolant tray is still able to be installed and removed easily
  8. If the coolant tray fowls the enclosure, increase the height of the whole machine but equal amounts on all three feet, then repeat the levelling process

2.1 Description of tool magazine

The tool can be loaded in and unloaded from the magazine not only manually through hand-operated door at the top of the magazine, but also through the spindle.

The magazine is connected to machining space through automatic door of magazine. When the door closes, the space between them is isolated. Automatic loading tool movement between spindle and tool is achieved by tool changing-manipulator.

The passage to magazine is monitored by photoelectric switch.

Magazine can be manually operated only in a state of JOG.

Machine program can be operated only when the magazine door closes. Please confirm that no one is within the tool magazine when machine tool is operated and after maintenance.

2.2 Technical parameters

2.3 Prerequisites

Check and confirm：

  • Alarm free for the operation panel
  • Air pressure value is normal.

2.4 Basic operation

2.4.1 General notes

It must be noted first that no employee is in the magazine when the magazine is moved manually.

For security reasons, after the safety door of machine tool is opened, manual loading & unloading tool key can be pressed to operate only after the unloading tool preparation key is pressed.

After automatic tool changing, wrong tool installing on the magazine or wrong record on tool management table can lead to processing errors or collision, and may cause interruption of the tool changing process.

  • The allocation of the present magazine shall always be noted when loading &unloding tools.
  • Every loading in & unloading from the tool case for tools shall be updated in the tool management table. Tools can be identified by the numerical control system only through tool names registered on the tool management table.
  • Special tool with major diameter (refer to Technical Data).
  • Additional requirements for the oversized tool shall be registered on the tool management table (encode in a fixed position).
  • Make sure that the actual tool conditions shall be strictly in accordance with records in the tool table.

2.4.2 Magazine operation

Magazine shall be operated in the mode of JOG.

Manual mode (MAG JOG) of magazine shall be activated only in the following situations:

  • Exception handling of tool magazine
  • Check magazine by manual operation

All operations can be finished in the tool magazine management interface at normal using.

The blade is sharp, so there is a risk of injury if toughing the blade.

Please wear safety gloves.

Don’t clamp the tool within the range of synchro flange.

2.4.2.1 Enter the tool management interface

Procedures:

  •  Press <MENU SELECT> key. 
  •  Press[Parameter]soft key. 
  •  Press[Tool List]soft key，magazine can be operated here. 

2.4.2.2 Rotate the tool manually

Procedures:

  •  Press machine tool panel <JOG> key (manual). 
  •  Press machine tool panel <MAG JOG> key （magazine manual mode）. 
  • Close the magazine door.
  • Press key 2: Magazine rotates clockwise.
  • Press key 3: Magazine rotates counterclockwise.

Key 1: unlock key of the magazine door;

The magazine can be rotated manually only when magazine door is closed.

2.4.3 Tool list

Tool list shows the present use condition of tool paths, that is to say, a tool is placed on the spindle, manipulator or other positions in the magazine.

The specification on tool management in numerical control system materials

shall also be valued.

2.4.2 Created a new tool

Plug the tool in the present cursor position (spindle, magazine vacancy or buffer vacancy).

Before operation, make sure that the magazine door at the loading point 2 is closed.

When creating a new tool in the spindle, you shall plug the tool in the spindle manually, and respond from the prompts.

When creating a new tool in idle magazine, the magazine will rotate a selected tool path to the position of loading point 2 automatically, after it is in place, the corresponding tool shall be plugged from the prompts, and the magazine door will be closed.

Tools newly created apart from the magazine and spindle shall be manual tools, when they are called, the spindle will move to the tool installing position firstly, then they will be plugged in the spindle manually.

Create a new tool in the spindle

Procedures:

  • Select the spindle in the tool list through moving cursor.


    In [Parameter] interface, click soft key [New Tool]
  •  Select required tools in the pop-up list. 
  •  Click [OK] 
  • Number, letter or Chinese can be entered when setting the tool name. If the entered tool name has the same name with the original tool name, this tool is the sister tool of the original tool. For specification on the sister tool, please refer to the Chapter “Tool management” of
    《SINUMERIK ONE Universal Operating
    Manual》.
  • Move the cursor to set other parameters of tool.
  • Plug the tool on the spindle manually, then press loading & unloading tool key <OK> on the machine tool panel to finish loading. 

Installing backwards or plugging dislocation of tool may damage the magazine or

spindle during tool changing; be sure to check carefully after the tool is plugged.

Create a new tool in the buffer:

Tools in the magazine of the buffer are manual; tools put outside the magazine for daily use can be stored in this zone.

Procedures:

  • Select a vacancy in the buffer.
  •  In the interface [Parameter], click the function key [New Tool]. 
  • Select required tools in the pop-up list.
  •  Click [OK]. 
  • Enter tool name and related tool parameters.

2.4.5 Tool loading

Loading, used for plugging tool within the buffer in magazine or spindle manually.

Load program appears only when selected tool path or spindle is vacant.

Prerequisites

Be sure to align down the guide gib (German angle projection).

The blade is sharp, so there is a risk of injury if toughing the blade.

Please wear safety gloves.

Don’t clamp the tool within the range of synchro flange.

Installing backwards of plugging dislocation may damage the magazine or spindle during tool changing; be sure to check carefully after the tool is plugged.

  • When closing the tool magazine, the door lock will block automatically.
  • A mechanical drop-proof mechanism keeps tools in the tool cylinder.
  • Load the tool in the magazine

Tool-loading in the magazine can be operated in the mode of JOG.

2.7 Protection function

2.7.1 Interlocked operation function

This function mainly aims at manual operation of the magazine to prevent collisions inside the magazine caused by human error.

After <MAG JOG> is activated, there are the following protection functions:

When the magazine door opens, the magazine stops rotating;

When the automatic door closes, positive shift of the mechanism arm is limited;

When the stroke of negative shift manually of the mechanism arm is limited, the arm will not come into the range of the tool link;

When the mechanism arm is in the tool chain, the tool magazine will be forbidden to rotate.

2.8 Maintenance

2.8.1 Tool magazine cleanup

Iron dust on moving parts of tool magazine shall be cleaned after work every day.

2.8.2 Lubrication check

  • With displacement of axis X, Y and Z, guide lubrication pump starts automatically instead of starting manually.
  • Check the guide lubrication line every week, if there is blockage, it shall be dealt with promptly.
  • Check if there is enough grease on the moving parts of tool chain in magazine; take care of replenishing the grease in time.

The following sections provide guidelines for the correct maintenance of SYIL X and T Series machines.

To prevent hazardous conditions that can result in injury or equipment damage, ensure that the equipment and personnel at your worksite fully satisfy these requirements.

For some procedures, to be performed, specialist tooling may be required. Contact Technical Support for advice as needed.

27.1 Lockout – Tagout

Always follow your company lockout tagout procedure in addition to the instruction given here

27.1.1 Lockout procedures and indicators

The mains isolator switch is designed to be locked out with a padlock when doing the lockout. Use a 5 mm

diameter padlock.

To prevent the possibility of accidental startup and the sudden release of accumulated energy, put the SYIL into lockout before beginning inspection and maintenance work.

During lockout, post signs to indicate the machine’s service status and prevent unauthorized personnel from accessing its main energy isolation facilities. In addition, paste labels over the closure of the electrical cabinet in such a way that opening it requires breaking or tearing them, thus indicating whether any attempt has been made to activate the equipment during lockout.

27.2 Lubrication

It is critical that the machine rolling and sliding elements remain lubricated. Failure of the lubrication system can lead to rapid damage to costly elements such as ballscrews, linear rails and sliders.

The automatic oiler is set on a timer controlled by the PLC ladder of the controller. Parameters within the service level of the controllers dictate the interval at which the oiler will run and for how long each burst is.

Always ensure the correct grade of lubricant is used in the automatic lubrication pump as indicated on the sticker above the oiler.

It is recommended that an ISO 32 grade oil is used rather than any heavier oils.

The Automatic Tool Changer, lubrication of the two roller runners is key. Use waterproof grease on the bearings and the runners.

27.5 Resetting the Home Position of Axes

All SYIL CNC machines work with absolute position servo motor, negating the need for home switches. This means that if during installation or maintenance, if the servo motors of the axes are disconnected either electrically, from the cables, or mechanically from the mounts and ballscrews, their absolute position must be reset.

This process writes the absolute encoder position to the controller such that the rotational position of the servo motor corresponds correctly to the linear location of the axis it is connected to.

The X, Y and Z axis follow the same process, while the spindle orientation, (Referred to in other service bulletins as setting the ORI position), is different.

As the Z axis is also responsible for actuating the tool changer, a separate set of steps is required for resetting the actual position of the Z axis prior to resetting the home position.

27.7Recovering after a Crash

It is not uncommon for new as well as experienced users to miscalculate tool lengths or mistakenly declare WCS coordinates resulting in the machine violently ramming into the workpiece.

To protect the machine, torque limits have been defined in the Controller and Drivers such that the machine will error in the event of a crash. In the event of a very violent crash, it is possible that the ballscrew to motor coupling may slip resulting in the apparent machine coordinates not corresponding to those set by the factory.

In this case, it is very important to establish if the machine has lost its absolute positions. The implications are that the machine may hit hard stops on any of the axis travels before the soft limits become active. In the case of the Z axis, the tool change position may be incorrect in space and an result in further errors or damage if not corrected.

  6. Manually rotate the spindle or motor and check the belt is correctly seated on the spindle and motor pulleys
  7. Tighten the 4 x M10 screws to 5 Nm
  8. As a starting point tension, the belt must be tight enough not to be able to twist one side more than 45°, or deflect more than 6 mm
  9. If the belt is adjusted the tighten the 4 x M10 screws to 35 Nm or repeat the previous steps to tighten the belt if necessary
  10. Refit the panels 

27.10 Other Maintenance Tasks

For more information on other maintenance tasks, for example torquing the ballscrew mounting screws or bearing replacement, refer to https://support.SYIL.com or contact customer service.

This machine is composed mainly with iron, steel, cast iron and other materials like rubber and plastic, all materials that isn't dangerous.

The disposal action of these components doesn't require particular procedure.

Disposal of oil and other reject materials will be done in observance of environment norms and laws in force for the country of machine installation and use.

1. Immediately remove all water and oil spills from the floor of machine vicinity and keep the floor dry to prevent accidents.
  2. Keep combustible materials away from the work area and any other place where there are hot chips.
  3. Always provide sufficient lighting in the work area.
  4. Always provide sufficient working space for maintenance work when installing the machine.
  5. Never place tools or other potentially dangerous object on top of the headstock, turret and covers.
  6. Protect all cables which are along the floor from being damaged by chips: damaged cables and wires will cause current leakage and short-circuit.
  7. Use strong service platforms only and make sure that nothing can slip off them.
  8. Make sure that the nominal cross-sectional area of the power supply cable between the factory power supply switch and the machine main power breaker is such as to enable a stable supply for operation at the maximum output.

26.2 Adding Coolant to the Coolant tank

Coolant used in metal cutting machines is in most cases a mixture or water and a mixable oil. A wide range of products exists with differencing properties to suit a wide variety of applications.

In all cases, the oil must be mixed into the water well for the concentration to be constant throughout the volume of fluid. Good mixing can be achieved using purpose made mixing systems offered by coolant fluid suppliers, or by pouring the required proportions of water and oil into the coolant tank directly.

In the case where the fluids are mixed inside the coolant tank, the fluids must be stirred while in the tank. Stir by doing these steps:

  1. Remove the chip trays and mesh filters from the coolant See Figure 41
  2. Unscrew and remove the secondary covers of the coolant tank under the chip trays. See Figure 41 
     



 

 

  1. Stir the fluid on both sides of the pump using a suitable method
 

  1. Stir the fluid using a suitable tool

 NOTE: A good example of a suitable tool that may be used is a cordless drill with a paint stirrer.

25.3 Switching ON and Starting

Connected to the power supply.

There are two stages to this operation to guard against unexpected starting of the machine in the case of a general power failure:

Stage 1: Give power to the machine Stage 2: Start the control system

NOTE: Rapidly switching the mains OFF and back ON may result in Servo Driver errors or damage. Always allow

26.4 Switching OFF and Powering Down

The CNC controllers may be powered down by pressing their respective OFF buttons. This may be useful in certain circumstances. This will not reset the servo drivers or timing relays within the Electrical Cabinet.

  2. Switch OFF the CNC controller using the RED illuminated button located on the controller panel
  3. Switch on the machine’s main isolator switch
  4. Switch on the mains power of the facility if required

26.5 Warm-Up Procedure

NOTE: Never rapid the SYIL X5 before ensuring lubrication is present and machine is warmed up.

Running a machine that has not been used for an extended period of time can cause faults and damage to the equipment due to the thermal expansion and contraction of its components while inactive. Always run cycles to prepare the machine to resume running following a long period of inactivity.

Complete a sufficient warmup procedure for the axes to ensure accuracy in machining. This will ensure the bearings are correctly lubricated, the ballscrews and the body of the SYIL X5 are at a nominal temperature. Contact the customer service for more information on the correct warmup procedure.

26.6 Spindle Care during Operation

For a long life of the spindle, it is the responsibility of the user to ensure they are operating within the recommended parameters. If a premature failure of the spindle occurs, replacement will depend on the outcome of investigation by the spindle manufacturer. Ensure a long life of the spindle by following these indications:

  • A new spindle must be allowed to run in
  • Do not start heavy machining until the spindle has completed the run-in procedure (See Chapter 14) and no abnormal or unexpected temperatures, vibration or noise is experienced
  • During normal operation, never exceed the speed and torque rating of the spindle
  • Follow the cooldown procedure if the spindle cartridge is seen to overheat
  • Never allow the spindle cartridge to exceed 20 °C above ambient temperature
  • Never allow the spindle cartridge to exceed 55 °C
  • Always use balanced tooling and tool holders
  • Always keep the spindle clean and complete a warm-up cycle before operating the machine

26.7 Spindle Air Curtain

An air curtain system is used to keep the spindle cool and free from debris.

The air curtain continuously leaks air through the body of the spindle cartridge. Be aware that this will require a significant volume of air to be available to the machine.

During a tool change additional air is exhausted through the spindle taper to eject any chips or cutting on the tool holder.

Each tool used in a program must be loaded into the tool changer’s magazine and the location number noted. Do not attempt to place a tool in a location that is not empty or corresponds to the tool currently in the spindle. Load the tool safely by following method1 or method  

(a) Loading Method 1

  1. Turn the user key to the unlocked position (MSO1)
  2. Using the MAG CCW or MAG CW turn so that the required tool location number aligns with the opening at 3 o’clock



  3. Unlock and open the main door
  4. Holding the tool holder from the gauge, and not the taper aligns and slide the V Groove into the spring-loaded jaws
  5. Close the door again to advance to the next tool location

  1. Jog the Z axis up until it reaches the top limit and the soft limit warning displays
