2. Operation

2.1 Composition of the Operation Panel

2.2    Manual Operation

2.2.1    Manual Operation Panel

The operation panel is shown in the figure below. Due to updates in machine configurations and versions, the actual panel may differ. Please refer to the configuration on the actual machine.

2.2.1.1    Model Selection

The machine has two operation modes: Manual and Automatic.
Manual Operation is used when adjusting the machine and involves manual control of the machine functions. Manual operation cannot perform complete workpiece machining. It includes axis control, coolant control, grinding wheel and workpiece spindle control, measuring instrument control, workpiece clamping control, and work light control.

Automatic Operation refers to the machine automatically performing grinding operations. In this mode, the CNC program can be executed for automatic grinding. Once the automatic cycle starts, no manual intervention is required until the program finishes running. Automatic operation also allows for functions such as single block execution, optional stop, block skip, handwheel insertion, and other CNC program run controls.

2.2.1.2            Feedrate Override

Feedrate override is used to control the speed multiplier of the machine’s movement without changing the programmed feedrate. The feedrate override is expressed as a percentage of the programmed feedrate, i.e.: Actual Feedrate = Programmed Feedrate × Feedrate Override.

2.2.1.3    Emergency Stop

Emergency Stop refers to the immediate shutdown of the machine in case of an abnormal situation. By pressing the Emergency Stop button, the system will be forced to stop immediately. Once the Emergency Stop button is pressed, it does not reset automatically. The machine can only resume operation after the Emergency Stop button has been released and reset.

2.2.1.4    System ON/OFF

After turning on the main power switch on the control cabinet, the machine does not start immediately. The following steps are required to start the machine. As shown in the figure, press the white Power ON button to officially start the system. Once the system startup is complete, the machine can be put into operation. Of course, a series of additional operations are required to bring the system to its normal working state.

Startup Sequence:

  • Turn on the system power.
  • Wait for the system to start up.
  • Release the Emergency Stop button.
  • Check for any alarm messages.
  • Reset any alarm messages.
  • The machine is considered fully started when no alarms are present.

Shutdown Sequence:

  • Press the Emergency Stop button.
  • Press the OFF button to turn off the system power.
  • Turn off the main power switch on the control cabinet.

2.2.1.5    Program Protection

Program protection is controlled by the key switch on the panel. When program protection is enabled, NC user programs cannot be modified or edited. To modify or edit an NC program, the program protection key switch must be turned to the OFF position.

2.2.1.6    Axis Movement

Manual Mode:
In manual mode, axis movement is performed manually, allowing the servo axes to be operated and moved using the panel buttons. The movement speed can be adjusted using the feedrate override dial. The maximum manual movement speed is limited by the value of parameter 1423.

 Handwheelmode：

In handwheel mode, axis movement is controlled using the handwheel pulse generator. The axis and movement multiplier are selected via the axis selection switch and the override dial. The direction and speed of the handwheel rotation determine the direction and speed of the axis movement.

In MDI mode, the corresponding function codes can be entered to perform specific actions.
After entering the function commands, press the Cycle Start button to execute the functions

2.4    Functional Screen Operation

The grinding parameter functional screen is a secondary development based on the FANUC system. It features simple operation, a user-friendly interface, and ease of use. The grinding parameter screen can be accessed through the   key located on the system’ s MDI screen. The interface is shown in the figure below.

2.4.1    Main Screen

After opening the functional screen, press <MAIN> to enter the main screen. The main screen displays information related to the grinding process.

2.4.1.1    Workpiece Zero Point
In the main screen, press the designated    key to enter the grinding zero-point setting screen. Three workpiece coordinate systems are predefined for grinding zero-point configuration. According to the workpiece zero point used in the actual program, set the origin in the corresponding workpiece coordinate system column. The screen is shown as follows

2.4.1.1.1    Zero-Point Input Methods
Three zero-point input methods are provided: Direct Input, Easy Setting, and Incremental Input (+Input) — each applicable to different situations.

    Direct Input
The mechanical coordinate value of the axis to be set is directly entered into the corresponding coordinate definition input field.

    Easy Setting

By pressing the designated    key on the screen, the current coordinate value can be automatically recorded into the coordinate system position where the cursor is located.
    +Input (Incremental Input)

By using the  key on the screen, arithmetic input can be performed on the existing coordinate system values. This method is typically used for dimensional adjustments or position compensation.

2.4.1.1.2    Origin Input Method

2.4.1.2    Dressing Origin

In the main screen, press the designated    key to open the dressing origin setting screen. Two coordinate systems are reserved for defining the dressing origin.

2.4.1.2.1    Dressing Origin Setting
Similar to the workpiece zero-point operation, three input methods are also provided. For detailed procedures, refer to the Workpiece Zero-Point Input section.

2.4.1.2.2    Grinding Wheel Definition

The grinding wheel definition can be accessed through the    key on the dressing origin setting screen.
It is used to define parameters such as wheel width, linear speed (optional), wheel outer diameter, minimum width, and new wheel outer diameter.
The screen is shown as follows:

2.4.1.2.3    Replacing a New Grinding Wheel
When a new grinding wheel needs to be replaced, perform the operation   key on the grinding wheel screen. The wheel outer diameter will be automatically set to the new wheel diameter.

At the same time, the origin values of the dressing coordinate systems (G57/G58) and the workpiece coordinate systems (G54/G55/G56) will be reset to zero.
After replacing the new grinding wheel, it is necessary to re-establish both the dressing and grinding zero points

2.4.1.2.4    Dressing Return Position
On the dressing origin screen, press the   key to open the Dressing Return Position setting screen, as shown below.

When the Dressing Safe Point value is not zero, the wheel will return to that position after dressing is completed; otherwise, it will return to the X-axis machine origin.

2.4.1.3    End-Face Measurement Origin

The end-face measuring device is used to measure the mounting position of the workpiece and to compensate for any lateral deviation caused by workpiece clamping.

The End-Face Measurement Origin serves as the reference point for surface measurement, and G59 is dedicated to setting this origin.

The input methods and procedures for defining the end-face origin are the same as those used for the workpiece origin.

2.4.2    Dressing
Before starting the grinding process, the grinding wheel must first be dressed. According to the requirements of the workpiece, the wheel can be dressed into a suitable shape.

Wheel dressing is divided into count-based dressing and call-based dressing. Both methods can complete the dressing process; however, it is essential to correctly set the dressing origin beforehand.

During the dressing process, the system automatically compensates for the material removed from the wheel to ensure that the final grinding dimensions remain unaffected.

On the main screen, press the     key to open the editing screen. Select the corresponding   key to enter the Dressing Cycle Parameters screen, and choose either the Dressing Cycle or Count-Based Dressing option to configure the relevant parameters.

2.4.2.1    Count-Based Dressing

In count-based dressing, during the automatic grinding cycle, the system tracks the number of completed grinding cycles. When the preset count value is reached, the machine automatically performs a dressing operation.

Once the count threshold is met, the system waits for the current grinding cycle to finish, then executes the dressing cycle before starting the next grinding operation.

After the dressing is completed, the machine automatically resumes the grinding process.

2.4.2.2    Dressing Cycle

A dressing cycle refers to invoking the wheel dressing routine, used for dressing a wheel individually or when using a new wheel. The parameters of the wheel dressing cycle are independent from those of the counted dressing cycle, but the profile parameters are the same. Compared to the counted dressing cycle, the dressing cycle additionally defines the dressing path method.

Dressing Path Method: 0 – Formed Wheel；1 – Plain Wheel.

A new wheel is initially treated as a plain wheel. When specified as a plain wheel, its profile is first roughly dressed at high speed according to the defined contour. Once the wheel has been fully formed, the dressing path method is automatically reset to 0.

2.4.3    Face Measurement

Face measurement refers to the positioning measurement of the wheel face, used to compensate for the displacement error of the grinding start point caused by variations in workpiece clamping. Before executing the face measurement cycle G406, the probe calibration program G405 must be performed first.

Face measurement uses coordinate system G59. Before setting measurement parameters and invoking the cycle, the face measurement origin must be defined.
Face Measurement Program: G405 Dd Ff. / G406 Dd Ff Hh Qq.
Open the face measurement interface：  ->  ->   or    .

 

2.4.3.1    Face Probe Calibration

The face probe calibration cycle G405 is called using the program G405 for face measurement calibration. A qualified workpiece is selected as the reference standard. After calibration, all measurements of subsequent workpieces are relative to this reference standard. Face measurement is meaningful only after calibration.

The face measurement origin interface records the measurement values of the reference standard. These values are updated after executing the standard program. In addition, the interface also stores the reference workpiece correction value, which is the Z-axis coordinate of the reference workpiece in its workpiece coordinate system. This value is used to restore the Z-axis workpiece origin of the reference standard.

Performing the calibration cycle periodically can improve the accuracy of face measurements.

2.4.3.2    Face Measurement

The face measurement cycle G406 is invoked using the program G406 to perform face measurements. After calibration, executing G406 measures a new workpiece. The deviation relative to the reference standard is either stored in the specified variable or used to update the specified workpiece coordinate system

 

2.4.4    Air Gap Elimination

The air gap elimination sensor (optional feature) is used during the wheel air gap segment. When a signal from the air gap elimination sensor is detected, the program immediately jumps to the next segment for execution.

2.4.5    Outer Diameter Measurement

Outer    diameter measurement uses the outer diameter measurement cycle. The maximum grinding value for    outer    diameter measurement should be set to ensure that the measuring device can obtain a measurement signal before grinding reaches the specified value.

The measurement status allows verification of whether the signals from P1 to P4 are valid.

2.4.6    Wheel Profile

Before wheel dressing, the wheel profile must be defined. Six types of wheel profile definitions are provided. The dressing cycle can only be executed after selecting the appropriate profile type.

General Parameters for Profile Definition:

Up to three wheel profiles can be defined simultaneously. During dressing, a profile will be executed if the Wheel Side set in the dressing parameters matches the Wheel Side defined in the profile parameters.

Example: If the dressing parameters specify a left-side wheel, and both Profile 1 and Profile 2 are set for the left-side wheel, Profile 1 will be dressed first, followed by Profile 2.

2.4.6.1    Profile Definition

In the Profile 1, 2, and 3 interfaces, define the profile number. Press the corresponding  key on the interface to enter the Profile Definition Parameters screen.

Follow the instructions on the profile definition screen to set the parameters. All values correspond to the dimensions indicated in the schematic diagram and are positive relative to the dressing origin. If a negative value is set, the dressing axis will move in the opposite direction.

The custom profile consists of 10 profile segments. Segment 1 is the starting point and is defined using absolute coordinates. Segments 2–10 are defined relative to the first segment. The feed rate for each segment is also specified.

Point (ABS): Set as absolute linear positioning, equivalent to G01 X Z. Point (INC): Set as incremental linear positioning, equivalent to G01 U W. Arc (CW): Clockwise circular arc.
Arc (CCW): Counterclockwise circular arc.
Chamfer (C): Defines the chamfer width of the profile.
Fillet (R): Defines the fillet radius of the profile (either chamfer or fillet can be selected, not both).

All X/Z coordinates for the segments are directional coordinates. The first segment defines the starting position, and the remaining segments define the end positions of each segment.

The presentation presents the features and improvements of the new X7 CNC machine by SYIL, emphasizing design, usability, and performance. ​

Design and Core Values

  • The new X7 embodies SYIL's values: Manufacturing Excellence, High Performance, and Continuous Innovation. ​
  • Distinctive design elements include an integrated signal light, unique column design, and a standout logo.

Improved Floorspace

  • New X7 dimensions: height 2180/2100 mm, width 1794 mm, and improved accessibility with larger doors and windows.
  • Integrated cabinets enhance space efficiency, with no protruding elements. ​

Usability Enhancements

  • Features a large 15" Siemens controller for better visibility and operability.
  • Ergonomic design includes round edges and bottom chamfer to prevent foot obstruction.
  • Two side-opening doors improve accessibility.

Signal Light and Chip Tray

  • Extra-high signal light tower with wide strip for enhanced visibility from all sides. ​

Hinged cover for chip tray allows easy access and integration of a chip conveyor.

Article subtitle: In this video, I walk you through managing tickets in HubSpot that result from form submissions on our website. Each submission generates a ticket assigned to the appropriate dealer based on the country, which you can find in your lead pipeline. For example, I show a ticket for a U.S. inquiry, and I explain how to follow up by accessing the contact record to send an email or make a phone call. Please make sure to check these tickets regularly and respond promptly to inquiries.
Article body:
Objective

This SOP outlines the steps for managing ticket submissions in HubSpot effectively, ensuring timely follow-ups and proper ticket status updates.

Key Steps

 

1. Accessing Ticket Submissions 0:00

  • Go to our website.

  • Navigate to the CRM tickets section.

  • Locate the lead pipeline to view form submissions as tickets.

 

2. Identifying Ticket Details 0:37

  • Review the ticket details for the specific submission.

  • Note the country associated with the ticket (e.g., U.S.).

 

3. Following Up on Tickets 1:08

  • Access the contact record linked to the ticket.

  • Initiate follow-up by sending an email or making a phone call.

 

4. Updating Ticket Status 1:29

  • After follow-up, update the ticket status:

    • Change to 'Waiting on Contact' if awaiting a response.

    • Change to 'Waiting on Us' if you are waiting to provide information.

    • Close the ticket once contact has been established.

Cautionary Notes

  • Ensure all follow-ups are documented in the ticket for future reference.

  • Do not close tickets without confirming that the issue has been resolved or the inquiry has been addressed.

Tips for Efficiency

  • Set reminders for follow-ups to avoid delays.

  • Use templates for common responses to save time when replying to inquiries.

Article subtitle: In this video, I explain how we categorize website visitors who fill out the request a quote form as qualified sales leads. These leads move directly to the deals section, reflecting their readiness to buy, rather than going through the leads or tickets pipeline. I also highlight that we typically receive essential information such as the person's first name, last name, and phone number, which aids in our follow-up process. It's crucial for our team to recognize this distinction in handling potential customers. Please ensure you familiarize yourself with this process to streamline our sales efforts.
Article body:
Objective

This SOP outlines the steps for processing qualified sales leads generated from the website's request for quote page.

Key Steps

 

1. Access the Request for Quote Page 0:00

  • Navigate to the detailed request for quote page on the website.

  • Ensure that the page is functioning correctly and is accessible to visitors.

 

2. Identify Qualified Sales Leads 0:32

  • When a visitor fills out the request for quote form and submits it, consider them a qualified sales lead.

  • These leads will be directed straight to the deals section in the CRM.

 

3. Review Deal Information 1:01

  • In the deals section, check the deal description to see what information the person is requesting.

  • Note that you will typically receive the first name, last name, and phone number of the lead.

 

4. Assess Estimated Deal Size 1:41

  • Based on the selection of the main machine in the request, HubSpot will automatically assign an estimated deal size to the deal.

 

5. Follow Up with the Lead 1:56

  • It is your responsibility to follow up with the lead promptly after reviewing their request.

Cautionary Notes

  • Ensure that all information is handled in compliance with data protection regulations.

  • Double-check the accuracy of the lead's contact information before reaching out.

Tips for Efficiency

  • Set reminders for follow-ups to ensure timely communication with leads.

  • Use templates for follow-up emails to save time while maintaining professionalism.

Column

Article title: General Overview of the SYIL N5
Article body:
SYIL N5 Two Spindle Two Turret Lathe

Equipment Features:

1.     Basic Structure

A versatile, high-productivity dual-spindle, dual-turret turning center. Both upper and lower turrets serve as milling power turrets, with the upper turret featuring a Y-axis for complex turning-milling operations, significantly boosting productivity. The dual-spindle configuration incorporates internal motors. Its low-center-of-gravity, 30-degree slant bed design and excellent thermal displacement performance meet heavy-load and high-precision machining demands.

The upper and lower turrets and sub-spindle utilize independent linear guideways. The non-shared guideway design between the lower turret and sub-spindle enhances sub-spindle rigidity. Furthermore, both turrets can machine the main spindle and sub-spindle, substantially increasing operational flexibility and efficiency.

2. Spindles

Both spindles are equipped with high-performance direct-drive synchronous electric spindles, enabling low-speed high-torque turning while also supporting high-speed precision cutting, thereby boosting production efficiency.

3. Y-Axis Composite Machining

The composite Y-axis structure design enables high-precision machining of various complex shapes.

4. Tool Turret

Servo motor control enables rapid and reliable tool selection. M and Y models feature the proprietary BMT power turret, supporting 7 MPa high-pressure coolant requirements to enhance high-speed, high-performance machining.

5. Control System

The SIEMENS CNC system optimizes cycle times, mechanism operation speeds, acceleration, and deceleration. It analyzes and minimizes non-cutting time during machining operations, thereby boosting productivity.

6. Options

This series of high-performance turning centers supports various optional equipment, including tool setters and feeders.

Article body:

The presentation presents the new X5 CNC machine design by SYIL, highlighting its features, improvements, and core values. ​

New X5 Design

  • The design reflects SYIL's core values: Manufacturing Excellence, High Performance, and Continuous Innovation.
  • The new X5 model was introduced on January 30, 2026.

Usability Improvements

  • Big side openings and windows enhance visibility and light inside the machine. ​
  • Higher doors improve accessibility and visibility. ​
  • Integrated cabinets eliminate protruding elements.
  • Ergonomic round handles and overall round edges enhance quality and ergonomics.
  • Bottom chamfer prevents foot obstruction when standing close to the machine.
  • A large 12" Siemens controller improves visibility and operability. ​

New Distinctive Design Elements I

  • Integrated signal light features the SYIL logo.
  • Unique column design enhances aesthetics.
  • The Siemens controller panel is outstanding.
  • A yellow "Signature" belt with the X5 logo adds branding.
  • The bottom area is completely housed for a clean look.

New Distinctive Design Elements II Signal Light Tower

  • Features an extra-high tower with a wide light strip for visibility. ​
  • The signal light strip is visible from all sides.
  • Large offset enhances the tower's distinct appearance.

Stand Out Logo

  • The logo is designed for a more premium perception of the brand name.

SYIL R1 Development Guide Document

This document explains the contents of the SYIL R1 Development Guide in terms of safety interface, electrical interface, pneumatic interface, Signals interface, SYIL user interface functions and robot sequence.

Safety Interface

The safety of the robot needs to be linked with the safety of the CNC. On this product, we will use two different safety features: Access Doors and Emergency Stop

We are planning to use two different modes with the robot: T1 and EXT.

T1: Teach mode à It’s possible to jog and test the robot program at slow speed with the cell door opened.

EXT: External mode à It’s possible to control the robot and run program from the Siemens controller at full speed if the safety is acknowledged.

Access Doors

The CNC is normally equipped with a dual channel safety switch on the main operator door. For the actual project, we will add two new doors. It’s important to safely control the side loading door (2).

Here are the 3 access doors:

  1. CNC main front door for the operator access
  2. Side Auto-Door for the robot access.
  3. Robot cell access to change and manipulate the parts

 

Emergency Stop

The CNC is normally equipped with dual channel emergency stop on the controller. For the actual project, the robot will need to know if the SYIL E-Stop is pressed.

Wiring

We will need to exchange some signal between the R1 and the CNC. The R1 needs to know when it’s ok to let the robot move. By example, if the operator door is open, Safety Door Ch. A-B circuits must be opened or if the Side loading door is open, CNC must not start machining.

You will see below an example of wiring.

2.2    Safe device warning message

The relevant safely devices cannot guarantee absolute safety in the event of accidents and dangerous situations. Be sure to observe the relevant precautions when using this machine tool.

2.2.1    Installation location of safely device

The installation location of the safely device is shown in Fig.3 .

 

Fig.3 Position diagram of machine safety device

2.2.2    Functional description of the safely device

1）Door switch (opt.)
The machine tool will not be able to operate in automatic mode as long as the door is not fully closed. When the machine is in the automatic mode, the machine tool will switch to the feed hold state if the door is opened. 
In the manual mode, even if the door is not closed, the switches about spindle collet clamping, spindle rotating and cutting oil, can still be operated in order to facilitate parts’ adjusting and cutting.

2）Main circuit breaker

If excessive current is detected in the machine tool , the power supply will be cut off automati-cally. 

3）Emergency stop button 
There is a red emergency stop button on the machine tool operation. When there is an emer-gency such as fire, earthquake or lightning and emergency refuge is necessary, press this but-ton before leaving the machine tool to stop the machine tool.

Pressing the emergency stop button during operation of the machine tool will not only damage the machined parts and tools, but also damage the machine tool. 

To release the emergency stop state, you must confirm that it is safe, and then rotate the emer-gency stop button clockwise.

2.2.3    Precautions before operation

1)    Before starting the machine tool, the operator must master the following
•    Location of the emergency stop button
•    The contents of all warning signs
•    The way to stop the machine tool in an emergency
•    The function, operation method and operation sequence of the switches and buttons on the operation panel
•    The correct order of start and end 
•    The method of handing when an abnormal situation occurs
•    Cutting off method of main Circuit Breaker of Machine tool 
2)    When the operator is harmful to personal safely and the safe operation of the machine tool , such as drinking , excessive fatigue and poor health , please do not operate the machine tool .
3)    Operators should wear appropriate overalls , hats and safety shoes , gloves , rings , ties , necklaces and other dangerous items that may be involved in the machine tool . please remove them in advance .  
4)    To prevent slipping , falling or tripping around the machine tool , keep the machine tool clean and tidy .
5)    Fire-prone objects should not be placed around the machine tool . 
6)    Please do not run the machine tool when the safety device does not work .
7)    Please make sure that the emergency stop button is function properly .
8)    Do not modify the machine tool and control circuit privately , otherwise it may cause personal injury or damage to the machine tool .
9)    Please use a lubricating , non-corrosive and non-flammable cutting fluid .
10)    Please make sure that the tools and fixtures are installed correctly before the machine tool is running .
11)    Before running the machine tool , please make sure that the amount of coolant is suffi-cient and the cutting part is fully cooled . Regular removal of chips in cutting parts and chip collection devices .
12)    It is forbidden to remove the shield of the machine tool to run the machine tool !
13)    It is prohibited to process flammable , explosive and dusty materials !

2.2.4    Matters needing attention during operation

1)    Please do not open the electric box protection door when the main circuit breaker is in “ON” .
2)    During the operation of  the machine tool , please do not touch or approach the cutting tool and the moving parts of the machine tool .
3)    Please confirm carefully before pressing the relevant operation button.

2.2.5    Matters needing attention for shutting down machine tools

Order in which machine tools are turned off :
1.    Reset and stop machine tool operation
2.    Press the emergency stop button
3.    Cut off  the power of  NC
4.    Cut off  the main circuit breaker

2.2.6    Measures to deal with emergencies 

1)    Measures to be taken in case of emergency such as fire, earthquake or thunder
•    Have plenty of  time
1.    Stop the machine tool from running 
2.    Cut off  the power of  NC
3.    Cut off  the main circuit breaker
•    Time is tight
1.    Press the emergency stop button
2.    Cut off the main circuit breaker

2)    Sudden power outage 
•    Treatment after sudden power outage:
1.    Press the emergency stop button
2.    Cut off the main circuit breaker

3)    Steps to resume machine tool operation after an emergency
1.    Power on the machine tool and restart the machine tool
2.    Check the damage of the tool
3.    Replace the broken toll
4.    Cut off or take out parts that were not finished during a power outage 

2.2.7    Matters needing attention in storage and transportation of machine tools 

1)    The machine tool is packed with rainproof, and coated with antirust oil on the key parts. The packaging box adopts certain anti-vibration and anti-shock measures to ensure safe transportation and storage in the temperature range of -25℃~55℃. However, the pack-aging box must not be allowed to be turned upside down or tilted through 15℃, and no violent impact or vibration is allowed to avoid damage to the internal devices.
2)    When the machine tool is not in operation for a long time, it is necessary to protect the machine tool with anti-rust oil and remove the power inlet; cover the machine with a film sleeve to prevent dust; block the power inlet hole in the electrical niche of the machine base to prevent rodent damage.

The machine tool is a CNC lathe controlled by a 64-bit microprocessor. The CNC axis is a 4 linkage control. It is a machine, electric, and gas-body product. It can automatically complete the turning of outer circles, end faces, milling flats, side drilling, processing of grooving, thread-ing, drilling, tapping, boring, internal threading, etc.

The machine tool spindle adopts a built-in spindle motor structure (electric spindle), which elim-inates the vibration instability caused by traditional belt transmission. The maximum main spin-dle speed can reach 8000 rpm. The main spindle bearing adopts Japan NSK high-precision main axial thrust ball bearing, which ensures the high rotation accuracy, high rigidity and the ability to maintain accuracy of the main spindle.

The linear axis motion pair of this machine tool adopts imported high-speed, high-precision lin-ear guideway and ball screw. It has low friction, high sensitivity and high accuracy stability. It can reach the fast feed speed of 24 m/min while meeting the μ-level precise feed accuracy, fully meets the needs of high-speed machining.

This machine tool standard with 5 side milling live tool, 7 external cutting tools, 4 cross-section drilling tools and 8 back drilling tools to meet the needs of different processing procedures.
This machine tool can be configured with automatic feeder, to realize the continuous feeding of the bar and taking the bar end, so as to realize the fully automatic continuous processing of the machine tool.
The machine tool can be widely used in high-precision, high-speed and efficient mass production of shaft parts in instruments, meters, light industry, electronics, medical equipment and other industries.

Fig.12 General layout diagram of machine tool

Base: Mainly used to support various components.

Column: X-axis pallet, Y-axis pallet and gang tool system are installed on the upright. The ma-chine tool realizes the tool changing action through the movement of the Y-axis pallet. The ma-chine tool realizes the radial feed motion of the tool through the up and down movement of the X axis.

Spindle: The spindle motor is a built-in motor (electric spindle), which is driven by frequency conversion and stepless speed regulation. The spindle box is equipped with a spindle speed detection encoder. The machine tool drives the spindle forward and backward through the Z-axis screw to realize the axial feed movement of the tool.

Pneumatic system: The pneumatic system is located under the back of the machine   tool. The machine tool controls the clamping/relaxing action of the spindle and the telescopic action of the cylinder through the pneumatic system.

Lubrication system: The lubrication system is located under the back of the machine tool. The machine tool provides lubrication to the ball screw and linear guideway through the lubrication system to ensure the long-term stable operation of the machine tool.
The coolant tank is under the base on the right side of the machine, and can be pulled out to the right to facilitate the cleaning of the coolant tank.

The main control electrical part of the machine tool is installed in the alcove at the lower left of the base. The left side of the base is provided with an electric box protection door. The door is provided with a power switch and an electric box ventilation device.

The control panel is located on the rocker arm on the front of the machine tool, and can be pulled away when the machine tool is debugged, which is convenient for the workers to oper-ate. The NC panel is equipped with two USB2.0 sockets, which can be used for data transmis-sion of the machine tool. A hand-held manual pulse generator is also configured on the side of the control panel.

The machine tool protection adopts a fully enclosed protective cover, a flip-up door is provided on the right side, and a tempered glass observation window is provided on the door, which is convenient for observing the operation of the machine tool during processing. After the door is opened, it is the main cutting area of the machine tool. Tool setting and coolant flow adjustment operations; there is a flip door on the left side. After the door is opened, it is the spindle area of the machine tool, which can modulate the clamping force of the spindle and guide sleeve.

6.1    Main spindle & Sub-spindle

The main spindle and sub-spindle of the machine tool are built-in electric spindle structures. In order to ensure the thermal stability of the main spindle, the main spindle box is cooled by means of circulating oil cooling. It is recommended to use Great Wall 7# spindle oil (or Mobil 4# spindle oil) as the spindle cooling oil.
Because the front end of the main spindle is protected by an air curtain seal, it is normal for the air flow sound at the front end of the main spindle. Adjust the gas pressure of the air curtain seal between 0.2~0.4 MPa.

Fig.13 Schematic diagram of spindle

6.2    Feed system

The linear axis of this machine tool has five linear axes: X1, Y1, Z1, X2, Z2

The rotation axes of this machine tool include S1 (spindle), S2 (sub-spindle), S3 (side live tool axis), and S5 (back live tool axis). And S1 (spindle) and S2 (sub-spindle) have C-axis function.

This machine tool system is a dual-channel control system. X1, Y1, Z1, S1 (spindle), S3 (side live tool axis) belong to the first channel. X2, Z2, S2 (sub-spindle), and S5 (*back driven tool axis) be-long to the second channel.

 

Fig.14  Diagram of the distribution of machine tool S205/S265

 

 

Fig.15  Diagram of the distribution of machine tool S206/S266

6.3    Coolant system

The cooling box is installed under the right base of the machine tool and can be pulled out to the right to facilitate the cleaning of the cooling box. When machining, it is necessary to select the appropriate cutting oil according to the material of the workpiece to be machined.
•     Water-soluble cutting fluids are not recommended.
•     Do not use cutting oil with high volatility and low ignition point.

Fig.16 Diagram of cooling system

6.4    Pneumatic system

The pneumatic system is installed in the pneumatic box at the right rear of the machine tool.

The main air source processing element adjusts the pressure to 0.5 MPa, the main air source should be dry and stable.

The air-tight air source processing element adjusts the pressure to between 0.08~0.1 MPa.

6.5    Lubrication system

The lead screw and guide rail of each axis of the machine tool are lubricated by a centralized lubrication system. The machine tool lubrication pump is installed on the back of the machine tool and on the base niche. Lubricant ISO VG 68 guide oil is recommended. The system can set the oiling time and oiling interval of lubricating oil. The lubricating oil setting recommends oiling once every 30 minutes for 5 seconds each time (new machine tools can appropriately extend the oiling time).

Lubricating oil pump filling time parameter:  3429 (setting unit: seconds)

Lubricating oil pump oil filling interval parameter: 3430 (setting unit: minutes) There is a lubricat-ing oil quantity detection switch on the lubricating oil pump. When the lubricating oil quantity is too low, the machine tool will alarm.

Article subtitle: S205/S265 SWISS-TYPE CNC LATHE S206/S266 SWISS-TYPE CNC LATHE (For SYNTEC systems) Operation Manual 2026
Article body:
This manual is only the operating instructions of this machine tool, for instruction on the use of other parts, please refer to the following technical documents provided at random.

  • SYNTEC controller specification
  • SYNTEC programming specification

Before using the machine tool, must fully grasp the contents of this manual and other instructions provided at random, to use the machine tool safely and correctly.

Operators must undergo adequate training in the safe use, adjustment and operation of machine tools before they can use machine tools.

5.1    Machine Removal

After opening the outer packaging box of the machine tool, firstly remove the random tools, cooling boxes and other accessories on the bottom plate of the packaging box, and then re-move the four fastening nuts at the connection between the machine tool and the bottom plate.

5.2    Machine hoisting, positioning

5.2.1    Machine hoisting

1)    Two Φ45mm diameter steel rods (made of high-quality low-carbon steel No. 20, one is 2 m long, the other is 1.5 m long, with a safety factor greater than 4) penetrate into the holes of 2 sets of M20 rings, as shown in Fig.4 The hook is used to hook the hoisting ca-ble on the steel rod (the safety factor of the hoisting cable is greater than 5, the hoisting cable should not touch the parts of the machine tool, and if necessary, use a wooden block to firmly and reliably open the hoisting cable and the machine tool parts Or use a special hanger).

Fig.4 Machine hoisting

2)    Raise the lifting cable gradually, check the lifting cable and the center of gravity of the machine tool to ensure safety

3)    When the machine is transported to the installation site and the machine is still in the air, screw the six leveling screws and lock nuts provided together, and screw the level-ing screws from the foot installation cavity into the six foot screw holes on the base In-side, make the ball protrude from the bottom surface of the base.

4)

Fig.5  Installation of machine tool foot screws

5)    Place the six supplied foot pads correctly in the machine tool placement position as shown in Fig.6.

Fig.6 Machine installation

6)    Let the machine tool down lower gradually and adjust the position to align the six blocks with six leveling screws. so that the six leveling screws are aligned with the six pads.
7)    Place the machine tool steadily on the six foot pads and adjust the six leveling screws so that the distance between the bottom surface of the machine tool base foot screw and the ground is 35mm.

Please observe the following precautions when lifting the machine, otherwise it may cause the machine to fall (damage) and cause serious personal injury.
1)    Hoisting personnel must have nationally recognized qualification certificates
2)    Prohibited rolling
3)    The non-slip mat (rubber or cloth) must be added to the part where the lifting rod and the lifting cable contact.
4)    Ensure that the lifting cable can withstand the weight of the machine tool (bout 3500kg) 
5)    During the hoisting process, the machine tool should not be inclined, and try to avoid impact and vibration.

5.2.2    Machine lifting

Fig.7 Forklift

Please observe the following precautions when lifting the machine, otherwise it may cause the machine to fall (damage) and cause serious personal injury.
1)    Lifting personnel must have nationally recognized qualification certificates
2)    Forklift tonnage requirement:  ≥5T
3)    During the lifting process, the machine tool should not be inclined, and try to avoid impact and vibration.

5.3    Machine installation

5.3.1    Machine foundation requirements

1)    The load bearing capacity of the foundation of the installed machine tool is not less than 3000kg/m2, and the thickness of the foundation is not less than 150mm.
2)    The foundation must extend more than 500mm from the periphery of the machine tool.
3)    The machine tool should be installed on a solid, level ground, and should not be af-fected by the vibration of other machines.
4)    When the machine tool is installed on the floor, the structural strength and vibra-tion frequency of the floor should be fully evaluated, and it should be approved by the plant design unit or the authority of the authority.
5)    The installation position of the machine tool should have enough operation and maintenance space.

5.3.2    Usage environment of machine tool

1)    Ambient temperature: 0℃～45℃ during operation; -20℃～55℃ during non-operation; temperature change≤20℃/hour.
2)    Relative humidity: usually 10% to 75% (without condensation), short-term (within a month) 5% to 95% (without condensation).
3)    ≤0.5G during operation and ≤1G during non-operation.
4)    The place where chips, water and oil cannot splash.
5)    Stay away from electric welding and other discharge machining machinery
6)    Keep away from strong electromagnetic interference
7)    Avoid direct sunlight

5.3.3    Machine cooling connection

1)    Push the cooling box under the machine tool from the right side of the machine tool to align it with the sheet metal outside the machine tool.
2)    Put the Chip collection box into the Cooling box and align it with the outlet of the machine tool.
3)    Cover the chip collection box cover.
4)    Connect the cooling pump to the machine tool with hose. Tighten the joint with a throat hoop.
5)    Power on the cooling pump
6)    Plug in the liquid level switch 
7)    Start-up cooling pump, observe the rotation direction of the cooling pump, if the ro-tation direction of the cooling pump is opposite to the direction marked on the pump body, the power phase sequence of the cooling pump needs to be changed, in order to adjust the rotation direction of the cooling pump.
8)    Add matching coolant according to the processed material. Cooling tank volume about 200L.

 

Fig.8 Cooling diagram

5.3.4    Machine tool lubricants

The volume of the lubricating pump oil tank is 2L, and the effective volume is 1.5L. The grade of lubricating oil is: ISO VG-68. It is necessary to add 1.5L of lubricating oil to the lubricating pump for the first time, and the machine tool needs to be replenished in time after a period of operation.

The lubricating oil must be clean, otherwise it will damage the machine guideway and screw.

5.3.5    Machine tool air source requirements

1)    Machine tool air source connected to air pipe：Φ8mm
2)    Machine tool air source requirements: air pressure 0.5MPa, air volume 80Nl/min
3)    Please keep the air source dry and clean. Drain the residual water in the air compressor in time, and add a first-level filtering device to the air compressor if necessary.

5.3.6    Machine tool power supply requirements

1)    power supply & voltage: 3phase 380V±10% 50Hz±2%
2)    Power: 15kVA 

The machine tool ground must be firm and reliable, the neutral line of power supply cannot be used as a protective ground wire！

 

Fig.9 Schematic diagram of external interface of machine tool

5.3.7    Spindle cooling oil

Recommended grade of spindle cooling oil: Mobil 4
The machine tool spindle is cooled by liquid internal circulation, when the machine tool leaves the factory, an appropriate amount of spindle cooling oil has been added. The phenomenon of spindle cooling oil loss may occur in the process of machine tool operation. When using the machine tool for the first time, it is necessary to ensure sufficient cooling oil for the spindle.
There is no loss of cooling oil of the spindle during the normal use of the machine tool. If there is abnormal loss of cooling oil in the spindle, please check whether the cooling oil circuit is dam-aged, necessary times manufacturer maintenance.

Please refer to the relevant operating instructions for the use and maintenance of the oil cooling machine.
Please clean the external filter of the oil cooling machine.

Fig.10 Schematic diagram of filter cleaning

5.3.8    Machine tool adjustment level

1)    Move the spindle box to the position of the Z1 axis negative limit.
2)    Cross the horizontal adjustment plat over the two rails of the Z1 axis.
3)    Put the bar horizontal ruler on the horizontal adjustment board.
4)    Adjust the machine too anchor screw, make the reading of the horizontal ruler with-in 0.04mm/m.
5)    Tighten the locking nut of the anchor screw.

Fig.11  Mounting location for leveling instrument

7.6.6    High pressure cooling control 

This machine tool can be equipped with a high-pressure cooling device, which can effectively remove the chips wrapped around the tool by configuring the high-pressure cooling device. The high-pressure cooling device draws cutting oil from the cooling oil tank. When using a high-pressure cooling device, the liquid level in the cooling tank will be lower than usual. At this time, if the cooling oil tank is filled with oil, when the cooling stops, it may cause too much oil in the cooling oil tank, causing the cooling oil to overflow the cooling oil tank. When using a high-pressure cooling device, check the amount of oil in the cooling oil tank and maintain an appro-priate amount of oil. The high-pressure cooling device has 4 sets of cooling oil circuits. When more than 2 oil circuits are opened at the same time, the oil pressure sprayed from the nozzle will be lost.


•     instruction format
M104        High pressure 1 on
M105        High pressure 1 Off
M106        High pressure 2 on
M107        High pressure 2 Off
M108        High pressure 3 on
M109        High pressure 3 Off
M110        High pressure 4 on
M111        High pressure 4 Off

7.6.7    Ejection control (M17, M18)

The extension and retraction of the ejector rod of this machine tool are controlled by the air valve.
When the machine tool is in the manual state, the extension and retraction of the ejector rod can be controlled through the material receiving button on the operation panel; when the ma-chine tool is in the automatic processing state, the corresponding M code is executed to control the extension and retraction of the ejector rod.

•    instruction format
M17      ejector rod extended
M18      ejector rod back

1.    When the sub-spindle chuck is in the clamped state or the sub-spindle is running, if the ejector rod extension (M17) is executed, an alarm will be issued.
2.    When the ejector rod is in the extended position, the sub-spindle clamping action (M20) shall not be performed, otherwise an alarm will be issued.
3.    The ejector cylinder is equipped with a detection switch for reaching out position. If the ejector rod extension (M17) action is executed, the detection switch will not detect the relevant signal, and an alarm will be issued.

Command format

1.    Depending on the shape of the parts, there are cases where the parts cannot be dis-charged.
2.    Execute the M26 command, the parts conveyor will automatically stop after rotating for about 15 seconds. There is no need to stop the conveyor with the M27 command.
3.    The running time of the parts conveyor can be adjusted by modifying the value of pa-rameter 3432.

7.6.9    Sub-spindle are blow control (M28, M29)

Chips remaining on the sub-spindle chuck can be cleaned by the sub-spindle blowing function.

•     Command format
M28      Sub-spindle blowing on
M29      Sub-spindle blow off

1.    There is a gas throttle valve on the air blowing line of the sub-spindle, which will affect the air volume and air pressure to a certain extent, and affect the cleaning of the resid-ual chips on the sub-spindle chuck.
2.    Do not cancel the air blowing throttle valve directly, otherwise the system pressure will drop rapidly when the sub-spindle air blowing is opened, which will affect the normal use of the machine tool. If it is necessary to increase the air blowing volume, cancel the gas throttle valve, and need to connect the air source separately from the outside for air blowing of the sub-spindle.
3.    Performing the ejector extension (M17) and retraction (M18) actions at the same time as the sub-spindle blowing can improve the cleaning effect of the remaining chips on the sub-spindle chuck.
4.    The sub-spindle rotates at a low speed while blowing air on the sub-spindle, which can improve the cleaning effect of the remaining chips on the chuck of the sub-spindle.

7.6.13    Automatic cut off (G266 A* X* S* F* )

In the process of machining parts, it is necessary to stop the operation of the machine tool when encountering abnormal conditions (such as: end of tool life, tool breakage, machine tool abnormality, etc.). After eliminating the abnormal situation of the machine tool, it is necessary to perform cutting head processing before starting the machine tool processing again. The au-tomatic cutting head can be processed by executing the G266 command.

    G266  A* X* S* F*  

    A:Quick positioning position - bar diameter value mm

    X:cutting feed position - cutting diameter mm

    S:Parts cutting speed

    F:Feed rate per revolution

    WAIT();               

    IF #1 =#0 THEN

    ALARM(100,"G266 A* DATA ERROR");

    END_IF;

    IF #19 =#0 THEN

    END_IF;

    IF #24 =#0 THEN

    ALARM(103,"G266 X* DATA ERROR");   

    END_IF;

    WAIT(); 

    N000;

    IF(#1036=1) THEN              

    GOTO100;

    ELSE;

    T0101;                                

    END_IF; 

    N100;

    IF (@10721<=#24*1000) THEN     

    IF (@10722=0.0) THEN         

    GOTO 999;

    END_IF;

    END_IF;

    N800;

    M10;

    M08;

    G28 U0.0;                      

    G00 Y0.0;                      

    M03 S#19;                      

    G00 X(#1+2.0);                

    G99 G01 X#24 F#9;             

    M05;

    M09;

    N999;

    M99;

    $2

    M99;

1)    The default T01 tool is the cutting tool. When the T01 tool is not used for cutting, do not execute the command, otherwise there will be a risk of collision.
2)    Before executing the command, the tool No. T01 should be moved to a relatively safe po-sition above the part.

Make the speed and phase of the main and sub-spindles consistent. In this state, the machine tool can complete the processing in the following situations:

1.    The workpiece clamped by the main spindle is converted to the action of the sub-spindle.
2.    The main spindle and the sub-spindle clamp a part for processing at the same time.
3.    The phases of the main spindle and the sub-spindle are consistent, and the processing of special-shaped parts is carried out.

G200  S□□□□     The main spindle and the sub-spindle rotate
synchronously at the speed of S□□□□

7.6.15    Double Z-axis linkage function (M1000, M1001)

The Z2 axis is linkage with the Z1 axis, and the Z2 axis follows the Z1 axis for synchronous opera-tion. In this state, the machine tool can complete the processing in the following situations:

1.    The main spindle and the sub-spindle clamp a part at the same time for external turn-ing.
2.    The main spindle and the sub-spindle clamp a part at the same time for side milling.
3.    The main spindle and the sub-spindle clamp a part at the same time for turning the ex-ternal thread.

  • Command format

M1000     Start the linkage function of Z1 axis and Z2 axis

M1001     Cancel the linkage function of Z1 axis and Z2 axis

7.6.17    Sub-spindle workpiece receiving failure detection (G201)

This command is executed when the cutting tool is detected for cutting. The sub-spindle picks up the workpiece, and after the cutting is completed, cancel the dual-spindle synchronization function, execute the G201 command, and judge whether the cutting tool is broken by detecting the rotation of the sub-spindle.


•     Command format
  G201      Detection of poor work piece access on the back side     

•     Programming example

When the material on the front side and the workpiece clamped on the back side are being sep-arated, for some reasons, although the cutting tool has been broken, the G201 command can-not effectively detect the breakage of the cutting tool. For example, when the cutting tool is damaged, only a small amount is left uncut. After executing the G201 command, the part will be twisted and broken, causing the system to mistakenly believe that the cutting tool is not dam-aged.

The torque of Z1 axis and Z2 axis is limited. When the load of Z1 axis or Z2 axis exceeds the limit value, the machine tool will alarm to achieve the purpose of protecting the machine tool.

•     Programming example

1.    This function can be turned on when the main and sub-spindles are drilling. When the drill bit is damaged, the load of the Z1 Z2 motor will increase instantly, triggering an alarm, reminding the customer to replace the drill bit in time to avoid subse-quent tool damage.
2.    This function can be turned on before the synchronous docking of the sub-spindle. When the workpiece on the spindle side has serious chip wrapping or there are re-sidual parts in the chuck of the sub-spindle, the sub-spindle cannot complete the normal docking task, and the Z1/Z2 axis The load of the motor will increase instant-ly, triggering an alarm, reminding the customer to check and improve the working condition of the synchronous docking of the sub-spindle in time.
3.    This function can be turned on before the synchronous docking of the sub-spindle (special-shaped material). When the synchronous phase of the sub-spindle and the main-spindle deviates, the sub-spindle cannot complete the normal docking, and the load of the Z1/Z2 axis motor will increase instantly, triggering an alarm, Remind the customer to correct the synchronization phase deviation between the sub-spindle and the main spindle.
4.    This function can be turned on after the main spindle/sub-spindle synchronous cut-ting is completed. When the cutting tool is damaged, the workpiece is not cut nor-mally, and the sub-spindle retreats, the load of the Z1/Z2 axis motor will increase instantaneously, triggering an alarm, reminding the customer in time Replace bro-ken cutting tools.

7.6.19    Machine tool control (T command)

The tool change action of this machine tool is completed by the system control servo axis. The user uses the method of T code tool change command to designate the required tool number in the preparation of the machining program.

•     Command format
T  □□△△
□□：Tool number

  •     Arrangement of cutters （T01～T09）

  •     Side powered tool（T11～T19）

  •     End face cutter （T21～T29）

  •     Back cutter （T31～T39） 

△△：Tool nose and wear compensation number

Tool positioning is performed with a T-coded 4-digit command. The first 2 digits correspond to the tool number, and the last 2 digits are the compensation number. If T0000 is executed, it rep-resents the compensation cancellation state. The X, Y, Z coordinate values corresponding to □□ (tool number) are recorded in the system tool length value.

1.    The usual tool selections are all run at rapid feed.
2.    Please specify T code in a separate block.
3.    The T code (T □□△△) cannot be the same block as the M code and S code commands.
4.    Non-professionals are not allowed to change the tool length value in the system, and a backup must be made before changing to avoid data loss.

7.8    The method of machine shutdown

1)    Machine tool shutdown during normal processing
2)    When part processing is in the process of automatic program running, should press "program stop" on the operation panel to make M01 effective (M01 is programmed in the program), when the program stops at M01, press the button "RESET" , the machine tool stop running.
3)    Machine tool shutdown after off work
1.     according to the first method to let the machine tool in shutdown state
2.    press the red "OFF" button on the operation panel, confirm that the display showing is end, and the indicator light on the operation panel is off
3.     press the main circuit breaker, let it at the position “OFF”.
4)    Emergency shutdown
1.    Press the emergency stop button on the operation panel
2.     press the red “OFF” button on the operation panel
3.     press the main circuit breaker, let it at the position “OFF”.

Do not press the emergency stop button if there is no emergency during the machining process. Because press the emergency stop button, all machine action will be forcibly interrupted, will not only damage the processed parts, but also damage the tool and even the machine tool.

1)    Turn on the air source ，confirm that the air pressure gauge reading of the machine tool air system is 0.5MPa±10%.
2)    Confirm that the lubricating oil in the lubrication station exceeds the min. required scale.
3)    If coolant liquid is necessary, confirm that the coolant liquid in the cooling box exceeds the minimum required scale.
4)    Check with the factory power supply voltage, confirm that the power supply meets the requirements, press the factory power circuit breaker.
5)    Press the factory power circuit breaker, let it at the position “ON”.
6)    Press the button "ON" on the system operation panel, CNC system start.
7)    Reset (turn right) the emergency stop button on the operation panel
8)    If need to use coolant liquid, please confirm whether the cooling system can work nor-mally or not: press the "Coolant" button to turn on the coolant, and press the "Coolant" button again to turn off the coolant.

Adjustment steps of clamping force:

1.    Loosen the fastening screw on the side of the lock nut. Rotate the locking nut at the back of the spindle counterclockwise so that the spindle is not clamped.
2.    Load the cone sleeve.
3.    Load the spring.
4.    Load the spring chuck.
5.    Install the spindle nut and lock it.
6.    Load the bar into the spindle and protrude the end face of the spring chuck.
7.    Clamp the spring chuck.
8.    Rotate the locking nut at the back of  the spindle clockwise until the spring chuck is just enough to clamp the bar.
9.    Loosen the spring chuck
10.    Continue to rotate the locking nut at the back end of the spindle clockwise for about 1/4 turns.
11.    Clamp the spring chuck again, check whether the clamping force is appropriate. Fine-tune the locking nut at the back end of the spindle until the spring chuck gets the ap-propriate clamping force.
12.    
13.    Tighten the fastening screw on the side of the locking nut.
14.    Confirm the position of the claw on the siding sleeve when clamping, and adjust the relative position of the claw on the sliding sleeve by clamping the connecting rod on the cylinder. 
15.    Lock the connecting rod with the nut on the cylinder.

7.11    Installation and Clamping Force adjustment of guide bushing 

1)    Use special hexagonal wrench to confirm that the locking screw on the left edge of the  locking screw has been relaxed.
2)    Cleaning the guide bushing  mounting hole and guide bushing , and add lubricating oil.
3)    Put the guide bushing  into the guide bushing, and the slot on the guide bushing  needs to correspond to the phase of the pin in the guide bushing.
4)    Put the bar into the guide bushing and extend the end face of the guide bushing . Use special wrench to rotate the guide bushing  to locking nut, tighten the guide bushing  gradually
5)    When tightened the guide bushing , the bar shall not be bitten to death, the bar can be pulled by hand flexibly (otherwise the  will be damaged). At the same time, there is no obvious gap between the bar and the guide bushing  (otherwise the cutting ef-fect of the part will be poor).
6)    After adjusting the clamping force of the guide bushing properly, use special hexa-gon wrench to locking the screw. And check the clamping force of the guide bushing  again. If the clamping force is not suitable, please repeat the above steps.

11. Install the spindle protective cover for non-guide bush mode.

Predict machine failure or early discovering, and controlling their losses to the production to a minimum, it is necessary to check the machine tools regularly regardless of whether there are failures. This chapter summarizes and explains the necessary inspection items starting from the daily inspection to once every 6 months.

8.1    Daily maintenance

The daily inspection is mainly a simple inspection that should be carried out before and during the operation of the machine tool every day. Please check the main points as shown below. For this reason, the state of the machine tool during normal operation should be grasped at ordinary times. This is the most effective daily inspection.

8.2    Common failures and solutions

This chapter will introduce the handing methods of common faults. The treatment method of fault belongs to the common range, faults other than the setting may occur in the actual opera-tion. When the cause of the failure can not be identified or can not be handled, please contact Machinery customer service center for maintenance.

8.2.1    Related alarm of spindle and sub spindle chuck  

When the spindle chuck can not be opened, there will be a phenomenon that the machined parts are short or the processed bars can not be discharged.
•    Step to deal with:
1.    Check whether the gas source is normal.
2.    Check whether the clamping solenoid valve is working properly.
3.    Check whether the clamping cylinder is working properly.
4.    Check whether clamping induction switch is normal, loose or damaged.
5.    Check whether the clamping cylinder connecting rod is loose.
6.    Check whether the front and rear stroke of the claw is normal.
7.    Disassemble the spindle nut, clean the chuck and taper sleeve, clean the inner hole of the spindle。
8.    Check whether the taper sleeve has any strain, check whether the taper sleeve and the inner hole of the spindle are killed.
9.    Replace a new chuck.

After confirming the above items, the problem has not been solved, please contact Machinery customer service canter for maintenance.

8.2.2    Low cooling flow rate 

When the machine tool uses cutting oil, there is a risk of fire when the work piece is not cooled enough. When the machine tool is in short supply of cooling oil, it should be dealt with in time.

•    Step to deal with：
1.    Check whether the cooling line is loose and fall off.
2.    Check whether the cooling pump is working properly.
3.    Check whether the cooler has enough oil.
4.    Clean the chip contact cavity.
5.    Clean the filter of the cooler.

8.2.3    Overheating alarm of spindle and sub spindle 

The spindle and sub spindle of this machine tool adopt the structure of built-in motorized spin-dle. A temperature sensor is preset in the spindle. Alarm will be given when the spindle is oper-ating abnormally and the temperature is too high.

•    Step to deal with：
1.    Check the I/O module of the machine tool. 
The input point ‘I16’ is the overheating detection of spindle;
The input point ‘I23’ is the overheating detection of sub spindle,
Damage to the input module will trigger this kind of alarm.
If the I/O module of the machine tool is damaged, please contact Machinery customer service center for repair.
2.    Check whether the spindle oil cooler is working properly.
3.    If the spindle is really too hoot and whether there is a scorched smell. The spindle coil may have been damaged. Please contact Machinery customer service center for repair.
4.    If the speed of the spindle is abnormal. Maybe the spindle coil or the encoder is damaged.  Please contact Machinery customer service center for repair.
5.    If the spindle load fluctuates abnormally under no load. The spindle coil may have been damaged. Please contact Machinery customer service center for repair.
6.    If the three resistance of the spindle coil is unbalanced. Maybe the spindle coil is damaged. Please contact Machinery customer service center for repair.
7.    If the earth resistance of the spindle coil is not infinite. Maybe the spindle coil is damaged. Please contact Machinery customer service center for repair.
8.     Check if the spindle power cable is damaged or loose.
9.    Inspect the spindle encoder cable for damage or loose.
10.    Inspect the spindle drive for damage. 

8.2.4    Abnormal alarm of ejector

The material ejector device is arranged in the sub spindle. For the parts whose length is less than 80 mm, the material can be ejected from the front end of the sub spindle through the ma-terial ejector device.
If the parts in the sub spindle are not ejected in time, in the subsequent processing, the parts in the sub spindle will interfere with other parts of the machine tool or subsequent parts.
For the structure and adjustment of the jacking device, please refer to: 6.16 Adjustment of the bar pusher device.

When performing the jacking action, if the machine tool does not receive the signal of the jack-ing sensor switch, it will issue a corresponding alarm.
•    Step to deal with:
1.    Check whether the gas source is normal.
2.    Check whether the solenoid valve is working properly.
3.    Check the trachea for damage.
4.    Check whether the cylinder throttle valve is adjusted properly.
5.    Check whether the cylinder action is stuttered.
6.    Inspect the cylinder induction switch for loosening or damage.
7.    Check whether the ejector rod is bent and whether is works smoothly.
8.    Check whether there are any residual work pieces or material heads in the sub spindle and clean them up in time.

By reasonably controlling the torque output of each shaft, the occurrence of similar situation can be avoided to a certain extent.

8.2.6    Lost position command alarm

•     Alarm description
The controller checks at any time whether the error between the feedback instruction and the output instruction is within the predetermined error range after the controller stops outputting a certain axial instruction for 1 second. If it is not within this range, the alarm is triggered.

•     Possible reasons
1.    The phenomenon of hindrance in the movement of the mechanism.
2.    Unexpected servo enable occurs in the servo driver.
3.    The possible reasons for the loss of the data sent by the CPU board to the shaft card are: abnormal CPU board, abnormal shaft card and poor contact with the shaft card.
4.    Poor contact or disconnection of the command transmission line from the controller to the servo drive.
5.    Local interference.

•      Method of exclusion
1.    Check whether the lubrication system of the machine tool.
2.    Check to see if the screw is stuck.
3.    Check whether the servo motor power and encoder cable are connected properly.
4.    Check whether the servo motor power and encoder cable are damaged.
5.    Check whether the driver is powered on properly and if there is any missing phase.
6.    Do not turn off the machine tool after the alarm occurs, check whether the date of diagnostic function Nos. 8, 9 and 10 converge to 0.
If the values of diagnostic variables 8, 9 and 10 remain unchanged, please re-find the origin. After finding the origin, observe the diagnostic variables 24, 25, 26 and 40, 41, 42:
If any of the values of variables 24, 25 and 26 is not 0, there is something wrong with the feedback loop.
If any of the values of variables 40, 41 and 42 is not 0, it means that there is a loss of instructions in the circuit of the controller motor.
If the variables 24, 25, 26 and 40, 41, 42 are not 0, the possibility of signal interfer-ence is greater, which is shown by the gradual increase of the values of variables 8, 9 and 10 in processing. The specific point of failure may be the poor contact between the CPU board and the shaft card. Try to replace the CPU board and the shaft card.
7.    Try to replace the motor and drive.

8.2.7    Tracking error alarm  

•     Alarm description
Due to the servo characteristics, the positioning of the servo motor can not immediately re-spond to the instructions of the controller, but will lag behind. When the backwardness is not within the allowable range, the controller will issue an alarm that the tracking error exceeds.

•     Possible reasons
1.    The mechanism does not move smoothly.
2.    Poor contact of wire rod.
3.    The deceleration time set by the controller parameters is too short.
4.    Drive or motor failure.

•      Method of exclusion
1.    Check whether the machine tool is installed.
2.    Check the lubrication circuit to ensure that the moving parts of the machine tool are fully lubricated
3.    Check the wiring of the machine tool to ensure that the motor, driver and other lines and connected properly and are not damaged.
4.    Adjust the acceleration and deceleration time of the corresponding shaft.
5.    The airborne machine tool reconfirms that the machine mechanism moves smoothly and there is no interference.
6.    If you still can’t rule out the alarm. Please contact Machinery customer service center for repair

1.    Diagnostic variable 32：X-axis reasonable tracking error
2.    Diagnostic variable 33：Y-axis reasonable tracking error
3.    Diagnostic variable 34：Z-axis reasonable tracking error

8.2.8    Absolute position battery is low power

Absolute position encoders are used in this machine tool servo motor. There is no need to re-turn to zero after the machine is shut down and restarted. When the machine tool is shut down, the encoder of the servo motor will record the position information of each linear axis. When the machine tool is shut down, the power supply of the servo motor encoder is provided by the bat-tery behind the machine tool. when the battery is low, the alarm of  “absolute position battery is low” will be issued.

Precautions when replacing batteries:
1.    Battery specification：LR20 Model（N0.1battery）
2.    The battery should be replaced when the machine tool is powered on normally, other-wise the absolute position information or the machine tool will be lost.

 

8.2.9    Absolute position zero lost

Absolute position encoders are used in this machine tool servo motor. There is no need to re-turn to zero after the machine is shut down and restarted. When the machine tool is shut down, the encoder of the servo motor will record the position information of each linear axis. When the machine tool is turned on, the system does not read the position information of the servo motor, their will be an alarm of “absolute position origin is set”.

•     Possible reasons
1.    The machine tool is shut down for a long time, and the battery is consumed in the absolute position.
2.    Absolute position when the battery is low, the battery is not replaced in time.
3.    Damage to servo motor or drive.
4.    A new motor or drive has been replaced.

•     Method of exclusion
1.    Power on the machine tool at least once a week.
2.    Change the battery in time when the battery is low power.
3.    Re Set the absolute zero point.
Machine tool zero, please refer to 5.6 machine tool itinerary.

•     Setting steps of zero position
1.    Switch the machine tool to hand wheel control mode.
2.    Control the movement of each straight axis to the origin position through the hand wheel. refer to 5.6 machine tool itinerary.
3.    Switch the machine tool to origin mode.
4.    Use the NC function key to enter the NC origin setting page, refer to the following steps:
“parameter setting” → “tandem parameter” → “general tandem axis” → “absolute posi-tion origin”.
5.    Move the cursor, select the corresponding axis, and complete the zero setting.

8.3    The attention of maintenance

1.    Before repairing the machine tool, professional maintenance personnel should be famil-iar with the electrical control principle of the machine tool and the operation steps of the machine tool.
2.    During the use of the machine tool, the dust in the electrical installation niche must be cleaned regularly, and the power supply must be cut off when cleaning the electrical in-stallation niche.
3.    When the machine tool is shut down for a long time, the machine tool needs to be ener-gized once a week to run the machine tool at a low speed. The running time is generally not less than 2 hours.
4.    When the machine tool fails, first check whether the power supply and each control voltage are normal; whether the circuit breakers and switches are in normal state; whether the connectors and plugs are in good contact and whether there is any loose-ness.
5.    It is strictly forbidden to plug and unplug any connecting devices when the machine is powered on.
6.    It is strictly forbidden to solder electronic circuits when the soldering iron is energized.
7.    The positions of switches and stoppers on the machine tool have been adjusted before leaving the factory. Users should not adjust them easily, so as not to affect the normal use of the machine tool.

If the user cannot solve the fault that appears, please contact with us in time for proper han-dling of the fault.

828d Driver Debugging (驱动器调试)

Modify parameter 918: change the x-axis to 11, the y-axis to 12, and the z-axis to 13. The system will then be able to recognize these drives. Remember to save the parameters after making the changes.

1：TOOL ADJUST

1.    Modify MD14510[19] to 1，machine will get into tool adjust mode ,and the system will give you alarm ”tool adjust mode”  after that，TSCW and TSCCW button will work（attention：The height of Z axis must be higher than the tool change position, otherwise the ATC Won’t move）,after you finish tool adjust，close tool adjust mode(change MD14510[19] to 0)
2：TOOL REF: in tool adjust mode, move the magazine to tool 1 position , then switch to REF mode ,press “tool ref” button , the tool ref will be completed 
Tool change safe position  MD14514[1]
Tool change position      MD14514[2]
Max tool number        MD14510[20]

2：M code

K11 spindle tool control enable，when the led of K11 light，the button on the head will work, press k11 again, enable will become disable
M21  ATC go to spindle poistion       
M22  ATC go back to original Position
