808d how to change language 

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. find language change.
  3. Choose English , press “EOB”
  4. Wait for a moment, the language will become English.

808d how to change home direction

1. press “shift+system”

2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”

3. find MD mach.data----expert list----axis MD

4. choose X axis , find 34010(REFP_VELO_DIR_IS_MINUS), change from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0,after that ,you will find the home direction has been ok.

808d how to install 4th

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find Mach.data, press “input”
  4. Find expert list—channel MD, you will see 20070[4], change it from 0 to 5, press active, the system will restart.
  5. find basic list, you can see MD14510[18], change it from 0 to 1,press active, the system will restart.
  6. After system restart complete, 4 axis will work

808d how to monitor  PLC

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find PLC, press “input”
  4. choose PLC status, input I/O number (for example ,I3.0,I3.1 and so on), then you can see the status of these i/o signals.

1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find Mach.data, press “input”
  4. find basic list, you can see MD14510[18], change it from 1 to 0,press active, the system will restart.
  5. Find expert list—channel MD, you will see 20070[4], change it from 5 to 0, press active, the system will restart.
  6. After system restart complete, turn off machine ,and remove 4th from machine, removing working finished.

808d how to restore arc file

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find Archv,press “input”
  4. if you have arc file in direction you can find two restore option, one is restore start-up archive ,the another is restore start-up archive from the default direction, if there is no arc file in default direction, you only see restore start-up archive.
  5. You can choose restore start-up archive from the default direction, the system will give you a confirm menu, press ok , the system will restore parameter from the file
  6. Waiting for a moment, the 808d will complete the restore progress and restart itself.

808d how to set home point

1. press “shift+system”

2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”

3. find MD mach.data----expert list----axis MD

4. if you want to reset z axis , choose Z axis , find 34210[0], change it from 0 to 1 ，then switch to ref mode, and press Z+(or Z-), the machine z coordinate will become 0, it means you have set z home point.(if you want to set x and y home point ,the same operation on x and y).

808d(ARM) how to adjust ATC

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find Mach.data, press “input”
  4. find basic list, you can see MD14510[0], change it from 0 to 1,press active, the system will restart.
  5. After system restart complete, you can see alarm that in tool adjust mode, it means the system has in tool adjust mode
  6. When in adjust mode, K9 and K10 on MCP will work, press K10, POT will down ,press again ,POT will up.
  7. When pot is up, press “mag CW “, maganize will turn CW, press “mag CCW”, maganize will turn CCW
  8. When pot is down, press k9, the arm will turn

808d(ARM) how to do tool ref

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find Mach.data, press “input”
  4. find basic list, you can see MD14510[0], change it from 0 to 1,press active, the system will restart.
  5. After system restart complete, you can see alarm that in tool adjust mode, it means the system has in tool adjust mode
  6. Find “MAG REF” button on the panel, press it ,the LED on the key will light, then make all axis go home, and switch to MDI mode, in MDI mode, press “M35” ,then press cycle start, the ATC will auto go REF, when the ATC stop turn, it’s in T1, position and in screen, it still show T0,it’s nothing, when tool REF finish ,tool REF alarm will be also disappeared
  7. Before you do tool change, please check MD14514[3], this number is for the tool change position of z axis, you can move z axis to the position to see if the position is right.
  8. After above, press offset on the panel, you can find tool list, make sure there is 16 tools in the list ,or the system will give alarm “wrong tool number “ and stop tool change.
  9. At last, try tool change , in MDI mode, press

T2

M6

They must be in different line.

If everything is ok, the ATC will go to T2 ,and the screen will also show T2 from T0

808d how to back&restore PLC

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find sys.data, press “input”


  4. choose NCK/PLC data
  5. OEM PLC application(*.pte) is the plc file, you can copy it to USB for backup and copy pte file from USB to this folder to upgrade plc.

808d how to restore parameter

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find SYS.data, press “input”
  4. choose NCK/PLC dat., press input.
  5. copy complete.tea to the this folder ,system will restart, when restart finished, parameter restore completed

808d(MG) how to do tool ref

  1. press “shift+system”
  2. choose set password, the password is “sunrise”
  3. find Mach.data, press “input”
  4. find basic list, you can see MD14510[19], change it from 0 to 1,press active, the system will restart.
  5. After system restart complete, you can see alarm that in tool adjust mode, it means the system has in tool adjust mode
  6. Switch to REF mode ,and find “MAG REF” button on the panel, press it , the ATC will auto go REF, when the ATC stop turn, it’s in T1, position and in screen, it still show T0,it’s nothing, tool REF have been finished.
  7. At last, try tool change , in MDI mode, press

T2M6

If everything is ok, the ATC will go to T2 ,and the screen will also show T2 from T0

808d-ttc100 how to use toolmeasure  screen

  1. switch to jog mode---get into tool measure screen---automea—press data probe, set the number as picture， ABS.position is not need input, system will input it when doing probe calibrate
  2. measure your standard tool, and press your standard tool length into tool offset, for example, my standard tool is 134.89 and it install in T1, I set T1 offset as picture
  3. return to tool measure screen, press calibrate probe, then move z axis down until the standard tool touch tool setter, wait for about 0.5~1s, the z axis will auto move up and down slowly to tool setter, when it touch tool setter and move up again , calibrate completed

1 Preface

1.1 Why you should calibrate your tool setter?

When your tool setter is assembled and mounted on the bench of the CNC machine, it is necessary to align the stylus faces with the machine axes to avoid errors when setting tools. It is worth taking care with the operation, you should try to get the faces aligned to within 0.01mm for normal use. It is suggest that you should calibrate the tool setter regularly. 
It needs calibration by using the modules which is supplied in the software to get the exact triggered position when the stylus is installed on the tool setter. Calibration results will be stored in the corresponding variables and used by the other programs.
Values obtained are axis trigger positions in machine co-ordinates. Errors due to machine and triggering characteristics can be calibrate out automatically in this way, so that it can improve the measuring accuracy. 


Attention: Poor repeatability of trigger point values indicates that either the tool setter/stylus assembly is loose or a machine/ setter fault exists. 
This tool setter requires calibration when it has been set up on the machine correctly. It is imperative that you should calibrate it in the following circumstances.
1. A new stylus fitted to your setter.
2. It has happened an impact, but the accuracy is normal.
3. When the measuring accuracy decline.
4. This tool setter has been idled for a long time. 
1.2 Notes about spindle RPM and feed rate

1.2 Notes about spindle RPM and feed rate

This software can be used to measure the length of the tool (rotating or non-rotating). You can also measure the length and diameter with a rotating spindle in order to make the measurement more closed to the actual working condition. 
RPM and the feed rate in the program is based on a large number of experiments, it can be improved on some special occasions. 
Attention: Setting tools by rotating against the stylus is suitable for most tools. However some tools, such as those with carbide tips or delicate cutting teeth, may have a tiny wear when it touch the stylus.

1.First touch spindle RPM
RPM for the first move onto the tool setter is calculated from a surface cutting speed of 60.0meters/min. This is maintained within the range from 150rpm to 800rpm.

2.First touch feed rate
The feed rate is calculated as the following methods:
When set the diameter: F= 0.125×RPM (mm/min)
When set the length: F= 0.165×RPM (mm/min) 

3.Second touch spindle RPM
800rpm

4.Second touch feed rate
4 mm/min

1.3 How to get technical support

If you have any technical problems in the using of this software, you can contact your dealer, or contact with Harbin Pioneer directly. 
Please give the models of your CNC system and your probe, and describe the technical problems you meet when you contact us. 

2 Software installation

2.1 Modules introduction

There are following five modules in the tool setting software. 
           Code                              Function
           L960                              Reset R variables. 
           L965                              Initial setting.
           L967                              Set the length of the tool.
           L968                              Set the diameter of the tool.
           L969                              Automatic length and diameter setting.
Modules L965 are secondary subroutines, which you can not call directly.

2.2 Check and adjustment

It may need to modify the settings in the software according to the condition of your CNC system. This work must be carried out by a professional and it can not be modified optionally.
Please adjust the settings in the software by following steps: 
1. Modify the related variable value according to the service condition in your CNC system.
2.. Set the values of concerned R variables according to the condition of your CNC system. 
3. Calibrate the tool setter by using the modules L967 and L968. 
4. Get the dimensions of the tool by using the modules L967 and L968. 
5. Measure the same tool by using the Modules L969.
There will have some detailed introduction in the following chapter.

1.Edit the module L965
...
D0
G94
R10=220; Base Addr.                        Base address of the data.
R[R10+15]=2; 1=Diameter, 2=Radius        Offset mode.
...
You may edit the bold content according to your CNC system.
Please modify the value of R10 according to the service condition in your CNC system. It is the staring address of the data storage for the tool setter, whose default value is 200. Variables R221~R235 will be used to store calibration data and settings, which you can not modify optionally.
Read your CNC system manual and set the tool offset mode(Diameter or Radius) correctly.

2.Back-off variable R[Base addr.+6]
This measuring software uses standard two-touch method of measurement. A back-off distance factor R[Base addr.+6] is provided for adjusting the move distance off the surface prior to the final measuring move. 
The software loads a default value of 0.15 when it first run. You should adjust the value of R[Base addr.+6] according to the waiting time between two touches, and it is suggest that this value should not be too big or too small, and its range is 0.01~0.6.

3.Input setting R[Base addr.+7]
You should set the value of the variable R[Base addr.+7] according to the actual connection between the tool setter and the CNC system:
R[Base addr.+7]=±1    Single wire of the tool setter has been connected to the post X20. (802Dsl）
R[Base addr.+7]=±2    Single wire of the tool setter has been connected to the post X21. (802Dsl）
R[Base addr.+7]=1(or “2”), it means that high level signal is available to the CNC system, R[Base addr.+7]=-1(or “-2”), it means that low level signal is available to the CNC system. This value is determined by the relevant settings of the CNC system, read the manual of the CNC system for details.

R variables R0~R33 will be used by the programs to store calculated values. it will use another 15 R variables to store the calibration data and settings.（Default base address is 220, so, variables R221~235will be used by the programs）If other programs in the CNC machine have used these variables, you should change the base address of the R variables in L965 to avoid conflict. 4 Calibrate the tool setter

It will use the standard mandrel to calibrate the tool setter. Length and  diameter of the mandrel is accurate values.
This chapter will introduce the methods to calibrate the length and diameters of the tool setter. 

4.1 Calibrate the length of the tool setter

Cycle code: L967
Function: This cycle is used to calibrate the top plane of the stylus and get the exact triggered points when dynamic and static measurements are performed.
Method:  (1) Move the mandrel to the starting point.
          (2) Run the program to calibrate the tool setter, and it will return to its starting point when the
             program end.
Format:  L960
         R0=k [R2=z]  []denotes optional inputs
         L967
Starting point::  Move the mandrel to a suitable point above the stylus. 
Description:     R0: k=Length of the standard mandrel.
      R2: z=Incremental depth for the measurement from the starting point (Default: -10mm), which is normally a minus value.

Output: Calibration results will be stored into the variables R[Base addr.+1] and R[Base addr.+2] automatically. 
Example:
Move the standard mandrel to the starting point (10mm above the stylus) and then run the program. 
             L960                    Reset R variables.
             R0=199.985                Length of the standard mandrel is 1999.985mm.
             L967                    Calibrate the tool setter.
             M30                    Program ends.

4.2 Calibrate the diameter of the tool setter

Cycle code: L968
Function: This program is used to calibrate the side of the stylus and get the exact triggered point. 
Method: (1)Move the standard mandrel to the starting point.
         (2)Run the program to calibrate the tool setter, and it will return to its starting point when the
           program ends.
Format:  L960
          R0=d R3=s [R2=z]  []denotes optional inputs
          L968
Starting point:    Move the standard mandrel to the point which is a suitable height above the center of the
              stylus. 

Description:    R0: d=Nominal size of the stylus.
            R3: s=Exact diameter of the standard mandrel. 
           R2:z=Incremental depth for the measurement from the starting point(Default: -15mm), which is 
              normally a minus value.
Output: All the calibration results will be written into the variables R[Base addr.+3]~ R[Base addr.+5] automatically when the program ends. 
Example:
You should calibrate the stylus both in X and Y axes, if you use a disc-shaped stylus. If you decide to measure the diameter along X axis, you should calibrate the stylus in Y axis first and X axis second. If you decide to measure the diameter along Y axis, you should calibrate the stylus in X axis first and Y axis second. It will do the calibration in order according to the setting in R variable R[Base addr.+8]. 
Although it only need calibration in the measuring direction, but the program will also calibrate the stylus in two directions, if you use a square stylus. 
Example: Calibrate the diameter of the stylus.
If you want to measure the diameter in X axis, measure the length towards Y+ axis, so that you should the value of the R[Base addr.+8] is “1”. Move the standard mandrel to the starting point, then run the following calibration program. It will calibrate in Y axis first, and then X axis.

            L960                    Reset R variates.
            R0=15                    Diameter of the stylus is 15mm.
            R3=40                    Exact diameter of the standard mandrel is 40mm.
            L968                    Calibrate the diameter. 
            M30                    Program end.

5 Tool dimensions setting

This tool setter can be used to set the parameters of the tool after a well calibration. This chapter will introduce the methods of the setting cycles.

5.1 Set the length of the tool semi-automatically

Cycle code: L967
Function: This cycle can be used to set the length of the tool semi-automatically. 
Method: (1) Move the tool to the starting point before running the program.
        (2) Run the program to set the length of the tool. It will return to its starting point when the program ends.
Format:  L960
         R1=t [R2=z R3=s R4=e R6=r]  []denotes optional inputs
         L967

Starting point:    Move the tool to a suitable position above the stylus.

Description:  R1: t=Tool offset number in the tool offset list.
             Example: (1) R1=10, Tool number 10 is selected and default offset number D1 is set for 
                      Diameter.
                      (2) R1=10.2, Tool number 10 is selected and offset number D2 is set for diameter. 
            R2: z=Incremental depth for the measurement from the starting point(Default: -10mm), which
                is normally a minus value.
            R3: s=Diameter of the tool to be measured. (1) +s: Right-handed cutting tools. 
                                                   (2) –s: Left-handed cutting tools.
            R4:e=Empirical compensation for the length. It will reduce the length if you input a positive
                 value.
            R6:r=Tolerance for breakage detection. Offset are not adjusted when using the breakage
               detection feature.
Variables R29 will be set to “1” when a broken tool is found, and it will sent out an alarm from the CNC system.
Output: Exact length of the tool will be written to corresponding variable in the tool offset list. 
Examples:
Move the tool to the position which is 20mm above the stylus and then run the program.
 (1)     L960
R1=20 R2=-20             Set the length (non-rotating), and write the value to T20D1. 
 L967
(2)     L960
 R1=8.2 R2=-20 R3=20     Set the length (rotating), diameter is 20mm, write the value to T8D2.
Note: In general, the tool to be measured is located to a point which is less than 10mm above the stylus, so that you do not need to input R2 when you call the program. (Default value is 10mm)

5.2 Set the diameter of the tool semi-automatically 

Cycle code: L968
Function: This program can be used to set the radius of the tool semi-automatically. 
Method: (1) Move the tool to the starting point before running the program.
        (2) Run the program to set the diameter of the tool, it will return to its starting point when the
           program ends.
Format:   L960
R1=t R3=s [R2=z R5=f R6=r]  []denotes optional inputs 
L968
Starting point::    Move the tool to a suitable and safe position above the stylus.

Description: R1: t=Tool offset number in the tool offset list. 
                      Example: (1) R1=10, Tool number 10 is selected and default offset number D1 is set for diameter. 
                               (2) R1=10.2, Tool number 10 is selected and offset number D2 is set for diameter. 
            R2: z=Incremental depth for the measurement from the starting point(Default: -15mm), which
               is normally a minus value.
                        R3: s=Diameter of the tool to be measured. (1) +s: Right-handed cutting tools. 
                                                               (2) –s: Left-handed cutting tools.
            R5: f=Empirical compensation for the diameter. It will reduce the diameter if you input a positive value.
            R6:r=Tolerance for breakage detection. Offset are not adjusted when using the breakage detection feature.
Variables R29 will be set to “1” when a broken tool is found, and it will sent out an alarm from the CNC
 system.
Output:: Diameter of the tool will be written into the corresponding offset variables automatically when the
         program ends. 
Example:
Move the tool to the starting point and run the program.
L960
        R1=6 R3=20        Measure the diameter of the tool (Rotating). Diameter is 20mm. Measuring
                           result will be written into T6D1. 

5.3 Automatic length and diameter setting

It can set the length and diameter of the tool at the same time by using this cycle. CNC machine will carry out the following steps:
(1) Select the tool from the tool changer.
(2) Move the tool in X and Y axes over the stylus.
(3) Fast move down to the approach position and apply the tool offset. (Protected move)
(4) Set the length of the tool. (If you input “R7=1” or “R7=3”) 
(5) Set the diameter of the tool. (If you input “R7=2” or “R7=3”） 
(6) Retract the setter to the home position through Z axis.

Attention: Nominal tool offset length values must be loaded in the tool registers before execution of the cycles.
Cycle code: L969
Function: This cycle can set the length and diameter of the tool automatically. The cycle can control the CNC system to select the tool in the tool changer, install it onto the spindle and move it to the starting point automatically. 
Method: (1) Nominal tool offset length values must be loaded in the tool registers before execution of the cycles. 
(2) Run the program, and it will return to its home position when the program ends.
Format: L960
    R1=t R3=s R7=w[R4=e R5=f ]  []denotes optional inputs
    L969
Starting point::    A suitable height above the stylus

Description:  R7: w represent measuring mode.
             w=1 Set the length of the tool only. (Default)  
         w=2 Set the radius only. 
         w=3 Set the length and radius together. 
             R1: t=Tool offset number in the tool offset list.
Example: (1) R1=10, Tool number 10 is selected and default offset number D1 is set for diameter. 
         (2) R1=10.2, Tool number 10 is selected and offset number D2 is set for diameter. 
                R3: s=Diameter of the tool to be measured. (1) +s: Right-handed cutting tools.
                                                                     (2) –s: Left-handed cutting tools.
            R4: e=Empirical compensation for the length. (Compensate for thermal expansion). 
                It will reduce the length if you input a positive value.
            R5: f=Empirical compensation for the diameter. (Compensate for cutting force expansion). It will reduce the diameter if you input a positive value.
Output:: Measuring results will be written into the corresponding offset value when the program ends. 
Examples:    
 (1)   L960
R7=1 R1=20 R3=5       Set the length only, length value will be written
                        Into the offset number 20.
 L969

 (2)   L960
R7=2 R1=8 R3=20       Set the diameter only, diameter will be written
 Into the offset number 8. 
L969

 (3)    L960
            R7=3 R1=10 R3=10     Set the length and diameter together, results will be written into the
                                   offset number 10. 
        L969

6 Tool breakage detection 

It is very important to check whether the tool is broken by using this cycle, especially in the automatic workshop. This cycle can also be used to determine whether the tool is damaged or broken.
Cycle code:  L969
Function:  Measure the length and diameter of the tool automatically and determine whether it is broken.
Attention: Tool offsets are not adjusted when using the tool breakage feature.
Note: Nominal tool offset length values must be loaded in the tool registers before execution of the cycles. 
Format:  L960
         R1=t R7=w R6=r [R3=s ]
         L969
Starting point::An appropriate and safe position.
Description: R7: w represent measuring mode.
              w=1  Check the length to see whether it is broken.(Default)  
         w=2  Check the diameter to see whether it is broken.
            R1: t=Tool offset number in the tool offset list.
                      Example: (1) R1=10, Tool number 10 is selected and default offset number D1 is set for diameter. 
                                (2) R1=10.2, Tool number 10 is selected and offset number D2 is set for diameter. 
             R3: s=Diameter of the tool to be measured. (1) +s: Right-handed cutting tools. 
                                                    (2) –s: Left-handed cutting tools. 
             R6: r=Tolerance for breakage detection. Offset are not adjusted when using the breakage detection feature.           
Output:: Variables will be set to “1” when a broken tool is found, and it will sent out a alarm from the CNC system.
Example:
    L960
        R1=10 R3=5 R7=1 R6=0.05    Check the length of the tool and determine whether it is broken.
    L969

When an error occurs during use, an alarm message is generated. This may be displayed on the screen of the CNC system. This chapter describes the meaning and likely reasons of each alarm.

DIA OUT OF RANGE

Tool size is out of range.

 

TOOL BROKEN

Tool is broken.

Article title: SYIL X7 Pioneer Probe Installation Guide
Article body:
Introduction

This guide describes the steps required to complete the field installation of a Pioneer Probe in a Syil X7 CNC Vertical Machining Center.

Electrical Safety

Caution: When you do maintenance or repair on CNC machine and their components, you must always follow basic safety precautions. This decreases the risk of injury and mechanical damage.

  • Set the main circuit breaker to the [OFF] position.

Danger: Before beginning any work inside the control cabinet the High Voltage indicator light on the Vector Drive must have been off for at least 5 minutes.

Some service procedures can be dangerous or life-threatening. DO NOT attempt a procedure that you do not fully understand. If you have any doubts about completing a procedure, request factory support.

 Contents

Probe Optical Components.............................................................................. 3

Probe Installation.............................................................................................. 3

Optical Interface Cable Routing and Termination............................................ 5

Installation Completion..................................................................................... 8

Operational Verification................................................................................ 8

Additional Information....................................................................................... 8

Figure 1 Cable Gutter and Access Covers...................................................... 4

Figure 3 Optical Interface Mounting Locations................................................ 4

Figure 2 Optical Interface Cable Pass-through................................................ 4

Figure 4 Optical Interface with Mounting Brackets.......................................... 5

Figure 5 Completed Optical interface Mounting.............................................. 5

Figure 6 Controller Enclosure Layout.............................................................. 6

Figure 7 Optical Interface Conductors............................................................. 6

Figure 8 Optical Interface Conductor Termination 7 

Probe Optical Components

The Pioneer OPS-30 probe kit consists of two major components. The two major components consist of the OP510 touch probe and the OSI-20 receiver and transmitter.
1.    The OP510 is mounted in the spindle of the mill and uses a stylus to contact the component it is to be probed. The OP510 communicates with the OSI-20 utilizing infrared signals.
2.    The OSI-20 transmitter and receiver provide the interface between the mill’s electronic and the OP510.
Addition details on the operation of the OPS probe kit can be found in the “OPS-30 User Manual” included in the kit.


Probe Installation

The focus of the guide is the installation and startup of the Pioneer probe system in a Syil X7 Vertical Machine Center. This guide does not cover the operation of the probing system other than the initial startup and operational verification.


Installation Preparation

This section of the guide will cover the modifications necessary to mount optical interface and route the interface cable.
1.    As shown in figure 1 remove the screws retaining the two cable covers and set the covers and screws to the side.
2.    From the inside of the mill enclosure drill a 18mm hole in the position shown in figure 2. Ensure that no existing cable in the cable gutter will not be damage when drill the 18mm hole.
3.    From the inside of the enclosure drill two 5mm mounting hole using the location shown figure 3.
4.    Prepare the optical interface for mounting by loosely attaching the provided mounting brackets. The mounting brackets should be assembled as shown in figure 4.
5.    With the bracket installed on the optical interface mount the assembly to the enclosure using the far-left mounting hole and a 5mm screw and nut.
6.    Position the optical interface aiming the face downward and toward the spindle centerline. When satisfied with the position of the interface, tighten all fasteners. Mounting and approximate position of interface can be seen in figure 5
7.    With the optical probe mounted pass the attached cable with bushing installed through the previously drilled 18m hole and use the bushing nut on the backside to hold the cable in place.
8.    Using the support strap, 5mm bolt and nut provided mount the cable using the 5mm hole previously drilled. The completed installation is shown in figure 5.

Optical Interface Cable Routing and Termination

This section of the guide will describe the details required to route and termination the optical interface cable and conductors.
1.    Remove the rear cover of the controller enclosure held in place by 12 screws. This will expose the terminal blocks as shown in figure 6.
2.    Route the optical interface cable through the cable gutter, down through the top of the controller enclosure and to the terminal blocks in the lower lefthand corner.
3.    Shorten the cable as need and prepare the conductors as shown in figure 7. Add labels to conductors as follows: First Green = “+24”, Second Green = “Probe” (order of green conductors does not matter), Red = “+24”, Black = “0V” and White = “Probe En”. The remaining wires are not used and should be cut back and insulated. It is suggested that wires be terminated using ferrules. The green +24 and the red +24 can be terminated in the same ferrule.
4.    Terminate the conductors as follows:
Green/yellow conduct in a green and yellow terminal block, the green and red conductors labeled “+24” in “+24” terminal block, the green conductor labeled “Probe” in the “Probe” terminal block, the black conductor labeled “0V” in the “0V” terminal block, and the white conductor labeled “Probe EN” in the “Probe-EN” terminal block as in fig 8.

Installation Completion

1.    Replace the two-metal gutter covers on the top of the mill.
2.    Replace the rear controller enclosure cover.
3.    Power up the mill and controller as normal.
Operational Verification
This section of the guide will test the basic functionality of the probing system.
1.    After the mill and controller are fully powered up verify that the OSI-20 has a single green LED illuminated. This verifies that the interface is powered and operational.
2.    Install two good batteries into the OP5100 touch probe per the included user’s manual.
3.    Place the touch probe in the spindle and lower the spindle to mid position.
4.    Open the MDI window on the controller and enter the following code:
i.    M80;
5.    Press the cycle start button. The touch probe should rotate and begin flashing green LEDs. The OSI-20 should have an addition green LED illuminate This verifies that the touch probe and optical interface are communicating
6.    As a final operational verification go the controller and press the following keys: “Settings” then “PLC Status”. A screen showing the status of the input bits should be visible. With the probe still operational from step 6 push on the end of the touch probe stylus. While moving the stylus verify that input status is changing from FF to 0 and back again. For a X7 with an umbrella tool changer this will be position 18, for an arm tool changer it will be position 21.
7.    To turn off the probe, return to the MDI window, clear the previous codes and then enter M81 and pressing cycle start. The probe should no longer be flashing and the second LED on the optical interface should be off.
If all the above steps were completed successfully the probing system should be ready for use.

Additional Information

For additional information related to the operation of the probing system please reference the included user’s manual.

Removing and Adding the 4th axis unit on a SYIL with Siemens 828D Control

 Foreword

Machines equipped with the 4th axis units have been built such that the user can remove and re-install the 4th axis as needed without manipulating multiple machine parameters

An Easy Extend function is available to make this process easy.

User level

The instructions herein require a user to have a good understanding of the operation of a CNC Milling machine.

In order for the user to be able to complete the steps, the physical controller key must be switched to “Setup” or “I”

 Procedure 

 

The 4th axis units are heavy!

Use suitable lifting equipment and observe safe lifting pratices

Correctly rated lifting eyes are provided with the 4th axis units for this purpose

 Removing the 4th axis: 

1

Press the Menu Select key on the controller to allow selection of the advance menus

2

Press the Setup Page soft key on the bottom row of the screen

3

Press the Password soft key on the vertical row on the right hand side of the screen

4

 

Type in the system Password: SUNRISE

5

Press the OK button to accept the password. If the password has been typed correctly you will receive an acknowledgement

6

Press the OFFSETS button on the Controller

7

Scroll the bottom row of softkeys to the Right pressing the menu advance button

8

Enter the Easy Extend Menu using the softkey on the bottom of the screen

9

 

Highlight the “add/remove A axis, Estop required” option on the screen

10

Press the enable function softkey

11

 

When prompted, type in the passcode: 123456

12

Press the Emergency Stop Button

13

Press the activate softkey to enable the ATC adjusting mode.

The Process or removing the 4th axis will take approximately 1-2minutes

14

When the process is complete, switch off the power to the machine using the Isolator on the electrical cabinet

15

 

The 4th axis can now be safely removed from the machine by disconnecting the air or oil hoses and electrical connectors

 

 Re-Installing the 4th axis: 

1

Press the Menu Select key on the controller to allow selection of the advance menus

2

Press the Setup Page soft key on the bottom row of the screen

3

Press the Password soft key on the vertical row on the right hand side of the screen

4

Press the OK button to accept the password. If the password has been typed correctly you will receive an acknowledgement

6

Press the OFFSETS button on the Controller

7

Scroll the bottom row of softkeys to the Right pressing the menu advance button

8

Enter the Easy Extend Menu using the softkey on the bottom of the screen

9

 

Highlight the “add/remove A axis, Estop required” option on the screen

10

Press the enable function softkey

11

 

When prompted, type in the passcode: 123456

12

Press the Emergency Stop Button

13

Press the activate softkey to enable the ATC adjusting mode.

The Process or removing the 4th axis will take approximately 1-2minutes

14

When the process is complete, switch off the power to the machine using the Isolator on the electrical cabinet

15

 

The 4th axis can now be safely installed in the machine by reconnecting the air or oil hoses and electrical connectors

Re-Referencing or resetting the ARM TYPE Tool Changer on a SYIL with Siemens 828D Control

 Foreword

There will potentially be instances in the operation of the SYIL CNC Machines that will require the user to manipulate the components of the Automatic Tool Changer in order to reset it or re-reference it.

Examples include when a user presses the Emergency Stop button during a tool change or if through use the physical carousel pocket numbers do not match the ones indicated within the controller.

For further understanding of the general operation of your Automatic Tool Changer, refer to the dedicated manual provided with your machine

User level

The instructions herein require a user to have a good understanding of the operation of a CNC Milling machine.

In order for the user to be able to complete the steps, the physical controller key must be switched to “Setup” or “I”

Procedure 

 

If the ATC ARM has stopped with a tool gripped or mid swing, Do not proceed until you have spoken to a SYIL Engineer

 Empty the magazine-Recommended: 

1

 

Remove the tool within the spindle

2

 

Open the right hand side of the machine

3

 

Using the sheet metal tool supplied with the machine, remove the tools within the magazine

4

On the controller, press enter the Offset screen

5

Virtually unload the tools on the controller so that the tool data is not lost

 Enable the Tool Adjust Mode: 

1

Press the Menu Select key on the controller to allow selection of the advance menus

2

Press the Setup Page soft key on the bottom row of the screen

3

Press the Password soft key on the vertical row on the right hand side of the screen

4

 

Type in the system Password: SUNRISE

5

Press the OK button to accept the password. If the password has been typed correctly you will receive an acknowledgement

6

Press the OFFSETS button on the Controller

7

Scroll the bottom row of softkeys to the Right pressing the menu advance button

8

Enter the Easy Extend Menu using the softkey on the bottom of the screen

9

 

Highlight the “Tool adjust mode” option on the screen

10

Press the enable function softkey

11

 

When prompted, type in the passcode: 123456

12

Press the activate softkey to enable the ATC adjusting mode

 Recovering from an E-stop during a tool change 

1

 

Remove the tool within the spindle

2

 

Open the right hand side of the machine

3

 

Using the sheet metal tool supplied with the machine, remove the tools within the magazine

4

Enter Jog Mode

 

Press the MAG EN to allow magazine manipulation button on the MCP keyboard and check that the LED stays on

5

If the tool pocket has stuck in the down position, press the Pocket UP/DOWN button to lift it to safe position

6

ONLY IF IT IS SAFE!

Press the ATC CW button to reset the ATC ARM

 Check the rotation direction of the Tool Magazine 

1

 

Ensure the safety door of the machine is closed and locked

2

Press the Ref Point button on the MCP keyboard

3

Press the MAG EN to allow magazine manipulation button on the MCP keyboard and check that the LED stays on

4

MAG CCW

Press the MAG CCW button and check that the magazine has advance in the Counter Clockwise direction

5

MAG CW

Press the MAG CW button and check that the magazine has advance in the Clockwise direction

6

MAG REF

Press the MAG REF button and check that the magazine has advanced and the Tool Pocket 1 is in the Standby Location

7

 

The Tool changer is now referenced

 Reload tools as required 

1

On the controller, press enter the Offset screen

2

Select the desired tool from the tool list

2

Load the selected tool to the tool Pocket Location of your choice

 

Press the OK softkey to store the tool in a Pocket or Spindle for loading into the spindle

 Reboot the controller

Press the Illuminated Red switch to Power down the controller. Restart pressing the green illuminated ON button.

The Procedure is now complete

Article title: How to set Z home on Syil X5 with Syntec 22MA controller
Article body:
How to set Z Home on Syil X5 with Syntec 22MA controller

  1. Press AUX1, then in MPG mode, you can move z freely up, higher than normal
  2. Find B1 point with feeler gauge. Move Z-axis up and down till you find B1 with 0.15mm feeler gauge.
  3. Write down Machine Z value Set X and Y values on zero, just to be safe. In this case, Z = 9.382
  4. Push the right arrow and push param. Button

  5. Goto parameter 3433, if this reads 33450, this means you have to move down 33.45mm.

    Do not change this parameter!

  6. If your B1 point is 9.382 like in this case, substract 33.45 that means you have to move Z to -24.068. Do that with MPG.
  7. Go back to Parameters. Push Serial tuning (Account is U, password is 520) – Normal Axis-Set ABS home







  9. Switch on your control panel from MPG to Home
  10. Select Z axis and set machine home.
  11. Congratulations for a job well done.

SOP Booting Failure (Syntec Technology Co. Ltd.)

 1 Booting Screen 

2 Booting Failure Countermeasure

1. If controller can't access HMI but axis function still work, please  homing all axes and press emergency button before start rescue.

2. An efficient countermeasure for x86 controller booting failure

a) remove CF2, try if booting successful.
b) make a new CF1 if motherboard is work, should booting  successful.

3 Booting Failure Countermeasure without troubleshooting

3.1 (definitely happen) stucked before 20% while  booting (including "booting yellow bar" and "black screen")

ARM

a) Currently no solution. Have the controller back to OEM to be fixed. DiskC unreserved.

b) Remove all the wire connection(IO, ethernet, serial) except for power supply, and take off the controller from the machine. Try to reboot. 

x86

a) Remove CF2 and reboot. Make sure controller is unable to boot successfully.

b) Remake CF1. Strongly suggest that use controller to make GHO restore of CF1. How to make GHO restore : Super槽箱维修SOP

c) If any decryption is needed, please consult to OEM. 

3.2 stucked after 20% while booting

ARM

a) Access SA interface and make a SB backup.
i.) Remove OCRes (Delete customize screen related.)
ii.) Restore System Data > Restore automatic backup data > 
iii.) Restore DiskA(Delete ncfiles and resgistry.dat.)
iv.) Re-install controller software version.
v.) Restore SB backup.
v. Above steps might get some chance to boot successful.

x86

a) Remove CF2 and reboot. Make sure controller is unable to boot successfully.
b) Remake CF1. Strongly suggest that use controller to make GHO restore of CF1.
How to make  GHO restore : Super槽箱维修SOP
c) If any decryption is needed, please consult to OEM.

4 Q&A

Any notices while switch the CF card?

a) Suggest the capacity of CF card the same with old one, if DOS system.

b) Format the CF card before restore it and check without any wired files. Some abnormal files might cause booting failure in history.

Any software version restriction via different OS?

a) x86 + DOS ：10.116.0Z。

b) x86 + CE6：10.116.56 latest version，can't cross 10.118 version， super model is an exception。

c) ARM + CE7：The main combination, no restriction 。

What if the ghost version is too old to restore a GHO restore?

a) The GHO file was made via a higher version, so it needs a sufficient high version for restoration.

how to remove 5th (10k-arm)

  1. Press “setting”--Param(Password:520)--Goto Param
  2. Goto parameter24, change it from 2000 to 0, 4th will disable

    Goto parameter25, change it from 3000 to 0, 5th will disable

  3. Press “→”—Param-- “→”—5 Axis Param, change 30001 from 2 to 0

  4. change 3444 from 1 to 0, system will disable temperature alarm of 4th &5th

    change 3448 from 1 to 0, system will disable third limit(it’s for 5axis kits)

    change 3449 from 1 to 0, the 4th&5th (brake, alarm and so on) will disable

  5.  Until now, you can remove 5th from machine ,and remove the power of 4th&5th driver 


    In 3034,3035, 3036, this number is original the 5th center, if you remove 5th or move 5th ,even X,Y,Z home point changed , you should input the right value in it, or 5th may hit machine when running program.

Article title: 22ma how to load plc and alarm
Article body:
22ma how to load plc and alarm

  1. Copy cnc.lad, alarmPLC_CHS.xml, alarmPLC_COM.xml, ParamExt_chs.xml, ParamExt_com.xml to usb, and insert usb to controller, press setting—sys.admin(psw:520)--sys.data manager—import, choose them and press next—press ok, controller will load them when it tell you completed, restart machine, upgrade finish.

22ma how to  set ORI position

  1. Set the right position by your hand
  2. press “setting”---diga(Password:520)， NO28 is the spindle current position
  3. press “setting”---Param(Password:520)---Goto Param, looking for 1771, input the right number which show in NO28

22ma how to load macro

  1. Copy macro file to usb, and insert usb to controller, press setting—sys.admin(psw:520)--macro manager—import, choose macro file.

Article title: 22ma-mg how to find original z home point
Article body:
22ma-mg how to  find  original z home point

  1. Move z axis to the tool change position
  2. Press setting—param---goto param---2803, password= 520.
  3. Move z up 91mm(-91000=-91), for example, current z coordinate it -102.3, move to -102.3+91=-11.3, that’s the original z home point，set z home again in this place.

220ma how to set zero point

1. Move the axis to zero point

2. press “→”----Param(Password:520)---Serial Turning---normal axis---set ABS home（and switch to home mode）---set machine home.( when you lost machine zero point, you may get limit alarm, please modify 2401~2410.)

how to install 5th (10K-arm)

  1. Make sure all wiring of 4th &5th have been connect well, then Press “setting”--Param(Password:520)--Goto Param
  2. Goto parameter24, change it from 0 to 2000 , 4th will enable
    Goto parameter25, change it from 0 to 3000 , 5th will enable

  3. 3. Press “→”—Param-- “→”—5 Axis Param, change 30001 from 0 to 2

  4. change 3444 from 0 to 1, system will enable temperature alarm of 4th &5th

    change 3448 from 0 to 1, system will enable third limit(it’s for 5axis kits)

    change 3449 from 0 to 1, the 4th&5th function (brake, alarm and so on) will enable


  5. After that, restart system, 4 and 5 axis will work.

    PS: please check 3034,3035, 3036, these numbers are original 5th kits center, if you remove 5th or move 5th , even X,Y,Z home point changed , you should input the right value in them, otherwise 5th may hit machine when running program.

how to remove 4th (22ma)

  1. Press “setting”--Param(Password:520)--Goto Param

     

  2. Goto parameter24, change from 2000 to 0, 4th will disable

  3. change 3445 from 1 to 0, 3446 from 1 to 0the home point and brake of 4th will disable


  4. Until now, you can remove 4th from machine, after remove 4th , remember to cut off the breaker of 4th driver(C6)

220ma how to  set ORI position

  1. find the right position by your hand
  2. press “→”---diga(Password:520)， NO28 is the spindle current position
  3. press “→”---Param(Password:520)---Goto Param, looking for 1771, input the right number which show in NO28

220ma-5 how to do tool measure 

  1. press “→”--Param(Password:520)--Goto Param, input 3430 it’s standard tool length for calibrication.
  2. press offset/setting—tool tip measure

    Mode: choose 4, in 5 axis mode, the measure result is positive tool length,
    Tool NO. T: choose the tool number which you want to measure
    Use Reference: choose 1, Ref coord. X, Ref coord. Y will enable
    Ref coord. X: the center of X coordinate.
    Ref coord. Y: the center of Y coordinate.
    Ref coord. Z: the fast moving coordinate.
    Min Z.Mach.H: the lowest point when do tool measure 
    Safe Z After Measure: Z back point when tool measure finished.
    Gauge Z Mach.coord: it’s calibration by Gauge Z coord. Teach

    Gauge Z Mach.coord teach(F7):
     Install your standard tool on the spindle, then switch to AUTO mode, press it, system will let you input password, it’s 520, then it will begin do tool length calibration, and save the result on the Gauge Z Mach.coord, when you do it first time you can enable MPG SAM function, it can protect your tool setter.



  3. After Gauge Z Mach.coord teach, press start(F1), it will begin to do tool measure, and sav e the result into tool list,press reset(f2) will stop tool measure, when you do it first time you can enable MPG SAM function, it can protect your tool setter.

how to install 4th (22ma)

  1. Connect motor on driver and Turn on the breaker of 4th driver(C6)
  2. Turn on machine , and press “setting”--Param(Password:520)--Goto Param
  3. Goto parameter24, change from 0 to 2000, 4th will enable

  4. change 3445 from 0 to 1, change 3446 from 0 to 1, 4th function will enable.

  5. Restart machine, you get alarm as follow, don’t worry, cut off the main power of machine, then give power again, alarm will disappear.
  6. After machine restart, you need to reset home point of 4th
  7. Move 4 axis to zero point
  8. press “setting”----Param(Password:520)---Serial Turning---normal axis---set ABS home（and switch to home mode）---set machine home(switch to home mode ,loose estop switch and choose A), when it show set, home setting completed

• The purpose of safety precautions is to protect the operator from injury and machine damage caused by accidents.
  • The safety precautions must be understood and followed as they apply to the set-up and operation of all machines, including this machine.
  • Fully understand the safety instructions and the operating instructions before operating the machine. SYIL accepts no responsibility if the specified precautions are not observed and/or an accident occurs due to improper use.
  • In this manual, there are 3 types of safety instructions such as DANGER, WARNING and CAUTION, which refer to safety. They have the following meaning.

Table 2

DANGER indicates an imminently hazardous situation which, if not avoided, will result in death or serious injury

• Tie back long hair that could get caught in the undercarriage.
  • Wear safety equipment (helmet, goggles, safety shoes, etc.) to ensure your safety.
  • Always wear a helmet if there are obstacles at height in the work area.
  • Always wear a protective mask when working with workpieces such as magnesium alloys or graphite.
  • Never wear loose or baggy clothing.
  • Always close buttons completely and tie the arms of clothing so that they do not get caught in rotating parts.
  • Do not operate the machine if you are under the influence of drugs with a strong effect, non-prescribed medication or alcohol.
  • Do not operate the machine if you feel faint or lose consciousness.
  • Always use gloves when loading or unloading workpieces or tools and when removing crisps.
  • Always use safety shoes with steel toecaps and oil-resistant soles.

 

All operations, maintenance and cleaning work must be carried out in the safest possible conditions by wearing protective clothing (see table).

Always follow the personal safety standards and laws of the country in which the machine is used.

1. There are high-voltage terminals (marked with a battery warning sign) on the switch cabinet, transformer, motors, distribution boxes and other devices. Never touch any of them.
  2. Make sure that all doors and covers are closed before you switch on the power. If a door or cover is opened, you must stop work and turn off the main switch.
  3. Never modify the machine in such a way as to affect its safety. We accept no responsibility for accidents or machine malfunctions caused by improper use.
  4. Never touch the rotating workpiece or tool with your bare hands or other objects. Failure to observe this warning may result in fatal injury due to contact with the rotating workpiece.



  1. Memorize the position of the EMERGENCY STOP button so that you can press it immediately from any position.

  4. To avoid operating the machine incorrectly, check the position of the switches carefully before operating the machine.
  5. If you notice anything suspicious about the machine, stop operation immediately and call the person responsible.
  6. Always turn off the power switch on the control panel and the main power switch before leaving the machine so that it cannot be operated arbitrarily by another person.
  7. If two or more operators are working together, provide mutual signals so that they can confirm each other's safety before proceeding with a new step.
  8. Do not touch a rotating workpiece or the tool with your bare hands or any other object.

Make sure that you use the specified standard parts as spare or consumable parts so that the specifications of the machine are met. We accept no responsibility for accidents or machine malfunctions resulting from failure to observe this warning.
  10. Do not stay in the area of the chuck while the spindle is turning.

We accept no responsibility for accidents or machine malfunctions caused by unauthorized attachments, modifications or other misuse by a customer.

  1. In the event of a power failure, switch off the main power switch immediately.
  2. Make sure that the CNC unit, the control panel or the control cabinet are not damaged.
  3. Do not change the parameters or other electrical settings without a valid reason. If it is necessary to change a setting value, first check whether it is safe after the person in charge has confirmed its function, and then make a note of the original value so that it can be reset.
  4. Never remove and/or damage any of the safety labels. If the nameplates become illegible or damaged, purchase them from SYIL and affix the replacement plate in its original position so that everyone can see it.
  5. Do not open any doors or safety covers while the machine is in automatic mode.
  6. Stop all operations and switch off the machine before cleaning the machine or peripheral equipment.
  7. After finishing a job, set up each part of the machine so that it is ready for the next work series.
  8. Make sure that the compressed air from the air gun does not come into contact with the human body.

1. Do not adjust the coolant nozzles while the machine is in operation.
  2. Do not remove or move safety devices such as cams or limit switches to increase the axis travel.
  3. Do not wipe the workpiece with your hand or a rag and do not remove crisps while the tool is rotating; always stop the machine and remove the crisps with the brush.
  4. Do not operate the machine if one of the safety covers is removed.

  1. Close all doors and covers of the CNC unit, operation panel, electrical cabinet, and junction boxes to protect the damage from coolant, chips and oil.
  2. Check all electrical cables for damage to prevent accidents due to current leakage or electric shock.
  3. Do not handle coolant with bare hands since it may cause irritation. Operators with allergies should take special precautions.
  4. Do not operate the machine during violent thunderstorm like thunder or lightning.
  5. Check the safety covers regularly to make sure that they are properly closed and that they are not damaged. Repair or replace any damaged covers immediately.
  6. Always obtain assistance in handling loads beyond your capacity.
  7. The work for fork lift, crane or hoist must be carried out by the authorized person.
  8. When using fork lift, crane or hoist, make sure that there are no obstruction in the vicinity of machine working range.
  9. When lifting the machine, workpiece or other parts, always use suitable wire rope or slings so as to secure from load. Refer to the instruction manual as regards to the machine's weight or installation.
  10. Be sure to check the sling, wire rope, crane, hoist or forklift before using it. If finding out the defectiveness, repair or replace it immediately.
  11. Always wear gloves and use a brush to remove chips from tool tips; never use bare hands. Fail to observe this warning may result in serious injury.
  12. Stop all machine operations before mounting or removing a tool.
  13. Switch key related to the safety must be managed by the responsible person: locking- release key of safety door, electrical cabinet key.
  14. Do not stay in front of the chuck area while a spindle is rotating.
  15. We don't take any responsibility for any personal accidents or machine trouble due to unauthorized attachments, modification, any other abuse or misuse by a customer.

  1. Do not allow chips to accumulate during machining the heavy-duty workpiece since they become hot and may take fire.
  2. Check that the belts such as spindle, feed axis and tool post have the correct tension before operating the machine.
  3. Warm up the spindle and all of the axis feed mechanisms before operation. (Operate the machine in the automatic mode for 10 to 20 minutes at 1/3 to 1/2 maximum spindle speed or maximum axis feed rate.)
  4. Make the program for the warming-up operation so as to execute the function of the full range of machine components, If operation is to be performed at maximum spindle speed, pay special attention to the warming-up operation.
  5. Do not operate the switches on the operation panel with wearing gloves, which could lead to incorrect operation or other mistake.
  6. When finishing the work, turn off the switch as following order; power switch on the CNC operation panel, main power breaker and factory power supply.

Article title: 7 Safety Related to Gripping Work piece and Tooling
Article body:
1. Do not rotate the spindle more than maximum allowable speed. This may result in fatal injury that spring out the workpiece.
  2. If the chuck or the jig being used is not SYIL products, check the maximum safe operating speed and maximum allowable pressure of the manufacturer, then operate them within maximum conditions.
  3. Make sure to set the machining condition securely when cutting the heavy or big diameter workpiece. Set the machining condition according to the instruction manual of chuck maker.

    1)    Always use tools suitable for the work and which conform to the machine specifications.
    2)    Replace tools quickly since badly worn tools may result in a sudden accident or machine damage.
    3)    Before starting to rotate the spindle, check that any part which are bolted or clamped to the chuck or the steady rest are properly secured.
    4)    If the center hole on large bar workpiece is too small, the workpiece could come off when a load is applied. Make sure that the hole is big enough and that it has the correct angle.
    5)    Take care not to be caught your fingers in the chuck.
    6)    Always use the crane or lifting gear for heavy chucks, steady rests, and workpieces.
    7)    Be sure not to turn off the power under the condition of clamping the workpiece.
    8)    Always close the front shield before starting to rotate the spindle.
    9)    Specially pay attention to the machining condition and the workpiece balancing when the spindle is rotating at maximum allowable speed.
    10)    If special jaws(larger than standard soft-top jaws) are used, observe the following points:
    •    Lower the spindle speed because centrifugal force reduce the gripping force of chuck.
    •    Jaw nuts must be positioned within outer diameter of the chuck.
    •    Machine the jaws with the workpiece shape.
    11)    Securely tighten the bolts on the chuck body and the jaws to the specified torque according to the instruction manual of chuck maker.
    12)    For safe chucking
    •    The gripping force of chuck must be set to enough the safety factor(2-3 or more). Run the spindle within the allowable speed range.
    •    In constant peripheral speed cutting, calculate the actual machining speed before desig-nating G50 (maximum speed limit function).
    •    Secure the jaw gripping depth as much as possible.
    •    Before machining an unbalanced workpiece, carry out balancing of the workpiece weight by gradual changing the spindle speed.
    •    Never attempt to install jigs using T-nut. Be sure to fix the jigs with bolts.
    •    No chucks prepared by SYIL have T-groove.
    •    When inserting a bar material into the hollow chuck, ensure that the bar does not pro-trude from the rear end of the cylinder.
    •    Never use double chucking method.

    13)    If the spindle must be rotated close to the maximum allowable spindle speed, observe the following points:
    •    Make sure that the workpiece clamped in the chuck is balanced.
    •    Apply the allowable maximum amount of pressure to grip the workpiece because centrif-ugal force reduces the chuck gripping force.
    •    The maximum allowable spindle speed and application pressure are indicated on the name plate on the front shield and on the chuck body. The allowable maximum speed and the applicable pressure ensure a chucking force that is more than one-third over the original chuck gripping force with the standard soft-top jaw set in line with the periphery of the chuck body.
    14)    Since the tool holders can be mounted from the left or the right, check that the tool holder is mounted facing the correct direction.
    15)    Spindle chuck must be adjusted so the radial stroke is no more than 4 mm over workpiece dimension, and it is very important to clean and grease at least every week at the chuck guide for keeping clamping force.
    16)    Tools setting must be done in axes and spindle stopped condition. In the tool setting and maintenance phase, it is necessary to pay attention to tool spike and turret position to avoid interference with machine parts or body parts. Tool and tool holder screw tightening torque must be as specified in normalized ISO table.

    1. Make sure that the tool length is not to interfered with fixtures or other objects.
    2. Perform a test operation after mounting a tool.
    3. After machining soft jaws, check that the workpiece is correctly clamped and the chuck pressure is correct.

Article body:
1. Always Turn off the main power breaker and lock it before carrying out any maintenance work so that someone else can not operate the machine inadvertently during maintenance work.
  2. After the power has been turned off for a short while, check the voltage with a multimeter or similar instrument to make sure that there is no residual voltage. Also discharge the capacitors.
  3. The inclined or vertical feed axes are installed with servo motor or electromagnetic brake device so that their feed axes can not slip down automatically by brake mechanism even being turned off the power.
  4. Do not remove or modify overtravel limit switches, interlock limit switches, proximity switches, or other safety devices.

  1. Maintenance work for electrical parts must be carried out by qualified personnel.
  2. Even if the door of the electrical cabinet is open, the power can not be cut off. When working inside the electrical cabinet or repairing the machine, always turn off the main breaker and lock it with key.
  3. When carrying out maintenance in high places, always use a suitable ladder or a service platform and always wear a helmet.
  4. Always turn off the main power breaker and lock it before electrical work is carried out.
  5. Never approach your hands such as belts or pulleys.
  6. Do not start the machine until all of the removed covers for maintenance have been refitted.
  7. Wipe up any water or oil immediately so as not to slip and keep the maintenance area and the workplace clean and tidy at all times.
  8. Check that working tool is still remained around machine inside or vicinity after maintenance work: this is extremely dangerous.

  1. Maintenance work should be carried out by qualified personnel in accordance with the instructions of the person in charge.
  2. Always use the SYIL replacement parts or approval parts.
  3. Read the manuals thoroughly first then perform the machine operation and the maintenance work.
  4. Do not use compressed air to clean the machine or to remove chips.
  5. Always use gloves when removing chips: never touch chips with bare hands.
  6. When changing a fuse, check that the new fuse has the correct rating. (Using a fuse with too high a rating could result in damage to the equipment.)
  7. Use only the specified grades of hydraulic oil, lubricating oil, and grease or their equivalents. Follow the instructions indicated on the instruction plate concerning the brands of oil to be used, lubrication points, amount to be used, and oil change intervals.
  8. If one of the belts in a set has stretched beyond the prescribed limit, change the entire set.
  9. Stop all machine operation before cleaning the machine or the surrounding area.
  10. Disposal of industrial waste such as oil, coolant, chips and refrigerants is to be performed in strict compliance with environmental protection laws as stipulated by the proper national and local authorities.

1. Immediately remove all water and oil spills from the floor of machine vicinity and keep the floor dry to prevent accidents.
  2. Keep combustible materials away from the work area and any other place where there are hot chips.
  3. Always provide sufficient lighting in the work area.
  4. Always provide sufficient working space for maintenance work when installing the machine.
  5. Never place tools or other potentially dangerous object on top of the headstock, turret and covers.
  6. Protect all cables which are along the floor from being damaged by chips: damaged cables and wires will cause current leakage and short-circuit.
  7. Use strong service platforms only and make sure that nothing can slip off them.
  8. Make sure that the nominal cross-sectional area of the power supply cable between the factory power supply switch and the machine main power breaker is such as to enable a stable supply for operation at the maximum output.

Non water soluble coolant has the potential to catch fire if it vaporizes or forms a mist inside the machine. Pay close attention to the following points to prevent the occurrence of a fire.

  • Never use anything flammable near the machine.
  • If an automatic fire extinguisher is not installed, place a fire extinguisher near the machine.
  • When the automatic fire extinguisher and mist collector are used together, attach a shutter so that mist can be stopped for safety. Attach the shutter between the machine and the mist collector.

  • Check that the discharge amount and direction of coolant are correct.

  • Check that the safety devices (coolant level detector, broken cut-off tool detector, etc.) function normally.
  • Ensure that all the doors are closed during operation.

20.1 Introduction

The SYIL X and T machines are vertical machining centers that can mill, drill, thread and bore under CNC (Computer Numerical Control) control. (They fall under Group 3 of the definitions in ISO 16090-1).

20.2 Areas of use

There are many different areas in which machines in the X and T series can be employed. High precision parts for virtually all sectors of industry can be produced or finished. The main areas of use lie in fine mechanics, optics, medical technology, computer technology, for the manufacture of hydraulic and pneumatic components and parts for the automobile and aircraft industries. The machines can also be used in entertainment electronics manufacture, the ball-bearing Industry, for the manufacture of articles for daily use and luxury articles such as watches or writing utensils, in toolmaking or also in Research and Development and training.

  • pistons
  • Electronics: Plug connectors
  • Automobile/Aircraft Industry: Valves, nozzles for petrol injection and ABS, sensors
  • Supply industries: Finishing of diecast, moulded and sintered parts
  • Roller Bearing Industry: Hard turning, the machining of ball cages
  • Tool making, mould making: Individual parts, electrodes, form cores

24.1.2    Installation site requirements

•    Environments with high levels of dust or humidity
•    Environments located near vibrating machinery
•    Environments built on soft foundations

24.1.5    Electrical service requirements

The customer is responsible for providing incoming electrical power to the SYIL X5 machine.

(a)    Power and voltage requirements
NOTE: The machine’s full load power rating can be found on the serial number identification tag that is affixed to the electrical power cabinet. Consult customer service for an accurate rating of your machine ahead of time to ensure the correct cabling is present.

A certified electrician should ensure the following electrical service requirements:
•    On-site wiring must comply with all applicable electrical codes
•    Dedicated, grounded 3-phase AC power is required to prevent high/low voltages, spikes, surges, and noise
•    The AC power source shall be balanced and must match the voltage specifications on the machine electrical cabinet
•    Wiring to the machine must be capable of supplying continuous specified amperage
•    Failure to provide the required power parameters may affect safety, machine performance, and the warranty

(b)    Transformer requirements
NOTE: In location where the mains power is different from 380-415 V Phase to Phase, a suitable transformer is required.

If a transformer is required and the machine was not equipped with one, the customer is respon-sible for providing a transformer. The transformer must meet SYIL machine operating voltage re-quirements. It is the customer’s responsibility to have a qualified electrician connect the trans-former to the power source.

(c)    Machine grounding
The electrical and electronic control systems of the machining centre are interconnected internal-ly and terminate at a single point ground (SPG) terminal. The SPG provides only one conducting path between the machine and external ground, preventing an unwanted ground loop (ground differential voltage). The SPG is located inside the machine power cabinet.

The SPG must be properly connected to the ground circuit of the AC power source. The grounding conductor must be sized to conform to all applicable electrical codes.

24.1.6    Compressed air requirements

A continuous supply of clean and dry compressed air is required for proper machine operation. Compressed air will
connect to the machine’s filter, regulator, lubricator (FRL) unit.
Sufficient air capacity must be supplied to ensure the correct operation of the SYIL X5. A compressor with a capacity greater than 50 litre and 90 psi is recommended.
•    Air humidity dew point: 2 °C (35 °F)
•    The machine is equipped with a push fit hose connection for 10 mm diameter pipe
•    Avoid using quick-coupler type fittings at the connection to the FRL unit or in the supply line to the machine because these fittings may restrict the air supply

24.2    Transport of the Machine

To prevent potential injuries and equipment damage before, during, and after installation, it is essential to follow the correct procedures for transporting SYIL 5 Series machines to their instal-lation sites.

24.2.1    General precautions

The machine will be delivered inside a crate. The base of the crate is a metal pallet (skid). The main machine body and the coolant tank are fastened for transportation to the pallet.

The main machine body must be lifted from the pallet. Lift the machine with a forklift.
Manoeuvring of the machine on a flat floor can be done with machine skates or a suitably sized and rated pallet truck.

 

 

 

 

WARNING
  • Do not lift any other articles during transportation of the machine
  • Do not go under the machine while it is being lifted
  • Keep a safe distance from the machine and lifting equipment to avoid being struck during transportation
  • Never operate the machine until transportation fixing devices are completely dismounted

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

CAUTION
  • Before transporting the machine, check to ensure its components are correctly and securely installed
  • Lift the machine slowly to ensure it remains completely balanced throughout the moving process
  • Ensure the machine’s body, electrical control panel, and other electrical equipment
  • Remove the coolant compartment from the machine before transportation
  • Ensure that the machine is positioned so that it will not hinder transportation in any way. If there is insufficient space for loading the machine on the transport mechanism, contact the person in charge of the worksite where it will be installed about adjusting the machine or other measures for ensuring transportation
  • Once the machine is placed at the installation site and does not need to be moved further, ensure operating personnel are aware of any safety considerations arising from the installation process before they begin work
  • To ensure safety, always use fixing devices to hold the machine’s spindles in place

24.3    Shipping Arrangements

24.3.1    Offloading the lorry and seating the machine

For lifting the crate off the lorry and the machine off the metal pallet base:

NOTE: An Installation Checklist is available in Chapter 15.
The installation and commissioning procedure is summarised in the following steps. Keep a rec-ord of your installation for warranty purposes if you are self-installing the SYIL.

25.1    Steps Overview

1.    Check and record the state of the crate as delivered
2.    De-crate the machine
3.    Visually check the machine and accessories, photograph as needed
4.    Remove the loose accessories from the pallet
5.    Lift the machine off the pallet

14.    Remove the shipping straps on the axes and the ATC
15.    Clean and install the armour on the X and Y axes
16.    Fill the oilers
17.    Level the machine
18.    Test functionality

25.2    Consumables Required during Installation and Commissioning

•    Slideway oil
•    WD-40 or similar
•    Grease
•    Air line/tool oil
•    Soluble coolant oil
•    Water

25.3    Disassembly of the Crate

Complete this task with the machine on solid ground with sufficient space around it.
NOTE: It is not advisable to remove the plywood panels in locations such as the bed of a lorry. Required tools for this task are:
•    a set of metric Allen Keys to remove the retaining screws
•    a crowbar to lift and pry the panels

25.3.1    How to disassemble the crate

1.    Using the crowbar, lift the lid portion of the crate such as to disengage the nails holding it in place. Lift the perimeter in total before attempting to move the lid
2.    Pull the free lid over side of the crate using the crowbar to dislodge it and to lift the lid as needed
3.    Once on the ground make the nails safe
4.    Select the first panel you will be removing and unscrew the self-drilling screws holding it in position on the base. (The hexagon head is 12 mm) Do not remove the screws holding the other panels yet
5.    Pry the panel free and lay aside. Make any nails present safe
6.    Repeat until the crate is removed in its entirety

 

 

 

NOTICE
  • Moving the machine from a cold environment to a warm indoor location may cause moisture to condense on the machine
  • Moisture may affect the electronics and electrics of the machine or cause damage
  • Keep the machine covered for at least 24 hours for its temperature to equalise

25.4    Inspect the Machine for Damage

SYIL recommends that the machine equipment be inspected for shipping damage before unload-ing and placing machine onto foundation.

•    Remove all wrapping around machine
•    Examine the machine for structural damage
•    Note any shipping damage to the machine on the shipper’s bill of lading. It is the custom-er’s responsibility to file a damage claim
•    Photograph any equipment damage for your records

25.5    Removing Machine from the Steel Pallet

SYIL recommends that the customer review this section to determine if there is proper capacity and ability to lift and place the machine into the location. If not, then a rigging agency should be contacted.

25.5.1    Preparation

Remove any loose items that may have been supplied with the machine. These may include some or all:
•    Coolant tray – now coolant tray is a single piece
•    Coolant washdown and air hose
•    Slide way armour panels
•    Toolkit
•    Manuals and paperwork

 

Figure 42: Coolant tank removed from the steel pallet

25.5.2    Releasing the machine from the pallet

The machine is held on to the base using 3 threaded studs. These pass through the jack-ing/levelling studs that in turn thread into the base of the machine.

Remove the nuts on the threaded studs.

25.6    Safe Lifting of the Machine off the Pallet

25.6.1    Lifting with a crane

•    Pay special attention to machine balance while lifting
•    Beware that the machine might be overturned because of an improper lifting height. Otherwise injury to people or machine damage may occur
•    Always assign a person to guide the way to ensure safety

When transporting the machine by crane, be sure to take the following precautions:
•    Position the base of the crane and the horizontal support plate so that the machine can be loaded with the fulcrum of the overhanging steel cable directly above its centre
•    Ensure the angle of the steel cable’s fulcrum does NOT exceed 90°. If possible, adjust the angle to 60°
•    Ensure that the steel cable is secured on both sides of the pedestal or with a fixing device designed for transporting heavy equipment.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

CAUTION
  • Lifting work should be performed only by qualified personnel
  • Lift the machine slowly while ensuring it is balanced on all sides and that the lifting cables are positioned against its external casing or outermost components
  • If two or more people are lifting the machine, they should communicate to ensure they exert force on it simultaneously and in the same direction
  • Do not use cables of inadequate length or that have sustained rust or other damage to lift the machine
  • Lift the machine slowly. When one of the steel cables has reached maximum tension, temporarily halt lifting and check that the machine is balanced before continuing to lift it to the designated height
  • The machine should be lowered slowly. When lowered almost to the ground,

temporarily halt lowering and check that the machine’s base is level and aligned with

the intended position, then resume lowering to set it down completely
