25.6.2    Lifting with a Forklift

When transporting the machine by forklift, be sure to take the following precautions:
•    Ensure you have read and understood the manual’s safety instructions before installing the machine
•    Ensure the ground is free of lubricant oil, grease, or water to prevent slipping and falling during installation
•    Before beginning installation, check and confirm that the machine has been placed in the correct position

 

 

 

 

CAUTION
  • Only qualified personnel to operate a forklift should attempt to transport the machine
  • In order to avoid damaging the machine or its surroundings, a minimum of two people should be present while operating the forklift
  • Lower the machine slowly to prevent impact with the ground
  • A wooden pallet can be used to support the machine during the lifting process

This machine should be lifted and moved by a forklift. Attention should be paid to the machine balance during lifting and moving. This machine should be lifted under the following conditions:
•    The weight of the machine is approximately 2,000 Kg. It is the responsibility of the op-erator to ensure that the rating of the forklift and the load capacity of the forks at the load distance are suitable for the task.
•    Beware that the lifting truck might overturn because of an improper lifting height. This might cause people injury and damage the machine
•    Always assign a person to guide the way to ensure safety

NOTE: Extended forks are required for this operation to be completed with ease.
NOTE: Having a selection of timber to hand will help with any potential mismatch in level of the front and rear of the machine.

NOTE: Do not lift the machine higher than it needs to be lifted. Adjust the levelling screws to get enough clearance, if necessary.

25.6.3    Moving with a pallet truck

Place 2 strips of wood of 10 mm in thickness between the pallet truck and casting so that the forks can be inserted all the way in. See Figure 100 and Figure 101

25.7    Installing the feet

The studs that secure the machine to the shipping pallet must be retained when the machine is lifted. The studs are then used to hold the cast iron feet to the machine for easy relocation of the machine.

Reuse the shipping nuts on the studs.

NOTE: Do NOT place the thick steel washer on the stud under the foot. This will result in the hex-agon head of the stud protruding from the foot and result in the machine being unstable.=

25.8    Fitting Through Low Doors

The SYIL X5 has two cable chains extending past the head of the machine. It may become neces-sary to unscrew these to allow the machine to pass through doors with an opening height of less than 2.1 m. See Figure 76
To loosen the cable chains, unscrew the 4 cap head screws, 2x each side, holding them to the column.

NOTE: The minimum height of the SYIL X5 is 1.95 m with the feet removed

Figure 33 - Cable chain and screws location

25.9    Test the Coolant Tray for Water Tightness

While the machine is not yet connected to the coolant hoses and the power, test the seal of the plug by doing these steps:
1.    Wipe down the coolant tank to remove excess oils
2.    Fill with water
3.    Let the tray sit for a few hours to identify if there are any small leaks
4.    If the tray is leaking from:
•    the plug, remove the plug and reapply the PTFE tape
•    any other location, contact the customer service

1.    Move the coolant tank into position behind the machine
2.    Align the chip trays with the spouts on the machine casting

X9

25.11.1    Air and consumables required

Compressed air is required for:
•    Clearing swarf and cuttings – Air blast (activate with macro M07)
•    Ensuring tool holder tapers are clean during tool change
•    Air curtain of the spindle. Keeps coolant and debris out of the high speed elements of the cartridge while also offering cooling to the cartridge

The Air Curtain of the spindle has a parameterised time delay. Contact customer service for in-structions.

A 90 psi with capacity more than 50 litre compressor is necessary for normal use if it is rated for extended duty cycles.

25.12    Connecting Power

NOTE: See Chapter 5 before connecting the machine to the power supply. Open the electrical cabinet using the keys provided in the toolbox.
Under the safety isolator switch, a terminal block can be seen as shown in Figure 79.

At this stage, also connect the MPG to the controller panel

25.12.1    Pre-Power ON Checks

Before powering on, check the following:

1.    Power cable is secure
2.    Using a multimeter check that the PE (Earth) cables are all connected to the PE connection of the input terminal
3.    Check that all DIN rail mounted electrical components are held well in place and have not come loose during shipping
4.    Gently pull each of the cables in terminal block in the electrical panel to ensure they are tight
5.    Take the panel off the rear of the controller and inspect the cables in that enclosure

25.12.1    Pre-Power ON Checks

Before powering on, check the following:

1.    Power cable is secure
2.    Using a multimeter check that the PE (Earth) cables are all connected to the PE connection of the input terminal
3.    Check that all DIN rail mounted electrical components are held well in place and have not come loose during shipping
4.    Gently pull each of the cables in terminal block in the electrical panel to ensure they are tight
5.    Take the panel off the rear of the controller and inspect the cables in that enclosure

Figure 54- CNC ON button on the LNC M6800 (left) and the SYNTEC 22MA (Right)

The machine will then boot up.

NOTE: When the machine is fully booted, the controller may give the E-stop warning as well as the air pressure low warning.

NOTE: It is preferable to use the MPG for this operation. Do not attempt to move the X or Y axes yet.

1.    Release the E-stop button and press the relevant Reset button to clear any alarms.
2.    Move the machine axes. Move the Z axis up so that the supporting block or tube can be re-moved.

25.12.2    Checking phase rotation

NOTE: It is very important that the 3 phases of the power cable are installed in the correct se-quence. The effect of incorrect phase sequence is to make 3 phase synchronous motors rotate in the opposite direction they are intended.

To check the correct sequence, the easiest test is to check the rotation of the coolant pump. The pump must rotate in the counter clockwise direction. See Figure 82

Remove the cover of the pump’s fan to be able to see the rotation easier, if needed. Remember to replace the cover to avoid injury or damage to the pump.

Figure 56 - Rotation of the pump

NOTE: Rotation of the pump is the best indicator of the phases of the 3-phase supply being in-stalled correctly. If the pump rotates in the incorrect direction:
1.    Power off the machine and isolate the power
2.    Swap any two of the power cables on the power inlet terminal


25.12.3    Clean the machine

NOTE: The machine will be shipped with some surfaces covered in a protective wax, while others are covered in grease

1.    Clean the machine using WD-40 and rags
2.    Clean the spindle taper
3.    Clean the coolant tray. Remnants of oil from the testing of the machine may be found


25.12.4    Check Lubrication Circuit

The lubrication pump can be activated manually by pressing the FEED button on it.

1.    Hold for 2-5 seconds and observe the pressure dial
2.    Look in the machine to ensure that oil has come through into the ways and ballscrews

25.13    Fitting the Axis Armour

The axis covers are shipped removed. A total of 3 loose elements are to install:
•    The front cover of the X axis
•    2 angle plates. See Figure 113
Assemble the armour as follow:
1.    Using the supplied button head screws and washers, attach the front Y axis cover to the table saddle
2.    Using the two angle brackets (See Figure 113), connect the front and rear Y axis armour. See Figure 114 for correct installation of the angles
3.    Assemble the front X axis cover

 

Figure 58: Angle brackets that connect the front and back Y axis covers

Figure 59: Correct placement of angle brackets

25.14    Check lubrication circuit

The lubrication pump can be activated manually by pressing the FEED button on it.

1.    Hold for 2-5 seconds and observe the pressure dial
2.    Look in the machine to ensure that oil has come through into the ways and ballscrews

Figure 60 - Automatic oil lubrication pump

25.15    Levelling after Seating

Use a precision level to level the machine with a sensitivity of 0.02 mm/m, example shown in Fig-ure 84
Connect power and air to have access to the bed. This allows to move the Z axis up and out of the way.
The machine is levelled through the 3 jacking screws that that locate on the conical machine feet. Applying grease to the threads makes the process easier, as does the use of a ratchet sock-et wrench. For optimum performance of the machine, it is advisable to achieve a level in the X and Y axes of 0.04 mm/m or better.

Figure 61 - Precision level


The procedure is as follows:

1.    Using all three of the jack bolts, lift the machine such that the coolant tray slides under it with ease. Depending
2.    on the floor’s flatness, this may vary. Typically, an extension of 30 mm is required
3.    Place the spirit level along the X axis of the machine and adjust the lowest foot
4.    It is easier to do with two people, one adjusting, the other advising of the level
5.    Once the bubble of the spirit level is centred in the sight glass, the right-to-left level is good
6.    Place the spirit level parallel to the Y axis of the machine and adjust the front foot
7.    When the front to back is level, check that the coolant tray is still able to be installed and removed easily
8.    If the coolant tray fowls the enclosure, increase the height of the whole machine but equal amounts on all three feet, then repeat the levelling process

INTRODUCTION

This manual is only the operating instructions of this machine（Equipped with SIEMENS System） tool, for instruction on the use of other parts , please refer to the following technical documents provided at random.
1.    SIEMENS Controller Operation Manual
2.    SIEMENS Programming Manual
Before using the machine tool , Must fully grasp the contents of this manual and other instruc-tions provided at random , to use the machine tool safely and correctly.
Operators must undergo adequate training in the safe use , adjustment and operation of machine tools before they can use machine tools.

A.    Safety Information

Schematic Diagram of Warning Label Mounting Positions 1

1    Personal Protection Warning Information

Warning: Warning labels are affixed on parts of this machine tool where personal injury may oc-cur to remind operators. Never remove these warning labels.
Operators shall take personal protection measures in accordance with the contents of warnings to avoid personal injury.

Schematic Diagram of Warning Label Mounting Positions 2

Warning Label 1

Warning Label 2

Warning Label 3

2    Safety Device Warning Information

Warning: Safety devices cannot guarantee absolute safety under accidents and hazardous conditions. Please strictly comply with relevant precautions when operating this machine tool.
Installation Positions of Safety Devices

The Installation Positions of Safety Devices Are Shown in the Figure Below.

Location Diagram of Machine Tool Safety Devices

2.1     Function Description of Safety Devices

1） Door Switch (Optional)
If the G2-Liding door is not fully closed, the machine tool cannot run in
automatic mode. If the G2-Liding door is opened during automatic operation, the machine tool will switch to feed hold status.
In manual mode, spindle chuck clamping, spindle rotation and coolant switch can be operated even if the door remains open, facilitating workpiece setup and trial cutting.
2） Main Circuit Breaker
It will automatically cut off the power supply when excessive current of the machine tool is detected.
3） Emergency Stop Button
A red emergency stop button is installed on the machine tool operation panel. In
case of emergencies such as fire, earthquake, thunderstorm or when emergency evacuation is needed, press this button before leaving the machine tool to halt machine operation.
Note: Pressing the emergency stop button while the machine tool is running will not only damage the workpiece and cutting tools, but also the machine tool itself.
To release the emergency stop status, confirm safety conditions first, then turn the emergency stop button clockwise.

3    Precautions Before Operation

1 ） Before starting the machine tool, the operator must master the following contents:
—Location of emergency stop and safety devices
—Contents of all warning labels
—Methods to stop the machine tool in case of emergency
—Functions, operation methods and operation sequence of switches and buttons on the opera-tion panel
—Correct sequence for startup and shutdown
—Handling methods for abnormal conditions
—Method to cut off the machine tool main circuit breaker
Do not operate the machine tool if the operator is in a condition endangering personal safety or safe machine operation, such as after drinking alcohol, suffering excessive fatigue or poor health.
1.    Operators shall wear suitable work clothes (avoid loose and baggy clothing), hats and safety shoes. Remove gloves, rings, ornaments, ties and other items that may be caught by the machine tool and cause hazards in advance.
2.    Do not place objects that may cause accidents around the machine tool to prevent G2-Lipping, falling or tripping.
3.    Flammable objects shall not be placed around the machine tool.
4.    Never operate the machine tool if safety devices fail to function properly.
5.    Verify that the emergency stop button works normally.
6.    Do not modify the machine tool or control circuit without authorization; otherwise, per-sonal injury and machine damage may occur.
7.    Use lubricative, non-corrosive and non-flammable cutting fluid.
8.    Check whether cutting tools, chucks and other components are installed correctly before machine operation.
9.    Confirm sufficient coolant volume and adequate cooling of necessary positions before startup. Regularly clear chips around the machining area and in the chip removal device.
10.    It is forbidden to operate the machine tool with protective covers removed!
11.    Machining of flammable, explosive and dust-generating materials is prohibited! If ma-chining of such materials is required, additional corresponding protective devices shall be equipped separately. You may consult our technical staff for details.

4    Precautions During Operation

1.    Do not open the electrical cabinet protective door when the main circuit breaker is set to "ON".
2.    Do not touch or get close to cutting tools, rotating and moving parts of the machine tool while it is running.
3.    When operating the machine tool, visually check the operation switch before pressing it after fully understanding its function.

5    Precautions for Shutting Down the Machine Tool

Machine shutdown sequence: Reset / stop machine operation → press the emergency stop button on the operation panel → turn off the system power supply, confirm that the display screen goes blank and the indicator lights on the operation panel are off → cut off the main circuit breaker.

6    Emergency Handling Measures

1） Measures to be taken in case of emergencies such as fire, earthquake or thunderstorm
---Sufficient time available
Stop the machine tool operation immediately, turn off the power switch of the NC
system. Confirm that the LCD screen is turned off and the panel lights go out, then cut off the main circuit breaker.
---No extra time available
2） Press the emergency stop button immediately, and then cut off the main circuit breaker.
Sudden power failure
After sudden power failure, turn off the main circuit breaker and press the emergency stop but-ton.
3） Resuming operation after an emergency
After the machine stops due to an emergency or sudden power failure, restart the machine tool in the following sequence:
Check whether the cutting tool is damaged; replace it if damaged → cut off or take out the unfin-ished workpiece processed before power failure → restart the machine tool.

7    Precautions for Machine Transportation and Storage

1 ） This machine tool is packed with rainproof packaging, and key components are coated with anti-rust oil. The packaging box is equipped with certain anti-vibration and anti-impact measures to ensure safe transportation and storage within the temperature range of -25°C to 55°C. How-ever, the packaging box must never be placed upside down or tilted over 15°. Severe impact and vibration are prohibited to avoid damage to internal components.
2 ） If the machine tool will remain out of service for a long time, perform anti-rust protection by applying anti-rust oil and disconnect the incoming power cable. Cover the machine tool with a film G2-Leeve to prevent dust. Block the incoming power cable hole in the electrical niche of the machine base to prevent rodent damage.

E.    Machine Tool Structural Layout

See Figure 5 for the general layout drawing of the machine tool.

1.Base 2.Main Spindle 3.Rear Tool Station 4.Column    5.Tool Holder Bar 6.Side Powered Tool
7.Forward Drilling Tool Holder    8.Sub-spindle    9.Sub-spindle Carriage Assembly

Figure 14 Machine Tool General Layout

Drawing Base: Mainly used to support all components.
Column: The column is equipped with X-axis carriage, Y-axis carriage and tool bar system. Tool change is realized by the movement of the Y-axis carriage. Radial feed motion of tools is realized through the vertical movement of the X-axis.
Main Spindle & Sub-spindle: The spindle motor is a built-in motor (commonly known as built-in motor spindle) with variable frequency drive and stepless speed
regulation. A spindle speed detection encoder is installed inside the spindle head. The Z-axis lead screw drives the spindle to move back and forth to realize the axial feed motion of tools.
Pneumatic System: The pneumatic system is located at the lower rear of the machine tool. It con-trols clamping/releasing of the spindle and extension/retraction of air cylinders.
Lubrication System: The lubrication system is arranged at the lower rear of the machine tool. It supplies lubricant to ball lead screws and linear guideways to ensure long-term stable operation of the machine.
The coolant tank is installed under the base on the right side of the machine tool and can be pulled out to the right for easy cleaning.
The main control electrical components are installed in the recess at the lower left of the base. An electrical cabinet protective door is fitted on the left side of the base, equipped with a power switch and ventilation device for the electric cabinet.

The control panel is mounted on the swing arm at the front of the machine tool. It can be swung out for convenient operation during machine commissioning. The NC panel is provided with two USB2.0 ports for machine data transmission. A handheld manual pulse generator is installed on the side of the control panel.
The machine adopts fully enclosed safety guards. A hinged door with tempered glass viewing window is arranged on the right side for observing machining status. Behind the door is the main cutting area for tool adjustment, tool setting and coolant flow regulation. Two G2-Liding doors are installed on the left side. The spindle area is accessible after opening the doors for adjusting clamping force of the spindle and guide bush.

12    Main Spindle and Sub-spindle

The main spindle and sub-spindle of the machine adopt built-in motor spindle structure. To en-sure thermal stability of the spindles, the spindle housings are cooled by circulating oil cooling system. Recommended spindle cooling oil: Great Wall No.7 Spindle Oil (or Mobil No.4 Spindle Oil).
Air curtain sealing is adopted at the front end of the spindle for protection.
Therefore, hissing airflow sound at the spindle front end is normal. Adjust the air pressure of the air curtain sealing within 0.2～0.4MPa.

Main Spindle and Sub-spindle Schematic Diagram

13    Feed System

The machine tool is equipped with five linear axes: X1, Y1, Z1, X2, Z2.
Rotary axes include S1 (Main Spindle), S2 (Sub-spindle), S3 (Side Powered Tool Axis) and S5 (Rear Powered Tool Axis). S1 (Main Spindle) and S2 (Sub-spindle) are equipped with C-axis function.
The machine adopts a dual-channel control system.Channel 1: X1, Y1, Z1, S1 (Main Spindle), S3 (Side Powered Tool Axis). Channel 2: X2, Z2, S2 (Sub-spindle), S5 (Rear Powered Tool Axis).

G2-205/G2-206 Machine Tool Tool Distribution Schematic Diagram

G2-206/S266 Machine Tool Tool Distribution Schematic Diagram

14    Cooling System

The coolant tank is mounted under the base on the right side of the machine tool and can be pulled out to the right for easy cleaning. Select suitable cutting oil according to the material of workpieces during machining.
•    Water-soluble cutting fluids are not recommended.
•    Cutting oils with high volatility and low flash point are prohibited.

Cooling System Schematic Diagram

15    Pneumatic System

The pneumatic system of the machine tool is installed in the pneumatic cabinet at the right rear of the machine.
Adjust the pressure of the main air service unit to approximately 0.5MPa. Ensure dry and stable main air supply.
Adjust the pressure of the air sealing air service unit within the range of 0.08～ 0.1MPa.

Machine Tool Pneumatic System Schematic Diagram

15.1    Pneumatic Schematic Diagram

16    Lubrication System

All axis lead screws and guideways of the machine are lubricated by a centralized lubrication system. The lubrication pump is mounted on the recess of the base at the rear of the machine tool.Recommended lubricant: ISO VG 64 guideway oil.The oil feeding duration and interval can be set in the system. Recommended setting: lubricate once every 30 minutes for 5 seconds each time.
An oil level detection switch is fitted on the lubrication pump. The machine will trigger an alarm when the oil level is too low.

Article title: B Main Purpose and Application Scope
Article body:
B.    Main Purpose and Application Scope

This machine tool is a CNC lathe with high-speed and high-precision control. It supports 4-axis simultaneous control. As an integrated mechanical, electrical and pneumatic equipment, it can automatically complete machining processes including external turning, face turning, flat milling, side drilling, grooving, thread turning, drilling, tapping, boring and internal thread turning.

The spindle adopts a built-in spindle motor structure (electric spindle), which eliminates vibration and unsmooth operation caused by conventional belt drive. The maximum spindle speed can reach 10000 r/min. The spindle is fitted with NSK high-precision angular contact ball bearings from Japan to guarantee high rotational accuracy, high rigidity and sustained precision retention of the spindle.

Linear motion pairs of this machine tool adopt imported high-speed and high-precision linear guideways and ball screws. Featuring low friction, high responsiveness and excellent precision stability, they achieve rapid traverse speed up to 24 m/min while maintaining micron-level feed accuracy, fully meeting the requirements of high-speed machining.

Standard tool configuration includes 5 side milling power tools, 7 outer turning tools, 4 face drill-ing tools and 8 back drilling tools to satisfy various machining processes.

Equipped with an automatic multi-bar feeder, the machine tool enables continuous bar feeding and remnant removal, realizing fully automatic continuous machining.

This machine tool is widely applied for high-precision, high-speed and high-efficiency mass production of shaft parts in industries such as instruments, light industry, electronics and medical devices.

Article title: D Unpacking, Lifting, Positioning and Installation of Machine Tool
Article body:
D.    Unpacking, Lifting, Positioning and Installation of Machine Tool

8    Machine Unpacking

After opening the outer packing case of the machine, first remove auxiliary devices including random tools and cooling tank mounted on the packing base plate, then remove four fastening nuts at the connecting position between the machine tool and the base plate.

9    Machine Tool Lifting and Positioning

Machine tool lifting and positioning requirements:
Pass two steel bars with a diameter of Φ45mm (material: Grade 20 high-quality low-carbon steel; one bar approx. 2m long, the other approx. 1.5m long; safety factor greater than 4) through holes of two sets of M24 lifting rings. Hook the lifting cables on the steel bars using lifting hooks as shown in Figure 2. (The safety factor of lifting cables shall be greater than 5. Lifting cables must not contact machine tool components. When necessary, firmly separate lifting cables from ma-chine tool parts with wooden blocks, or use a special lifting bracket.)

Machine Tool Lifting Diagram

1.    Lift the lifting cables gradually, check the lifting cables and the center of gravity of the machine tool to ensure safety.
2.    When the machine tool is transported to the installation site and suspended in the air, assemble six leveling screws and lock nuts delivered with the machine. Screw the levelling screws into six foot screw holes on the base via the foot mounting cavity, so that the ball heads protrude from the bottom face of the base.

Machine Tool Foot Screw Installation Diagram

1） Place the six foot pads supplied with the machine at the machine placement positions as shown in the drawing.

Machine Tool Installation Position Diagram

2)    Lower the machine tool gradually and adjust its position, so that the six leveling screws are aligned with the recesses of six pads respectively.
3)    Lower the machine tool steadily onto six foot pads, and adjust the six leveling screws to keep a distance of 35mm between the bottom surface of the machine base at foot screws and the ground.

Warning: The following precautions must be observed during machine tool lifting. Otherwise, the machine tool may fall (be damaged) and cause serious personal injury.

1.    Lifting operators must hold nationally recognized qualification certificates.
2.    Rolling transportation of the machine tool is strictly prohibited.
3.    Anti-G2-Lip pads (rubber or cloth) shall be arranged at the contact positions between lift-ing bars and lifting cables.
4.    Ensure that the lifting cables can bear the weight of the machine tool (approx. 3500kg).
5.    The machine tool shall not tilt during lifting and transportation, and impacts and vibra-tion shall be avoided as far as possible.

10    Forklift Transportation of Machine Tool

Machine Tool Forklift Schematic Diagram

Warning: The following precautions must be observed during machine tool handling. Non-compliance may lead to machine falling (damage) and result in serious personal injury.

1） Forklift operators shall hold nationally recognized qualification certificates.
2） Required forklift rated load: 5t.
3） The machine tool shall not be severely tilted during forklift transportation.
Impacts and vibration shall be avoided as far as possible.

11    Machine Tool Installation

11.1    Foundation Requirements for Machine Tool
1.    The bearing capacity of the foundation for installing the machine tool shall not be less than 3000kg/m², and the foundation thickness shall not be less than 150mm.
2.    The foundation shall extend outward by more than 500mm around the machine tool.
3.    The machine tool shall be installed on a solid and horizontal floor, free from vibration in-terference from other machinery.
4.    If the machine tool is installed on a building floor, the structural strength and vibration frequency of the floor shall be fully evaluated, and approval shall be obtained from the plant design institute or verified by authoritative institutions.
5.    Sufficient space for operation and maintenance shall be reserved at the machine tool placement position as shown in the drawing.

11.2    Operating Environmental Conditions of Machine Tool
1    Ambient Temperature: 0 ℃～ 45 ℃ during operation; -20℃～ 55 ℃ when non-operating; temperature change ≤20℃ per hour.
2    Relative Humidity: Normally 10% ～ 75% (non-condensing); short-term (within one month) 5%～95% (non-condensing).
3    Vibration acceleration: ≤0.5G during operation, ≤1G when non-operating.
4     Install at locations free from splashing chips, water and oil.
5    Keep away from electric welding equipment and other electrical discharge machine tools.
6    Keep away from areas with strong electromagnetic interference.
7    Avoid locations exposed to direct sunlight.

11.3    Machine Tool Coolant Connection
1.    Push the coolant tank under the machine tool from the right side, and align it with the outer sheet metal of the machine tool.
2.    Place the chip collecting box inside the coolant tank and align it with the drain outlet of the machine tool.
3.    Cover the chip collecting box.
4.    Connect the coolant pump to the machine tool with a hose, and fasten the joints with hose clamps.
5.    Connect the power supply of the coolant pump.
6.    Plug in the connector of the coolant tank liquid level detection switch.
7.    Jog the coolant pump to test its rotation direction. If the rotation direction is opposite to the direction marked on the pump body, change the power phase sequence of the cool-ant pump to correct the rotation direction.
8.    Fill with coolant. The volume of the coolant tank is approximately 200L. (Select suitable coolant according to the workpiece material.)
9.    Coolant connection is completed.

Machine Tool Coolant System Schematic Diagram

11.4    Machine Tool Lubricating Oil
The total capacity of the lubrication pump tank is 2L, and the usable capacity is
1.5L. Lubricant grade: ISO VG-68. Fill 1.5L lubricating oil into the lubrication pump for the first time, and replenish oil timely after the machine tool has been running for a period of time.

Note: The lubricating oil must be clean; otherwise, the machine guideways and lead screws will be damaged.

11.5    Pneumatic Supply Requirements for Machine Tool 
1.    Air pipe for machine air supply connection: Φ8mm
2.    Air supply requirements: Air pressure 0.5MPa, air flow 80Nl/min.
3.    Ensure dry and clean air supply as far as possible. Drain residual water in the air com-pressor in a timely manner. Install an additional primary filter for the air compressor when necessary.

11.6    Power Supply Requirements for Machine Tool
1.    Machine power supply: 3-phase 380V±10%, 50Hz±2%
2.    Machine power rating: 12kVA; 15kVA including high-pressure coolant system

Note: The machine tool grounding must be firm and reliable. The neutral wire of power sup-ply cannot be used as protective earth wire!

Machine Tool External Interface Schematic Diagram

11.7    Spindle Cooling Oil
Recommended spindle cooling oil: Great Wall No.7 Spindle Oil or Mobil No.4 Spindle Oil
The machine spindle adopts internal circulation cooling. Appropriate amount of spindle oil has been filled before delivery. Spindle oil leakage may occur during transportation. Ensure sufficient spindle cooling oil for initial startup.
Under normal operation, no consumption of spindle cooling oil occurs. If abnormal oil loss is found, check the cooling oil circuit for leakage and contact the manufacturer for maintenance if necessary.
The machine tool is equipped with a dedicated oil chiller for circulating cooling of the spindle. Please refer to the operation manual of the oil chiller for its operation and maintenance.
Clean the external filter screen of the oil chiller regularly. Clogged filter will block air circulation, reduce cooling efficiency and cause overload of the oil chiller. Long-term overload operation will easily damage the unit.

Oil Chiller Cleaning Schematic Diagram

11.8    Machine Tool Leveling
1.    Move the spindle head to the negative limit position of Z1 axis.
2.    Place the leveling plate horizontally above the two guideways of Z1 axis. 
3.    Put the spirit level on the leveling plate.
4.    Adjust the machine foot screws so that the reading of the spirit level is within 0.04mm/m. Adjustments shall be carried out in both transverse and longitudinal directions.
5.    Tighten the lock nuts of the machine foot screws.

The sub-spindle air blow function removes chips remaining on the sub-spindle chuck.

23.4    Automatic Cut-off (G266 A* X* S* F*)

Machine operation needs to be stopped in case of abnormalities during machining (e.g. tool life expiry, tool breakage, machine fault etc.). After troubleshooting and before restarting machining, remnant cutoff operation is required. The G266 command can be used to perform automatic remnant cutoff.

  • Command Format G266 A* X* S* F*

A: Rapid positioning position - Bar diameter value (mm)

X: Cutting feed position - Cut-off diameter value (mm)

S: Workpiece cutting spindle speed

F: Feed rate per revolution

The G266 command realizes automatic cut-off via pre-embedded macro program as follows:

$1

% @MACRO // G266 A* X* S*

F* WAIT();

IF #1 =#0 THEN

ALARM(100,"G266 A* DATA ERROR"); //A Diameter Data

Error END_IF;

IF #9 =#0 THEN

ALARM(101,"G266 F* DATA ERROR"); //F Feed Command

Error END_IF;

IF #19 =#0 THEN

ALARM(102,"G266 S* DATA ERROR"); //S Spindle Speed Command

Error END_IF;

IF #24 =#0 THEN

ALARM(103,"G266 X* DATA ERROR"); //X Cut-off Data

Error END_IF;

WAIT();

N000;

IF(#1036=1) THEN //TT-code judgment GOTO100;

ELSE;

T0101; //Call tool T0101 END_IF;

N100;

IF (@10721<=#24*1000) THEN //X-axis machine position

IF (@10722=0.0) THEN //Y-axis machine position GOTO999;

END_IF; END_IF;

G00 Y0.0; //Y-axis safe position

Tool T01 is defined as the default cut-off tool. Do not execute this command if tool T01 is not used for cut-off, otherwise collision risk exists.

Move tool T01 to a relatively safe position above the workpiece before executing the command.

23.10    Machine Tool Control (T Code)
Tool change movements of this machine are implemented by servo axes under system control. Users specify the required tool number via T code tool change commands in part programs.

■    Command Format T □□△△

□□：Tool Number
•    Gang Tools （T01～T09）
•    Side Power Tools （T11～T19）
•    Front Face Tools（T21～T29）
•    Back Side Tools（T31～T39）

△△：Tool nose and wear offset number
Tool positioning is performed by 4-digit T code commands. The first two digits correspond to the tool number, and the last two digits represent the offset number.
Executing T0000 means offset cancellation. The X, Y, Z coordinate values corresponding to □□ (tool number) are stored in the system tool length data.
Notes:

1.    Ordinary tool selection runs at rapid traverse speed.
2.    Program T codes in an independent block.
3.    Do not program T code (T □□△△) together with M code or S code within the same program block.
4.    Tool length parameters in the system shall not be modified by unqualified personnel. Back up data before modification to prevent data loss.

25    Machine Stop Procedures

1. Stop during normal automatic machining During automatic program operation, press Program Stop button on the panel to activate M01 (M01 must be programmed). After the program pauses at M01, press RESET to halt machine operation.
2.    Shutdown procedure after work Stop the machine following item 1 → Press the red system shutdown button on operation panel, confirm screen shutdown and panel indicators off → Switch main circuit breaker to OFF position.
3.    Emergency stop procedure Press E-Stop button on main panel or front operation box → Press red system shutdown button → Switch off main circuit breaker.
WARNING: Do not activate emergency stop unless an emergency occurs during machining. Emergency stop forcibly interrupts all machine movements, which may damage workpieces, tools and machine components.

26    Pre-machining Preparation

1.    Switch on air supply and confirm air pressure gauge reads 0.5MPa ±10%.
2.    Check lubrication station; oil level shall exceed minimum scale mark.
3.    If coolant is required, confirm coolant level exceeds minimum scale mark in tank.
4.    Verify factory power supply voltage meets specifications and switch on factory circuit breaker.
5.    Turn machine circuit breaker to ON position.
6.    Press System ON button on operation panel to start CNC system.
7.    Reset (rotate clockwise) E-Stop buttons on main panel and front operation box.
8.    If coolant is needed, test coolant system: press Coolant button to turn ON, press again to turn OFF.

27    Installation and Clamping Force Adjustment of Main Spindle Collet Chuck

27.12    Installation Method of Main Spindle Collet Chuck

Clamping Mechanism Schematic

Adjustment Procedures for Main Spindle & Sub-spindle Clamping Force

1.    Rotate the lock nut at the rear end of the spindle counterclockwise several turns to release the spindle clamping state.
2.    Install the taper G2-Leeve.
3.    Fit the spring.
4.    Mount the spindle collet chuck.
5.    Install and tighten the spindle nut.
6.    Insert the bar stock into the spindle and extend it past the end face of the collet chuck.
7.    Activate spindle chuck clamping.
8.    Rotate the rear spindle lock nut clockwise until the collet chuck just grips the bar stock

.9.    Release the spindle chuck.
10.    Continue turning the rear lock nut clockwise by approximately 1/4 turn.
11.    Clamp the spindle chuck and verify whether the clamping force is appropriate. Fine-adjust the rear lock nut to obtain proper spindle clamping force.
12.    Tighten the anti-loosening set screw on the side of the rear spindle lock nut.

1.    Confirm the position of jaws on the G2-Liding G2-Leeve during clamping. Adjust
the relative position of jaws on the G2-Liding G2-Leeve via the connecting rod of the clamping cylinder.
2.    Tighten the nut on the cylinder connecting rod.

28    Installation and Clamping Force Adjustment of Guide Bush Collet

1.    Use a dedicated hex wrench to ensure the locking screw on the left edge of the collet lock nut is loosened.
2.    Thoroughly clean the guide bush collet mounting bore and the collet chuck, then apply lubri-cant.
3.    Insert the collet chuck into the guide bush. Align the G2-Lots on the collet chuck with
the pins inside the guide bush.
4.    Feed bar stock through the guide bush and extend it past the end face of the collet chuck. Turn the guide bush collet lock nut with a special wrench to gradually tighten the collet.
5.    The bar stock shall not be jammed after tightening. The bar shall G2-Lide smoothly by hand (otherwise the collet will be burnt). Meanwhile, no obvious clearance shall exist between the bar stock and the collet chuck (otherwise poor machining quality will occur).
6.    After the clamping force is properly set, tighten the locking screw with the dedicated hex wrench and recheck the clamping force. Repeat the above steps if adjustment is required.

29    Application of Guide Bushless Mode

This machine supports machining under non-guide bush mode.
Non-guide bush mode can be adopted for workpieces with length-to-diameter ratio less than 3, which effectively reduces remnant length.
Maximum workpiece machining length under non-guide bush mode: 50 mm.
The guide bush mode must be set correctly before operation. Different guide bush modes corre-spond to different soft limits of Z1 axis.
Scroll rightwards on the initial NC system page and find the " Machinery" function option in the last item. Select the "Guide Bush" setting inside this menu, and move the cursor up and down to choose the correct guide bush mode.

 Guide Bush Mode Setting

Rotating Guide Bush Assembly Transmission Schematic

Non-Guide Bush Machining Schematic

Procedures for Switching from Rotating Guide Bush to Non-Guide Bush Machining
1.    Remove the spindle nut at the front end of the main spindle.
2.    Dismount the spline belt protective sheet metal cover.
3.    Take off the front spindle protective cover.
4.    Detach the spindle belt.
5.    Remove the spline nut fixing bracket (two M8 screws connected to the spindle head).
6.    Secure the spline nut fixing bracket onto the column.
7.    Remove the side protective sheet metal of the rotating guide bush.
8.    Disengage the driving belt of the rotating guide bush.
9.    Dismantle the rotating guide bush assembly.
10.    Install the protective G2-Leeve for non-guide bush configuration.
11.    Refit the front spindle protective cover.
12.    Mount the sheet metal cover on the side of the guide bush base.
13.    Reinstall the spindle nut.

34    Part Machining Operation Procedure

The operation procedure for formal part machining on the machine tool is shown in Figure 8.

Figure 33 Flow Chart of Part Machining Operation

In the part machining operation procedure, special attention shall be paid to the following items:
1.    If there is an error in the compiled part machining program, the program must be corrected before further execution.
2.    After programming is completed, the program must be dry-run without tools mounted on the machine tool. Subsequent operations can only be carried out after the dry run is verified er-ror-free.
3.    Mount cutting tools and workpiece blanks. Position each tool to the position before feed travel according to programming data, and check for potential collision interference.
4.    Press the Single Block button on the operation panel, turn down the feed override
knob, and execute automatic operation in single block mode. The next block can only be run after the current block runs successfully. During single block operation, closely monitor faults caused by command errors and tool offset setting errors. If abnormal movements are anticipated, press the emergency stop button immediately to halt operation. Automatic operation can only resume after all faults are eliminated.

36    Common Faults and Solutions

This chapter introduces troubleshooting methods for common faults. The solutions cover typical fault conditions; however, unexpected faults beyond the scope stated herein may occur during actual operation. If the fault cause cannot be identified or the fault cannot be rectified, please contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance.

36.4    Alarm: Spindle / Sub-spindle Collet Fails to Open, or Clamping / Unclamping Timeout

If the spindle collet cannot be opened, problems such as short machined workpieces or failure to eject the machined bar stock may occur.
■    Troubleshooting Procedures:
1.    Check whether the air supply is normal.
2.    Verify normal operation of the clamping solenoid valve.
3.    Verify normal operation of the clamping cylinder.
4.    Check whether the clamping sensor switch works properly; confirm no looseness or damage.
5.    Check whether the connecting rod of the clamping cylinder is loose.
6.    Verify that the forward and backward travel of the jaws is within normal range.
7.    Dismantle the spindle nut, clean the collet, taper G2-Leeve and spindle bore.
8.    Check the taper G2-Leeve for scratches, and check whether the taper G2-Leeve seizes
with the spindle bore.
9.    Replace with a new collet.
If the fault persists after all above inspections confirm no abnormalities, please contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance.

36.5    Low Coolant Flow

The machine tool adopts cutting oil for machining. Insufficient workpiece cooling may lead to fire hazards. Troubleshooting shall be carried out promptly when insufficient cooling oil supply oc-curs.
Troubleshooting Procedures:
· Check if the cooling pipeline is disconnected.
1.    Verify whether the cooling pump operates normally.
2.    Check whether the liquid level in the coolant tank is sufficient.
3.    Clean the chip collecting cavity of the machine base.
4.    Clean the coolant tank and filter screen.

Schematic of Chip Collector and Coolant Tank

36.6    Spindle / Sub-spindle Overheat Alarm

Both the spindle and sub-spindle of this machine tool adopt built-in motor spindle structure. Temperature sensing modules are pre-installed inside the spindle rotor. An alarm will be trig-gered if abnormal operation causes excessive spindle temperature.
Troubleshooting Procedures:
1.    Check whether input terminals I16 (Spindle Overheat Detection) and I23 (Sub-spindle Over-heat Detection) of the machine I/O input module work normally. Faulty I/O input module may cause false alarms. Contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance if the I/O input module is damaged.
2.    Verify whether the spindle temperature is actually excessively high and check for burnt odor. If the spindle temperature is abnormal with burnt odor, the spindle rotor may be damaged. Contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance.
3.    Check for abnormal fluctuation of spindle speed. Abnormal spindle speed fluctuation may indicate damage to the spindle rotor or encoder. Contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance.
4.    Check whether the spindle load fluctuates abnormally during idle running. Abnormal spindle load fluctuation may indicate damage to the spindle rotor. Contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance.
5.    Check whether the three-phase resistance of the spindle is balanced.
Unbalanced three-phase resistance suggests potential damage to the spindle rotor. Contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Machinery for maintenance.
6.    Measure insulation resistance between each spindle three-phase winding and spindle hous-ing. If the resistance of any phase to housing is not infinite, short-circuit occurs between spindle rotor winding and spindle housing. Contact the Customer Service Center of SYIL Ma-chinery for maintenance.
7.    Check the spindle power cable for damage and phase loss.
8.    Check whether the spindle drive unit is damaged.

36.7    Ejector Stroke Abnormality Alarm
The sub-spindle is equipped with an ejector device. For workpieces shorter than 80 mm, the ejec-tor can push workpieces out from the front end of the sub-spindle for unloading.
If the workpiece inside the sub-spindle fails to be ejected effectively, collision may occur between the retained workpiece and other machine components or subsequent workpieces during the machining of the next part.
For the structure and adjustment method of the ejector device, refer to 6.16 Installation and Ad-justment of Ejector Device.
When ejection is executed, the machine system will trigger the corresponding alarm if no signal is received from the ejector cylinder sensor switch.

Troubleshooting Procedures:
1.    Check whether the air supply pressure is normal.
2.    Verify proper operation of the solenoid valve for the ejector cylinder.
3.    Check if any air tubing is damaged.
4.    Check whether the throttle valve of the ejector cylinder is properly adjusted.
5.    Check the movement of the ejector cylinder for smooth operation without jamming.
6.    Check whether the ejector cylinder sensor switch is loose or damaged.
7.    Check the ejector rod for bending; verify its movement is smooth without jamming.
8.    Check for residual workpieces or material scraps inside the sub-spindle and remove them thoroughly.

36.9    Loss of Absolute Position Zero Point
Servo motors of this machine tool are equipped with absolute encoders. After power-off and re-start, zero return operation is not required, and machining can start directly. When the machine is powered off, the servo motor encoder records position data of all linear axes. If the system fails to read position data from servo motor encoders upon power-on, this alarm will be triggered.

Possible Causes
1.    The machine remains shut down for a long time, and the absolute encoder backup battery is fully discharged.
2.    The absolute encoder backup battery was not replaced in a timely manner when its voltage was low.
3.    Motor or drive unit damage.
4.    New motor has been replaced.

Troubleshooting Methods
1.    If the machine will not be used for a long period, power it on at least once a week.
2.    Replace the absolute encoder backup battery promptly when the voltage is low.
3.    Reset the absolute position zero point.
4.    Refer to Section 5.6 Machine Travel Diagram Setting for machine zero positions. Z1-axis ze-ro position: 5 mm away from the positive hard limit stop of Z1 axis.
X1-axis zero position: Position where the center of T25 drilling tool station coincides with the spindle center.
Y1-axis zero position: Position where the right cutting edge of T01 tool coincides with the spindle center.
X2-axis zero position: Position where the sub-spindle center coincides with the spindle center.
Z2-axis zero position: 5 mm away from the negative hard limit stop of Z2 axis.

37    Maintenance Precautions
1.    Professional maintenance personnel shall be familiar with the electrical control principle and operation procedures of this machine tool before maintenance.
2.    Dust inside the electrical installation enclosure shall be cleaned regularly during machine operation. Power supply must be cut off when cleaning the electrical enclosure.
3.    If the machine is shut down for an extended period, power on the machine once a week and run it at low speed for no less than 2 hours each time.
4.    When a fault occurs, first check whether power supply and each control voltage are normal; check the status of circuit breakers and switches; verify good contact and no looseness of all connectors and plugs.
5.    It is strictly prohibited to plug or unplug any connectors while the machine is powered on.
6.    It is strictly prohibited to solder electronic circuits when the electric soldering iron is powered on.
7.    Positions of switches and stoppers on the machine have been adjusted before delivery. Us-ers shall not adjust them arbitrarily to avoid abnormal machine operation.

Notice: If users cannot resolve the occurring faults, please contact our company in a timely manner for proper troubleshooting.
